surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything below ~$120M of Q4 OCF reopens the working-capital/receivable-quality bear case”; the preview also asked what remained of the Mexico receivable after a $74 million collection just after Q3.

surprises.description: Healthcare was far stronger than the preview’s concern about another breakeven quarter: revenue grew about 5%, and adjusted operating margin reached 10%, up from 1% a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The healthcare division's Q4 adjusted operating margin expanded dramatically to 10% from just 1% a year earlier on ~5% revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said healthcare margin was “negligible” in Q3 and that “a second consecutive breakeven quarter” could make the division a strategic-review question. Its revenue consensus was “$43.6M” with “+2.2%” year-over-year growth.

surprises.description: OSI repurchased a large amount of stock in Q4 even though the preview said no repurchase program had been discussed and that a buyback authorization was not in anyone’s model. The preview instead characterized the cash balance as M&A dry powder.
surprises.fact_evidence: OSI repurchased “~565,000 shares at ~$219 for $123.6 million in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management framed the balance sheet as M&A ‘dry powder’ in May with no repurchase program discussed”; “A buyback authorization would be the single cleanest narrative shift available and is not in anyone’s model.”

surprises.description: The year-end backlog was a record, but at approximately $1.9 billion it did not reach the preview’s watch level of $2.0 billion or more. That leaves less backlog growth than the preview wanted as confirmation of the FY27 outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: OSI ended fiscal 2026 with a “record backlog of approximately $1.9 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch for ≥$2.0B” and warned that a flat or down backlog would undercut the FY27 guide.

surprises.description: The CBP awards were larger in total than the single contract highlighted in the preview, but their near-term contribution is limited: only some delivery orders are included in FY27 guidance, and most revenue is expected in FY28 and beyond. This makes the awards less of an immediate FY27 revenue driver than the preview’s request to confirm additive visibility might have suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: CBP awarded two five-year sole-source IDIQ contracts with ceilings of “~$200 million and ~$85 million”; “only a portion of delivery orders in hand” is included in FY27 guidance, with “the majority of revenue expected in fiscal 2028 and beyond.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the $200 million CBP IDIQ and $235 million OTHR award potential FY27 visibility and asked whether the CBP award was “additive, not substitutional,” noting that task orders were discretionary and asking how much was actually in backlog.

surprises.description: The Mexico security revenue headwind is expected to fall sharply in FY27, from nearly $150 million in FY26 to less than $25 million, although it remains concentrated in the first half. The preview focused on Mexico collections and service mix but did not anticipate this degree of easing in the revenue headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Mexico security headwind “reduced fiscal 2026 revenue by nearly $150 million” and is “expected to moderate to less than $25 million in fiscal 2027, concentrated in the first half.”

surprises.description: Opto-electronics’ Q4 adjusted operating margin exceeded the preview estimate, reaching 14.7% versus a consensus estimate of 13.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Opto-electronics reached 14.7%” adjusted operating margin in Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Opto non-GAAP op income” at a “13.8%” margin.

surprises.description: Management gave an unusually strong FY27 free-cash-flow outlook, expecting free cash flow to exceed net income; the preview discussed Q4 cash flow but did not flag this full-year conversion target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects fiscal 2027 free cash flow to exceed 100% of net income.”

in_line: Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $3.78 was close to the $3.76 consensus estimate, and FY26 adjusted EPS of $10.35 was essentially in line with the preview’s $10.36 consensus.
Security adjusted operating margin of 20.8% was close to the preview’s 21.0% consensus estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $70.6 million, versus the preview’s $67.5 million model, and grew 7.3% year over year (about 10% in constant currency). That is a stronger return to growth than the preview’s modeled 2.6% increase and is in the preview’s $70–73 million bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 7.3% year-over-year to $70.6 million (approximately 10% growth on a constant currency basis), marking a return to year-over-year revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Q2 FY2026E (my base) $67.5M” and “YoY +2.6%”; the bull scenario projected “$70–73M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 22.6%, above the preview’s 20.5% base expectation and even above its bull-case threshold of 22%. The preview treated a second consecutive margin around 20% as the key confirmation; the reported level was stronger than that confirmation scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 22.6%, the highest quarterly level in more than five years,” driven by completion of the battery upgrade program and better network utilization.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “IFRS gross margin … Q2 FY2026E … 20.5%”; the bull case required “GM ≥22%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $19.3 million, modestly above the preview’s $18.0 million base model, though short of its $20–22 million bull range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased to $19.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … Q2 FY2026E (my base) $18.0M”; the bull scenario projected “$20–22M.”

surprises.description: Net loss improved by more than $21.6 million year over year. Against the prior-year loss of $26.5 million cited in the preview, that implies a current-quarter loss below $4.9 million, better than the preview’s $6.5 million loss estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss improved by more than $21.6 million year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss … Q2 FY2026E (my base) $(6.5)M”; the preview listed Q2 FY2025 net loss as “$(26.5)M.”

surprises.description: The company reaffirmed the full $285–305 million FY2026 revenue range instead of narrowing toward the low end, as the preview’s base case anticipated. This was better than that modeled outcome, although it did not raise the existing range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $285 million to $305 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “guide narrowed toward $285–295M”; the preview also said “FY2026 guide vs. $285–305M” and that narrowing to the low end would be a de facto cut.

surprises.description: First-half operating cash flow increased more than 70% year over year, a favorable cash-generation update beyond the preview’s specific forecasts. The preview noted positive Q1 operating cash flow and lower planned capex, but did not forecast this first-half increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow in the first half increased more than 70% versus the same period last year, aided by lower capex following the battery upgrade program.”

surprises.description: Cash ended at $68.8 million, below the preview’s roughly $72 million estimate, despite being bolstered by the initial Gold Sino equity investment. The preview had flagged the facility and remaining tranches as a key liquidity issue, but the reported ending cash was lower than its modeled balance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $68.8 million in cash and cash equivalents, bolstered by the initial Gold Sino equity investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash (EOP) … Q2 FY2026E (my base) ~$72M”; the preview also said to watch “EOP cash” and “whether the next tranche was drawn.”

surprises.description: CFO Bruce Aitken is leaving after more than eight years, with Jackie Lee replacing him as Principal Financial Officer. The preview did not flag an executive departure or succession.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Bruce Aitken is departing after more than 8 years and will be replaced by Jackie Lee as Principal Financial Officer.”

in_line: The subscriber base was approximately 677,000, close to the preview’s estimate of approximately 678,000; the reported modest pressure on average revenue per subscriber from entry-level vehicles was consistent with its discussion of EZZY-driven mix and ASP pressure.
Battery-swapping remained on track for non-IFRS profitability in 2026, consistent with the preview’s base-case expectation that the commitment would remain on track.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.36, well above the preview’s $1.16–$1.17 consensus range. That is a much larger beat than the preview’s base case of $1.16–$1.20.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $1.36” and management said it was “ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $1.16 (Zacks) / $1.17 (MarketBeat)” and base scenario “$1.16–1.20.”

surprises.description: BJ’s raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.60–$4.80 rather than reaffirming the $4.40–$4.60 range the preview expected. The increase was largely attributed to fuel outperformance, while comp-sales guidance was left unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.60-$4.80” from the prior range, “largely due to fuel outperformance,” while maintaining comp guidance of 2%–3% excluding gasoline.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of “$4.40–$4.60” and said reaffirmation unchanged was the base case; it identified “raising the floor” as the cleanest bull trigger.

surprises.description: Net sales reached $6.1 billion, above the preview’s $5.89–$5.97 billion consensus range. The gap was accompanied by unusually strong fuel volume and fuel profit dollars, whereas the preview cautioned that fuel could boost revenue while profit dollars disappointed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 15.9% year-over-year to $6.1 billion”; comp gallons grew 10.5%, and strong volume plus favorable gas-price pullback drove fuel profit dollars “ahead of plan” and contributed materially to the earnings beat.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave total-revenue consensus of “$5.89B” / “$5.97B” and said fuel was “high-revenue, low-margin and volatile,” warning that “headline revenue can beat handily while profit dollars disappoint.”

surprises.description: Merchandise comps were 3.1%, above the preview’s roughly 2.5% expectation and within the company’s 2%–3% full-year range. This avoided the second consecutive sub-2% quarter the preview identified as the key risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Merchandise comps grew 3.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed comps ex-gas at “~+2.5%” and warned that a “second consecutive quarter below 2% breaks the guidance bridge.”

surprises.description: The comp was not primarily ticket-led: traffic and ticket contributed roughly evenly. That was a better-quality mix than the preview’s concern, based on Q1, that comps were driven primarily by ticket.
surprises.fact_evidence: Comps were “driven by a roughly even balance of traffic and ticket.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 growth was “driven primarily by ticket” and emphasized that “Traffic-led comps are worth a premium multiple; ticket-led comps … are not.”

surprises.description: Current membership fee income slightly exceeded the preview’s derived estimate, reaching $136 million with growth of 9.9%; the call also reported record membership and record higher-tier penetration. However, management expects growth to slow toward a 6% exit rate, below the preview’s 7%–8% level of concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Membership fee income grew 9.9% to $136 million,” membership reached a record 8.5 million, and higher-tier penetration reached about 43%; management expects MFI growth to moderate “toward a ~6% exit rate by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated MFI at “~$132–135M” and said deceleration “below ~7–8%” would be a concern.

surprises.description: Fuel profit dollars were a positive earnings driver rather than the potential disappointment the preview warned about. Comp gallons rose sharply even as the broader industry’s fuel gallons declined.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comp gallons grew 10.5% while the broader industry saw fuel gallons decline approximately 5%”; strong volume and a favorable gas-price pullback drove fuel profit dollars “ahead of plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that fuel was “volatile” and specifically said to watch for whether “profit dollars disappoint.”

surprises.description: The call said tariff refunds were nearly exhausted, whereas the preview expected additional tariff dollars to flow into Q2. Merchandise gross margin still declined about 20 basis points, with price investments cited as the cause.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Merchandise gross margin rate declined approximately 20 basis points year-over-year due to continued price investments,” partly funded by tariff refunds “that are now nearly exhausted.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had flagged “additional tariff dollars that flow into Q2” and expected tariff refunds to help flatter reported margin in its base case.

surprises.description: Digitally enabled comp sales grew 30%, modestly above the preview’s 28% Q1 reference point. The call also said digital now represents roughly 19% of the business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digitally enabled comp sales grew 30% (64% on a 2-year stack) and now represent roughly 19% of the business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “digitally enabled comps (+28% in Q1)” as a secondary metric to watch.

surprises.description: Texas expansion membership is running materially ahead of plan, a specific execution update not anticipated in the preview. The gas stations at the four clubs are also performing strongly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Texas expansion is tracking more than 30% ahead of membership plan,” with all four gas stations in the chain’s top 30% for gallons and two in the top 10%.

surprises.description: Management disclosed a plan to remove about one-fifth of the SKU range over the next few years, an operational initiative the preview did not flag. The call facts do not quantify its expected financial effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “plans to remove about 20% of SKUs over the next few years.”

in_line: The company maintained its full-year comp club sales growth guidance of 2%–3% excluding gasoline, consistent with the preview’s stated guide range.

Membership fee income remained near 10% growth in the quarter, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would stay above 8%; the more significant difference was management’s stated path toward a roughly 6% exit rate.

surprises.description: Foot Locker comps fell 3.6%, materially below the preview’s roughly negative 1% to flat expectation, and the business posted a $31.9 million operating loss. The preview had flagged weak footwear trends, but the reported decline was worse than the already-lowered bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Foot Locker business posted a Q2 operating loss of $31.9 million with pro forma comps declining 3.6%,” hurt by weak launches, legacy silhouette softness, and a more challenging EMEA environment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Foot Locker comps: ~–1% to flat”; the preview also said “–3% or worse breaks the turnaround narrative.”

surprises.description: Management cut full-year consolidated non-GAAP EPS guidance to $11–$12 from $13.50–$14.50, contrary to the preview’s expectation of a raise to the low end. This was a substantial reversal from the anticipated guidance direction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management cut full-year consolidated non-GAAP EPS guidance sharply to $11–$12 from the prior $13.50–$14.50 range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus expectation is a raise to the low end of sales and EPS”; the preview said a cut would be “the bear case.”

surprises.description: The full-year Foot Locker outlook swung from expected operating profit and comp growth to an operating loss and negative-to-flat comps. This was much worse than the preview’s already cautious Q2 comp expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The full-year Foot Locker outlook was slashed to an operating loss of $40–$80 million from prior guidance of $110–$150 million in profit, with pro forma comps now expected at negative 2% to flat versus prior 1.5%–3% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed standing FY2026 “FL comps 1.5–3.0%” and expected a “raised FL comp floor.”

surprises.description: Consolidated non-GAAP EPS was $3.53, below the $3.77–$3.80 consensus range, a larger decline than the preview’s expected year-over-year decline of about 13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated non-GAAP EPS fell to $3.53 from $4.38 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus adjusted EPS was “$3.77–3.80,” with “–13%” year over year.

surprises.description: DICK’S lowered its full-year operating margin guidance to 10.6%–10.9% from 11%–11.4%, with gross margin now expected to decline slightly and the pressure most pronounced in Q3. That ran against the preview’s focus on decelerating margin dilution as evidence of progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DICK'S maintained its full-year comp sales guidance of 2.5%–4% but lowered operating margin guidance to 10.6%–10.9% from 11%–11.4%, with gross margin now expected to decline slightly and pressure most pronounced in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether “the deceleration in dilution is tracking” and described a base case of “margin dilution ~300 bps.”

surprises.description: Full-year effective tax guidance rose to about 29%, adding an estimated $0.35 EPS headwind. The preview did not flag a tax-rate increase as an issue to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The full-year effective tax rate was raised to approximately 29% (up ~200 bps), unfavorably impacting non-GAAP EPS by roughly $0.35 due to persistent EMEA marketplace conditions.”

surprises.description: Net sales of $5.59 billion came in modestly below the preview’s $5.64–$5.65 billion consensus, despite the large year-over-year increase from Foot Locker consolidation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net sales rose 53.2% to $5.59 billion, including a $1.74 billion contribution from Foot Locker.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus net sales were “$5.64–5.65B.”

surprises.description: DICK’S core comps grew 4.9%, ahead of the preview’s 4.1% consensus, with both average ticket and transactions contributing. That was better than expected for the legacy business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DICK'S core business delivered Q2 comp sales growth of 4.9% (total sales up 5.6%), outpacing the broader industry by nearly 200 basis points, with growth in both average ticket (+3.6%) and transactions (+1.3%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “DICK'S Business comps: +4.1%.”

surprises.description: The DICK’S business’s gross margin expanded 79 basis points year over year, with merchandise margin up about 150 basis points, despite promotional pricing pressure. This was a positive contrast to the preview’s concern about margin dilution, though it is a DICK’S-business result rather than a consolidated gross-margin figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DICK'S business gross margin expanded 79 basis points year-over-year (merch margin up ~150 bps), driven by DICK'S Media Network, GameChanger, and tariff refunds offsetting promotional pricing pressure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “non-GAAP gross margin dilution vs. Q1's –328 bps” as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: The company received about $59 million in tariff refunds, including $21 million that benefited non-GAAP results, and management reinvested the benefits in competitive pricing. The preview mentioned tariffs as a topic but did not anticipate a refund of this size or its earnings and pricing effects.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received approximately $59 million of tariff refunds in Q2, of which $21 million benefited non-GAAP results, and management reinvested these benefits into competitive pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “commentary on tariffs” as a catalyst to watch but gave no expectation of refunds.

surprises.description: Fast Break stores exceeded the roughly 250-store back-to-school goal, and management now expects more than 300–350 by year-end. The preview had identified about 250 by back-to-school as the target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company surpassed its back-to-school goal of ~250 Fast Break stores globally and now expects north of 300–350 by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a target of “~250 by back-to-school.”

in_line: DICK’S maintained its full-year comp sales guidance of 2.5%–4%, consistent with the standing range in the preview.
Total Foot Locker integration charges remained within the preview’s stated $500–$750 million envelope, and management reaffirmed the $100–$125 million medium-term cost-synergy target.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted net income was BRL 283 million, about 6% above the preview’s roughly BRL 267 million extrapolated expectation and 15.5% above the high end of guidance. The beat was partly boosted by the Lei do Bem R&D tax incentive, rather than being entirely attributable to operating performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted net income reached BRL 283 million” and came in “15.5% above the high end of guidance,” “though partly boosted by Brazil's Lei do Bem R&D tax incentive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Applying that pattern to the Q2 guide yields ~R$3.9B revenue and ~R$267M adj. NI”; the preview also says “a ~9% beat is the expectation.”

surprises.description: NPL over 90 days rose to 9.8%, above the preview’s 9.3% bear-trigger level and against its expectation that the ratio be flat-to-down from 8.9%. Management also guided it toward the low teens by year-end; the reported Stage 3 level was 12.9%, though the preview’s Stage 3 figure referred to formation, not the same measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NPL over 90 days rose to 9.8% and Stage 3 reached 12.9%,” with management “guiding NPL over 90 days toward low teens by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said NPL 90+ “Needs to be flat-to-down; a rise toward 9.3%+ is a bear trigger.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted net income is guided to approximately BRL 265 million, below the preview’s BRL 270–280 million base-case range and its stated expectation of at least BRL 270 million. Management attributed the sequential decline to the normalization of the tax rate after Lei do Bem benefits were concentrated in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects adjusted net income declining ~6% sequentially to approximately BRL 265 million due to the effective tax rate normalizing after Lei do Bem benefits were heavily concentrated in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected a “Q3 guide R$270–280M,” and its catalyst checklist said “Implied adj. NI ≥R$270M keeps the compounding story intact.”

surprises.description: Q3 cost of risk is expected to rise to 3.9%–4.1%, extending above the preview’s 3.7%–3.9% Q2 range. The stated driver is seasoning in the private payroll loan portfolio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost of risk rose to 3.9% (within guidance) and is expected to increase further to a 3.9%-4.1% range in Q3, driven by seasoning of the private payroll loan portfolio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Cost of risk 3.7%–3.9%” and said investors were watching for cost of risk “inside 3.7–3.9%.”

surprises.description: The credit portfolio reached BRL 31.9 billion, 3% above the roughly BRL 31.0 billion guidance. This modestly exceeded the preview’s expected level, though it does not establish whether the portfolio’s secured share met the preview’s desired threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total credit portfolio grew 99% year-over-year to BRL 31.9 billion (3% above guidance).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave a Q2 portfolio guide of “~R$31.0B” and said “Guide R$31B.”

surprises.description: A larger share of revenue came from lower- or no-credit-risk streams, while secured-credit revenue grew sharply. The preview emphasized the quality and secured composition of portfolio growth, but did not anticipate this reported improvement in revenue mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “71% of revenues now come from lower or no-credit-risk streams (float, hedge accounting, fees, secured credit), up from 63% a year earlier, with secured credit revenues up 158% year-over-year to BRL 1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Quality of growth” mattered, that “Secured share must hold above 54%,” and that secured mix above 56% was part of its bull case.

surprises.description: Adjusted ROE rose to 20.2%, well above the preview’s 15.5% reference point. That is a stronger return improvement than the preview had specifically laid out as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted ROE improved to 20.2% from 15.5% in the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “CET1 / ROE 16.7% / 15.5%.”

surprises.description: The efficiency ratio improved to 44.8%, a 210-basis-point sequential improvement from the preview’s 46.9% reference. The preview anticipated operating leverage, but this quarter’s reported improvement was an additional favorable result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The adjusted efficiency ratio improved 210 basis points sequentially to 44.8%, with management targeting low 40s/high 30s by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Efficiency ratio 46.9% (from 61.5%)” and described operating leverage as “the margin story.”

surprises.description: AI productivity gains avoided a previously planned 10% increase in the workforce for 2026 and cut token costs by 70%. The preview expected headcount to remain flat, but did not anticipate these additional reported savings and avoided hiring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI productivity gains kept headcount flat since October 2025, eliminating a previously planned 10% workforce increase for 2026 and cutting token costs by 70% since the start of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Headcount flat since Oct 2025; AI leverage.”

surprises.description: The Desenrola program had a material positive effect on reported credit costs and NPLs, but management expected that benefit to be smaller in Q3. The preview did not flag this program’s contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Desenrola renegotiation program provided a BRL 59 million positive impact (~5% of total cost of credit) and reduced NPL over 90 days by 117 basis points, benefits expected to be more limited in Q3.”

surprises.description: The Cover (rebranded CAF) acquisition had closed and was expected to add BRL 80–100 million of net income from August through December, while using about 150 basis points of capital in Q3. The preview did not discuss the acquisition or its contribution and capital requirement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Cover (rebranded CAF) insurance acquisition closed August 3, is expected to contribute BRL 80-100 million in net income from August to December 2026, and will consume approximately 150 basis points of capital in Q3.”

in_line: Q2 cost of risk was 3.9%, at the upper end of the preview’s expected 3.7%–3.9% range.
Headcount remained flat since October 2025, as the preview had anticipated.

surprises.description: Revenue was $10.4 million, well above the preview’s $9.2 million house estimate and even above its $10.2 million bull scenario. The preview had expected a decline against the year-ago quarter, while revenue grew 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 8% year-over-year to $10.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “House estimate (this note, Aug 25, 2026): $9.2M (-5% YoY)”; bull scenario revenue: “$10.2M (+6%).”

surprises.description: Senstar returned to profit, reporting $0.02 per share, rather than the preview’s expected $0.02 loss. The preview’s base case anticipated a small operating loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 8% year-over-year to $10.4 million, returning the company to profitability”; net income was “$351,000 ($0.02 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “House estimate (this note, Aug 25, 2026): … EPS $(0.02)”; base scenario: “small op. loss.”

surprises.description: Cash ended the quarter at $8 million, below the preview’s expected $9.5–10.0 million and below its $9 million level of concern. The cash-funded Blickfeld acquisition was the main reason for the decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and short-term deposits fell to $8 million ($0.34 per share) as of June 30, 2026 from $22.5 million ($0.96 per share) at year-end 2025, mainly due to the 10.4 million euro cash-funded Blickfield acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario expected “cash ~$9.5–10.0M”; the preview said “If Q2 cash prints below ~$9.0M, the market will start pricing a financing risk.”

surprises.description: Gross margin rose to 64.2%, substantially above the preview’s 61% base-case expectation and back near the 64% bull scenario. This was a stronger recovery from Q1’s 60% margin than the central case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 64.2%, down from 66.1% a year earlier but up from 60% in the first quarter, reflecting product mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “GM 61%”; bull scenario: “GM 64%.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses reached $6.4 million, above the preview’s $6.0 million base case and its $6.1 million bear-case estimate. The reported figure included $1.2 million of Blickfield acquisition costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses rose 18% to $6.4 million, including $1.2 million of Blickfield acquisition costs, and reached 60.9% of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “Opex $6.0M”; bear scenario: “$6.1M.”

surprises.description: APAC revenue surged 93% year over year, lifting its share of revenue to 19%. That was a sharp departure from the preview’s downside scenario, which contemplated APAC remaining down around 30%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC was the fastest-growing region with revenue up 93% year-over-year, lifting its share of revenue to 19% from 11% in the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Bear scenario: “APAC still down ~30%.”

surprises.description: LiDAR solutions nearly doubled year over year and rose to 20% of global sales from 11% in Q1. The preview highlighted uncertainty about Blickfield’s contribution and lower-margin LiDAR hardware, but did not anticipate this pace of growth in the overall LiDAR category.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LiDAR solutions grew nearly 100% year-over-year and now represent 20% of global sales, up from 11% in the first quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1 LiDAR as “11% of group revenue” and said the full quarter would make Blickfield’s contribution visible, but gave no expectation for near-100% growth in LiDAR solutions.

in_line: North American revenue declined 12% (including a 14% U.S. decline) amid delayed U.S. corrections projects; the preview expected softness in the Americas during Q2 because delayed projects were not expected to convert until H2.

EMEA revenue remained positive, rising 14% year over year and 26% year to date, consistent with the preview’s expectation of another growth quarter, although the quarterly growth rate was below Q1’s 43%.

The two product innovations remained on the expected H2 2026 schedule: the preview had flagged H2 launches, and the call said they would launch in the second half and be showcased at GSX in September.

surprises.description: CTRN delivered Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $5.5 million, well above the preview’s rough $1–2 million estimate, with a 2.6% margin and 320 basis points of margin expansion. First-half adjusted EBITDA was also $19.4 million versus the preview’s approximate $15.4 million base-case estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA reached $5.5 million,” with “adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 320 basis points to 2.6%”; “First-half 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $19.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My base case has Q2 at roughly +$1–2M vs. -$2.6M LY” and “1H would then be ~$15.4M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin expanded 60 basis points to 40.6%, modestly ahead of the preview’s base case of about 40.3% and above its 40.5% threshold for a clean beat. Higher merchandise margin and lower shrink more than offset rising freight from fuel surcharges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin expanded 60 basis points to 40.6%, driven by higher merchandise margin and lower shrink, partially offset by rising freight from fuel surcharges.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case forecast “~40.3% (+30bps),” while the catalyst checklist said “Anything ≥40.5% is a clean beat”; it also warned fuel could leave gross margin “flat to down.”

surprises.description: The 2026 store plan shifted below the preview’s roughly 25 expected openings: CTRN trimmed openings to about 20 because of timing, while increasing planned remodels to 60–65 from 50. The change is mixed because fewer openings are offset by more remodels.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New store openings for 2026 were trimmed to ~20 (from 25) due to timing, while remodels were increased to 60-65 (from 50).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for confirmation of “~40 new stores in 2027 (vs. ~25 in 2026).”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was $55.9 million, below the $81.1 million cash figure cited in the preview. CTRN remained debt-free and had an undrawn $75 million revolver, but the lower cash balance was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$55.9 million in cash, no debt, and an undrawn $75 million revolver.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$81.1M cash, debt-free.”

surprises.description: CTRN authorized a $100 million shelf registration for potential acquisitions or strategic investments, a more formal financing option than the preview’s description of management merely evaluating synergistic acquisitions. Management emphasized that it has no immediate financing need.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The board authorized a $100 million shelf registration for potential acquisitions or strategic investments,” while management “stressed no immediate financing need.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted management was beginning to evaluate “synergistic acquisition opportunities” and flagged M&A language as a capital-allocation debate.

surprises.description: The call disclosed that customers with household incomes of $75,000–$150,000 account for about a quarter of customers but more than 40% of revenue. The preview did not flag this customer mix or provide an expectation for it, so its significance relative to expectations is unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers with household incomes between $75,000 and $150,000 make up about 25% of the customer base but generate more than 40% of revenue.”

in_line: Q2 sales of $211.6 million and comparable-store sales growth of 10.5% were already pre-announced, so the headline top line matched what the preview said investors already knew.
The full-year guidance raise matched the preview’s base case: comp growth of 9%–11% and adjusted EBITDA of $38–$42 million.
The plan to accelerate to about 40 new stores in 2027 matched the preview’s expectation.

surprises.description: FY2027 revenue guidance of $1.35–1.45 billion is well below the preview’s $1.74 billion consensus, with the midpoint implying a 14% decline rather than the expected 5.6% growth. Management attributed the decline to fewer MA approved policies and lower healthcare services revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $1.35-1.45 billion implies a 14% decline at the midpoint,” with MA approved policies expected to fall 10-15% and healthcare services revenue down 10-15%.

surprises.description: FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $90–115 million falls short of the preview’s $120–140 million buy-side bar, even though the guide includes margin expansion. The guidance midpoint is about $18 million below the bar’s lower end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA is guided to $90-115 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy-side bar: FY27 EBITDA of roughly $120–140M.”

surprises.description: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA exceeded the full-year guidance range, rather than merely landing within it. The $109 million result was $9 million above the range’s upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $109 million beat guidance of $90-100 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance … Adjusted EBITDA $90–100M.”

surprises.description: The company reported a $44 million year-over-year operating-cash-flow improvement, above the preview’s cited $25–35 million FY2026 guide. That is a stronger cash-flow improvement than the preview’s stated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company delivered a $44 million year-over-year improvement in operating cash flow in fiscal 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided to “$25–35M” of FY26 operating cash flow improvement.

surprises.description: SelectQuote identified more than $30 million of annualized expense improvement from AI, technology, process changes, and organizational rightsizing—an additional cost-saving opportunity not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company identified over $30 million of annualized run-rate expense improvement, driven by AI, technology, process improvements, and organizational rightsizing.”

surprises.description: Management now expects senior-segment margins to decline in FY2027, a qualification to the preview’s emphasis on the segment’s durable mid-20% margins. The forecast remains above the 20% target, which limits the size of the downside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The senior segment generated a 26% adjusted EBITDA margin for a fourth consecutive year of mid-20% margins, though fiscal 2027 margins are expected to decline while staying above the 20% target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Senior segment durability” and Q3’s “~26% normalized margins.”

surprises.description: The FY2026 revenue total was slightly below consensus, although it remained within the company’s guided range. The $1.62 billion result was $30 million below the preview’s $1.65 billion estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year fiscal 2026 revenue totaled $1.62 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue | $1.65B.”

surprises.description: Management forecast roughly 60 basis points of FY2027 adjusted EBITDA margin expansion, including approximately doubling healthcare services margins. The preview focused on EBITDA dollars and healthcare services’ run-rate milestone but did not anticipate this margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA is guided to $90-115 million with roughly 60 basis points of margin expansion, supported by healthcare services margins expected to approximately double.”

in_line: Healthcare services exited FY2026 at a nearly $50 million annual EBITDA run rate, matching the preview’s $40–50 million near-term run-rate expectation.
The senior segment’s FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin was 26%, consistent with the preview’s approximately 26% normalized-margin reference.
FY2027 operating cash flow guidance of $60 million-plus is consistent with the preview’s expectation of cash flow comfortably above $50 million.
The Olathe facility’s approximately 30% shipment-efficiency gains were in line with the preview’s focus on whether its claimed 30%+ gains were materializing.

surprises.description: Reported Q4 sales were $465 million, about 2.3% below the preview’s $476 million consensus. However, sales excluding the discontinued temporary supply agreement grew 0.4%, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of roughly flat adjusted sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 consolidated net sales declined 2.2% to $465 million,” while “adjusted net sales (excluding the discontinued temporary supply agreement) grew 40 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $476.0M” consensus; the preview also expected “core net sales” of about $473M, “≈ flat to –0.5% organic.”

surprises.description: Underlying profitability came in stronger than the preview’s earnings math suggested: adjusted operating income grew 17.5%, versus the preview’s implied roughly 12% growth, and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.46 topped the $1.40 consensus figure. The EPS comparison is not perfectly like-for-like because the preview discusses both GAAP and adjusted bases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted operating income grew 17.5%” and “adjusted diluted EPS increased $0.12 to $1.46.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $1.40” consensus; the preview’s EPS math implied “operating income of ~$49–50M vs. ~$44M adjusted in Q4 FY25 — roughly +12%,” and its base case put EPS at “$1.30–1.40.”

surprises.description: Gross-margin expansion exceeded the preview’s expected range: adjusted margin rose 160 basis points, versus the preview’s base-case expectation of 50–80 basis points and its estimate that consensus required about 100 basis points. The 12-quarter streak continued as anticipated, but by more than the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded for the 12th consecutive quarter, up 220 basis points reported and 160 basis points adjusted.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “~100bps of GM expansion” for consensus and listed “GM +50–80bps” in its base case; it also expected a 12th straight quarter of year-over-year expansion.

surprises.description: Management gave a more specific and constructive FY2027 outlook than the preview expected: mid-single-digit revenue and operating-income growth, with about 100 basis points of gross-margin expansion. The preview anticipated qualitative framing and warned that a non-committal outlook would be a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided to “mid-single-digit revenue growth and mid-single-digit operating income growth,” with consolidated gross margin expected to expand “about 100 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Marzetti does not give formal numeric guidance,” and the preview expected a “qualitative FY27 setup”; it described management as potentially “non-committal on FY27.”

surprises.description: The call introduced a significant near-term disruption that the preview did not anticipate: a Cyclospora outbreak is expected to weigh on Q1 sales and earnings, with no gross-margin growth and operating income down about 15%. The sales impact is expected to fade over roughly four months.
surprises.fact_evidence: The outbreak is expected to create an “approximately 250 basis point net sales headwind” in Q1, with “flattish net sales, no gross margin growth, and an approximately 15% decline in operating income”; recovery is modeled on a “roughly 4-month decaying path.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged FY2027 framing and soybean-oil costs as key issues but did not mention an outbreak-related Q1 disruption.

surprises.description: Reported EPS was boosted by a substantial facility-sale gain that the preview did not anticipate, making the headline $1.76 figure less representative of recurring earnings. The adjusted result was $1.46.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported diluted EPS rose 49.2% to $1.76, boosted by an $18.5 million gain from selling the Milpitas, California facility,” while adjusted diluted EPS was $1.46.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited $1.40 diluted-EPS consensus and discussed the potential for purchase-accounting and financing costs, but did not anticipate a facility-sale gain.

surprises.description: Texas Roadhouse dinner rolls showed substantial retail momentum: $58 million in sales, up 76%, with velocity nearly twice the category average and a 61.7% combined category share with Sister Schubert’s. The preview flagged the pipeline-build lap and Retail weakness, but did not anticipate these strong brand-level metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Texas Roadhouse dinner rolls generated $58 million in retail sales over the 52-week period (up 76%), with velocity nearly 2x the category average,” and the brands held “a 61.7% category-leading share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Q4 would lap “prior-year pipeline builds for Chick-fil-A club packs and Texas Roadhouse rolls” and highlighted Retail weakness, but did not set an expectation for these sales, velocity, or share figures.

surprises.description: Bachan’s current scanner-sales growth was more modest than the momentum cited in the preview: sales were up 8.7%, compared with the preview’s cited +25% sales data through March. Low household penetration of 5–6% and management’s expectation that growth strengthens only in the second half also temper the outlook, though distribution expanded and new launches are planned.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bachan's brand showed Circana scanner sales up 8.7% with distribution points up 16.6%, but household penetration/trial remains low at only 5-6%,” with growth expected to strengthen in the back half on new launches and refreshed marketing.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Circana data through March showing Bachan’s “+25% sales and +50% TDPs,” and said “the underlying brand momentum should read well.”

surprises.description: The company reported record operating cash flow and completed materially higher buybacks, neither of which the preview had identified as an expected outcome. The preview did note the 63-year dividend-increase record, so the continued annual dividend raise itself was less surprising.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record full-year operating cash flow of $283.8 million (up 8.5%),” a “5%” dividend increase, and “$36.3 million in buybacks, up $28.3 million year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted the company’s “63 consecutive years of increases” for its dividend and said a pivot to deleveraging would be reassuring, but did not anticipate record cash flow or higher buybacks.

in_line: Sales excluding the discontinued temporary supply agreement grew 0.4%, broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of roughly flat adjusted sales.
Bachan’s contributed $15.4 million in incremental sales, close to the preview’s roughly $15 million estimate.
The 12th consecutive quarter of gross-margin expansion was anticipated, although the adjusted expansion of 160 basis points was stronger than the preview expected.

Management’s discussion of commodity pressure and offsetting actions was broadly consistent with the preview’s focus on soybean-oil pass-through: it forecast roughly 5% commodity inflation, a 50-basis-point margin drag, and planned pricing and cost-savings offsets.
The annual dividend increase was consistent with the preview’s emphasis on the company’s long record of consecutive increases.

surprises.description: nCino reported Q2 revenue of $161 million and subscription revenue of $143.5 million, above the preview’s $159.14 million total-revenue consensus and roughly $141.5 million subscription estimate. Subscription revenue growth was 10%, versus the expected 8%, and growth excluding U.S. mortgage was 12%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues for Q2 FY27 were $161 million, up 8% year-over-year, with subscription revenues of $143.5 million, up 10% year-over-year”; excluding U.S. mortgage, subscription revenues grew 12%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus was “$159.14M”; subscription revenue consensus was “~$141.5M,” with “Implied YoY” growth of “+8.0%.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP operating income was $40.8 million, well above the preview’s $36.5 million guidance midpoint and its roughly $38 million functional buy-side bar. The 25% operating margin also came in above the preview’s roughly 23% guided margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income was $40.8 million (25% of total revenues).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 non-GAAP operating income guidance of “$35.5M – $37.5M (mid $36.5M)” and said the functional buy-side bar was “~$38M”; it estimated “~23.0% at mid” for non-GAAP operating margin.

surprises.description: The U.S. mortgage outlook weakened beyond the preview’s concern about a roughly 2% Q2 decline: nCino lowered its Q3 and Q4 mortgage subscription outlook by a combined approximately $1.9 million because of higher IMB churn. Total company churn, however, was unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “nCino lowered its U.S. mortgage subscription revenue outlook by approximately $700,000 in Q3 and $1.2 million in Q4 due to higher IMB churn from persistently high mortgage rates, though total company churn remains unchanged at about $25 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said U.S. mortgage was “Guided to decline ~2% in Q2” and that “~1% [was] assumed for the full year”; it flagged whether “the ~1% FY assumption holds.”

surprises.description: Four of nCino’s top 20 U.S. enterprise customers renewed early, each contributing to an average ACV increase of more than 10%. This is positive evidence on large-customer retention and expansion amid the preview’s concern about ACV growth and net adds, but it does not establish the company’s overall ACV result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Four of the top 20 U.S. enterprise customers (representing over $900 billion in assets) renewed early with an average ACV increase of more than 10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called ACV and net adds a key metric to watch and said to “push for the H1 net-add run-rate on the call.”

surprises.description: Adoption indicators for nCino’s AI products advanced: more than 230 customers had purchased intelligence units, banking advisor production deployments more than doubled year to date, and one-third of named AI adopters were in production. The preview highlighted AI monetization as an open question, but these facts show progress in customer adoption and deployment rather than a disclosed dollar contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 230 customers have purchased AI intelligence units, with year-to-date production deployments of banking advisor more than doubling, and one-third of named AI-adopting customers now in production.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “>40% of ACV had converted” and “200+ customers had bought initial IU bundles,” and called for “the first hard dollar disclosure” on IU revenue, attach rate, or overage dollars.

surprises.description: nCino signed what it expects to be its largest deal of the year, an international customer deal, early in Q3. The preview focused on ACV and bookings as a key debate but did not anticipate this specific large international deal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed what it expects to be its largest deal of the year, an international customer deal, in early Q3 FY27.”

surprises.description: nCino raised its FY27 non-GAAP operating income guidance to $171–174 million from $166–171 million, lifting the midpoint by $4 million. This is a favorable increase, although the preview had anticipated that a modest full-year operating-income raise was possible.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year FY27 non-GAAP operating income guidance to $171-174 million (from $166-171 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case allowed for “FY revenue/op income raised by roughly the size of the beat and no more.”

surprises.description: FY27 free cash flow guidance rose to $137–142 million from $135–140 million, a $2 million increase at the midpoint. The raise is positive but modest, and the preview had specifically flagged a possible FCF guidance increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company raised] free cash flow guidance to $137-142 million,” representing 69% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 FCF guidance of “$135–140M” and said “a raise here is cheap”; it also flagged “any FCF guidance raise.”

surprises.description: The share repurchase authorization was increased by another $100 million. This matched a possibility the preview had explicitly identified, rather than exceeding an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized an additional $100 million buyback program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a new authorization is a live, cheap catalyst” and identified a “Buyback re-up” as something to watch.

in_line: The new $100 million buyback authorization was a catalyst the preview had already identified as possible.

The preview described qualitative AI usage and customer-bundle growth without dollarized IU revenue as a plausible base case; the reported adoption and deployment metrics did not include a dollar revenue disclosure.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $342 million exceeded the preview’s $328.4 million consensus, while adjusted EPS of $0.71 was well above the $0.62 consensus. Both also beat the prior guidance midpoint, with EPS particularly strong relative to expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached a record $342 million” and “adjusted EPS of $0.71.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 consensus of “$328.4M” in net sales and “$0.62” in adjusted diluted EPS.

surprises.description: Q3 guidance was far above the preview’s inferred $340–350 million buy-side revenue bar: Semtech guided to $410 million in sales and $1.05 adjusted EPS, rather than the preview’s stale screen estimate of about $333 million and $0.61 EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales of $410 million (+/- $5 million)” and “adjusted EPS of $1.05.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “$340–350M buy-side bar” was the key benchmark and described published Q3 consensus of “~$333M revenue / $0.61 EPS” as stale.

surprises.description: Data center revenue reached $100 million, slightly above the preview’s expected $96–97 million and its $96 million catalyst threshold. Management also projected another 45% sequential increase in Q3, a specific acceleration outlook the preview did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center revenue hit a record $100 million, up 39% sequentially” and management “guided for 45% sequential growth” in Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview embedded a Q2 data center target of “≈ $96–97M” and listed “Data center revenue ≥ $96M” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Gross margin came in above the preview’s 54% Q2 guidance benchmark, and the Q3 outlook rose sharply to 58.3%. The preview focused on whether Q2 could reach 54% despite higher Signal Integrity mix; it did not anticipate this much sequential margin expansion in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 54.5% in Q2” and “Q3 consolidated gross margin [is] guided to 58.3% (a 380 basis point sequential increase) driven by favorable product mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted gross margin guidance of “54.0% ± 50bp” and said to watch for “Adj. GM ≥ 54.0%.”

surprises.description: LoRa sales substantially exceeded the preview’s already-strong growth target: sales reached $58 million, up 31% sequentially versus an expected increase of more than 15%. Management also guided to another 15% sequential increase in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LoRa-enabled sales hit an all-time record of $58 million, up 31% sequentially” and Q3 was “guided to grow another 15% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “LoRa +>15% QoQ (≈ $51M+ off $44.5M).”

surprises.description: The cellular module sale was not reported as completed, despite the preview asking investors to confirm the close. However, management clarified that the pending transaction should be EPS-neutral while lifting gross margin by more than 500 basis points structurally, with Q3 ex-module margin of 63.9% versus 58.3% consolidated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pending divestiture of the cellular module business is expected to be EPS-neutral but structurally lift gross margin by over 500 basis points,” with “ex-module Q3 gross margin guided to 63.9% versus 58.3% consolidated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the transaction as in its “final stages” and said to “Confirm close and how Q3 guidance treats the revenue removal.”

surprises.description: Management said 800-gig transceiver industry volume is about 90 million units this year, versus an initial forecast of 50 million. That is a substantial demand outlook revision not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “800-gig transceiver industry volumes have roughly doubled to 90 million units this year (versus an initial forecast of 50 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call itself cited the “initial forecast of 50 million” units.

surprises.description: Semtech reported that FiberEdge share had risen from 18% two years ago to well over 50%, and projected that 1.6T FiberEdge and CopperEdge together would exceed half of Q3 data center revenue. The preview flagged the ramp and design wins but did not set an expectation for this degree of share or mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: Semtech “has grown its FiberEdge share from 18% two years ago to well over 50%”; management expects “1.6T FiberEdge and CopperEdge combined to surpass 50% of total data center revenue in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “1.6T/CopperEdge ramp” and noted Q1 “secured 1.6T design wins,” without specifying market share or expected revenue mix.

surprises.description: Management outlined a much higher future content opportunity from photonics: content per transceiver could rise from high single-digit dollars to $80–90 as the industry moves to 3.2T, with meaningful deployment estimated in roughly two years. The preview did not discuss this opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: The photonics expansion is expected to drive content per transceiver “from high single-digit dollars to high double-digit dollars (80-90 dollars)” as the industry transitions to 3.2T, with meaningful deployment “in roughly two years.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that fiscal 2028 backlog is already more than 70% booked, providing a substantial forward-visibility data point that the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog for fiscal 2028 is already over 70% booked.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue of $19.4 million was above the derived $19.2 million consensus, but below the preview’s $19.8–$20.3 million functional whisper and $19.8 million base case. The result therefore beat the stated consensus but fell short of the preview’s higher working expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 net revenue reached a record $19.4 million, up 12% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave “Q4 consensus” revenue of “~$19.2M,” but said the “functional whisper is ~$19.8–20.3M” and its base case was “$19.8M.”

surprises.description: Q4 diluted EPS of $0.39 exceeded both the preview’s $0.28–$0.31 derived consensus and its $0.37 base case. The beat was especially large versus the derived consensus, though modest versus the preview’s own estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS hit a quarterly record of $0.39.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed diluted EPS consensus of “~$0.28–0.31” and a base-case estimate of “$0.37.”

surprises.description: Q4 operating income was $3.8 million, below the preview’s $4.0 million base estimate; implied operating margin was about 19.6%, below its 20.4% estimate. This was less operating leverage than the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 operating income grew 26% year-over-year to $3.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q4 base case estimated “Operating income $4.0M (20.4%).”

surprises.description: Hospital revenue fell sharply rather than delivering the preview’s expected modest growth. The preview estimated hospital, distributor, and other revenue at $2.1 million versus $2.0 million a year earlier, while the call attributed the decline to longer, less predictable hospital sales cycles.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hospital revenue declined 29% in the quarter due to longer, less predictable sales cycles.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “Hospital / distributor / other” revenue of “$2.1M” versus “$2.0M” a year earlier, or “+6%.”

surprises.description: Full-year diluted EPS of $1.30 was above the preview’s cited FY26 consensus range of $1.20–$1.23 and just above its own approximately $1.29 base estimate. The result beat consensus, but only narrowly exceeded the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net income was $11.3 million with diluted EPS of $1.30.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 EPS at “$1.20 (Zacks) / ~$1.23 (implied from $10.53M NI)” and estimated “EPS ~$1.29” in its base case.

surprises.description: Revenue per weighted-average sales representative reached $1.145 million for FY26, slightly below the preview’s key threshold of sustaining more than $1.15 million and below the $1.168 million annualized Q3 run rate it cited. It nevertheless exceeded the company’s prior $1.0–$1.1 million target, and the FY27 target was raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Home care revenue per weighted average sales rep reached $1,145,000 in fiscal 2026, exceeding the $1.0M–$1.1M target, and the fiscal 2027 target was raised to $1,050,000–$1,150,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said sustaining “>$1.15M” was key and cited “$1.168M annualized in Q3”; it warned that a rollback toward “$1.05–1.10M” would confirm the bear case.

surprises.description: Payer coverage increased to 87% rather than remaining flat at the Q3 level the preview flagged as a possible concern. The 40 new contracts and more than 6 million added covered lives also indicate continued contracting progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payer coverage reached 87% of U.S. covered lives with 40 new payer contracts adding over 6 million covered lives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported coverage at “86% at Q3” and flagged a print “at 86% flat” as a possibility that would mean the contracting lever was largely pulled.

surprises.description: The CEO announced a planned retirement in April 2027, a leadership transition not anticipated in the preview. A Board-led succession process is underway, but the departure introduces an unpreviewed transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Jim Cunniff announced plans to retire in April 2027, with a Board-led succession process underway.”

surprises.description: Electromed ended the year with $20.5 million in cash, above the preview’s estimate of $17–$19 million in net cash, and generated $9.7 million of operating cash flow. The company was debt-free, as the preview had expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the year debt-free with $20.5 million in cash (up $5.2 million), $9.7 million in operating cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview assumed “~$17–19M net cash, no debt.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted a possible buyback resumption after management had slowed repurchases, but the reported total remained $3.9 million for the year—the same amount the preview said had been used through the first nine months. No resumption was reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call reported that Electromed “repurchased $3.9 million of common stock.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “$3.9M used through 9M,” noted that management had slowed repurchases, and flagged “Buyback resumption” as a catalyst to watch.

in_line: Q4 home care revenue grew 15%, matching the preview’s base-case estimate of +15%.
Full-year revenue of $73.8 million was close to both the preview’s $73.6 million consensus and its approximately $74.2 million base case.
Full-year gross margin of 78.5% was within the preview’s expected 78–79% range.

surprises.description: Box’s Q2 billings were $310 million, up 17%, versus the preview’s estimate of roughly $286–290 million and about 9% growth. That is a substantially stronger bookings result than the preview’s expected low-single-digit-dollar beat over the estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 billings grew 17% year-over-year to $310 million, well above the company's low double-digit growth expectations, driven by record Q2 bookings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs ~$288M (+9%) reported”; billings consensus was “~$286–290M (my est.).”

surprises.description: NRR reached 106% against the 105% guidance and the preview’s base case of holding at 105%; management also expects to exit FY27 at 106%. This delivers the preview’s bullish NRR threshold rather than merely maintaining the prior quarter’s level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net retention rate improved to 106%, beating guidance of 105% and up from 103% a year ago, with management now expecting to exit FY27 at 106%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hold 105% = thesis intact; 106%+ = re-rating”; the base case expected NRR to “hold at 105%.”

surprises.description: Operating margin was 29.4%, 90 basis points above guidance of 28.5%, despite an FX headwind. The preview expected roughly 28.5%, so profitability exceeded the stated quarterly target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded 90 basis points to 29.4%, beating guidance of 28.5% despite a 100 basis point FX headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Q2 preview table listed non-GAAP operating margin at “~28.5%.”

surprises.description: The full-year EPS outlook is $1.54, below the prior $1.56 guide and well below the preview’s expected $1.58–$1.60 bull-case range. Management cited a $0.09 FX headwind, leaving only a $0.01 underlying increase versus prior guidance, much less than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 EPS guidance of $1.54 includes a $0.09 FX headwind, representing only a $0.01 underlying increase versus prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said bulls needed “~$1.58–1.60 EPS” and its catalyst checklist called for “EPS ≥ $1.58”; it also listed the prior full-year guide as approximately $1.56.

surprises.description: Box expects gross margin to fall to roughly 80% in Q4 as AI workloads grow and access to public-cloud infrastructure capacity is constrained. The preview expected gross margin around 81.0–81.5% and flagged rising AI inference costs, but did not anticipate this specific decline and capacity constraint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin came in at 81.2% but is guided to decline to roughly 80% in Q4, pressured by growing AI workload adoption and constrained access to public cloud provider infrastructure capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 gross margin guidance of “81.0–81.5%” and noted “rising AI inference COGS.”

surprises.description: The Q2 repurchase was $66 million, versus the preview’s reference point of $114 million in Q1 as the pace supporting the roughly 139 million share-count assumption. The call’s expected diluted share count of about 141 million is also above that preview assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Box repurchased 2.6 million shares for approximately $66 million in Q2” and “diluted share count [is] expected to fall to ~141 million from 149 million a year prior.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buyback pace matters: 4.8M shares / ~$114M in Q1 supports the ~139M share count underpinning EPS”; the preview table listed diluted shares at “~139M.”

surprises.description: The reported suite mix and large-customer growth provide stronger evidence of broader enterprise uptake than the preview’s base case, which described expansion as potentially remaining seat-driven and reserved broadening attach for the bull case. The call reported suites at 69% of revenue and customers paying at least $100,000 annually up 10%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Suites customers now represent 69% of revenue, up from 63% a year ago, while customers paying at least $100,000 annually grew 10% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case required “Enterprise Advanced attach broadening beyond early adopters”; its base case said growth “stays seat-expansion-driven.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $321 million, a modest beat consistent with the preview’s expected small beat and its $321–323 million base-case range.
Q2 EPS of $0.40 matched the preview’s operative consensus estimate of $0.40, despite topping company guidance of $0.39.
The full-year revenue guide rose to approximately $1.29 billion, within the preview’s expected $1.285–1.29 billion range and at its stated bullish threshold.
Q2 gross margin of 81.2% was within the preview’s expected 81.0–81.5% range.
Q2 free cash flow fell to $60 million from the preview’s seasonally elevated Q1 expectation, which anticipated a material sequential step-down.

surprises.description: Intuit guided FY27 revenue growth to 9%-10%, below the preview’s roughly 11%-12% consensus expectation, though within the 9%-10% buy-side whisper the preview cited. The guide therefore met the lower whispered bar but missed the published consensus bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 total revenue guidance of $23.279B-$23.512B implies deceleration to 9%-10% growth, driven by weakness in Desktop, TurboTax, and Credit Karma.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus FY27 revenue is ~$23.7–23.9B (+11–12%)”; the preview also says “TD Cowen expects total revenue guided below 10%” and that “a guide of 9–10% is a beat against the whisper and a miss against the model.”

surprises.description: FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $22.88-$23.12 is below the preview’s roughly $26 expectation. The comparison is complicated by Intuit’s newly including stock-based compensation in non-GAAP results, a change with a stated $5.81-per-share impact; despite that change, the company still guides to 23%-24% EPS growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Beginning fiscal 2027, share-based compensation will no longer be excluded from non-GAAP measures, carrying a $5.81 per share impact, yet non-GAAP diluted EPS is still guided to grow 23%-24% to $22.88-$23.12.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus FY27 ... non-GAAP EPS ~$26”; the preview also asked whether the headcount cut would show up in a defended EPS line “(~$26+).”

surprises.description: TurboTax is guided to grow 2%-3% in FY27, slightly above the preview’s base-case expectation of flat-to-low-single-digit growth. But Intuit says it is accepting lower DIY ARPC to address customer losses, with price now the leading reason customers leave—confirming the pricing and retention problem the preview was watching.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TurboTax revenue growth is guided to just 2%-3% in fiscal 2027 as the company deliberately accepts lower DIY tax ARPC to combat customer losses, with price now cited as the #1 reason customers leave TurboTax.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “TurboTax guided flat-to-LSD with a credible price/volume plan,” and it highlighted the question of whether management would “trade price for volume.”

surprises.description: Intuit disclosed that total online paying customers reached 8.9 million, up only 3% and about two percentage points slower than the prior year. The preview raised filer-share erosion as a debate but did not anticipate or set an expectation for this customer metric.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total online paying customers reached only 8.9 million at year-end, growing just 3% year-over-year (about 2 points slower than the prior year), highlighting the new-customer weakness driving the strategy reset.”

surprises.description: Intuit provided a concrete mid-market and Enterprise Suite update: mid-market revenue grew 39%, customers grew 28%, and IES annualized revenue exceeded $145 million, up fourfold year over year. The preview expected mid-market momentum above 35% and specifically identified a quantified IES or AI monetization metric as a possible upside disclosure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mid-market momentum remained strong with revenue up 39%, customers up 28%, and Intuit Enterprise Suite annualized revenue surpassing $145 million in Q4, a 4x increase year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Mid-market and assisted are running above 35%” and called a disclosed “IES/agents ARR, attach, or pricing uplift” a plausible upside surprise.

surprises.description: Intuit reported sizable growth in consumer-money offerings—online money portfolio revenue up 31%, personal finance offerings up 44%, and consumer money revenue up 26%—plus fast-money refunds up 79%. The preview discussed Consumer Group expectations and Credit Karma, but did not anticipate these specific operating metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Online money portfolio revenue up 31%, personal finance offerings (insurance and home loans) up 44%, consumer money revenue up 26%, and fast money refunds of over $29 billion, up 79%.”

surprises.description: Intuit said its new QuickBooks Free/Lite offerings attracted over 20,000 customers in their first month and positioned them as a way to pursue low-end customer growth in a large, lightly penetrated market. The preview discussed customer acquisition and low-end weakness but did not anticipate this product launch or its early adoption figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New QuickBooks Free/Lite offerings reached over 20,000 customers in their first month,” with the company targeting a “nearly $200 billion TAM” that is “currently only 7% penetrated.”

surprises.description: The preview cited a quarterly dividend of $1.20 after a prior 15% increase; Intuit reported raising the quarterly dividend another 15%, to $1.38. The share repurchases were also substantial, but an aggressive buyback pace was already anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchasing $5.5 billion of stock for the full year ... including $2.1 billion in Q4 ... and raised the quarterly dividend 15% to $1.38 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “a dividend raised 15% to $1.20/quarter” and said an “aggressive Q4 repurchase print” was a credible signal.

in_line: The long-term Global Business Solutions growth framework was cut to 10%-15%, matching the preview’s expectation that the prior 15%-20% framework would be formally lowered.
Mid-market revenue growth of 39% was consistent with the preview’s note that mid-market and assisted growth was running above 35%.
The large share-repurchase program was consistent with the preview’s expectation of an aggressive Q4 buyback pace.

surprises.description: The call announced that Elliott Rogers would join Kohl’s as Chief Operating Officer on September 9, an appointment the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: Elliott Rogers was introduced as Kohl’s new Chief Operating Officer, who will join on September 9.

surprises.description: Kohl’s announced a newly created Chief Customer Officer role for Brian Parisi, a management change not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Brian Parisi was announced to assume the newly created role of Chief Customer Officer.

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS was $4.17, far above the preview’s $1.90 consensus and the company’s $1.80–$2.00 guide. The call said the beat exceeded even the roughly $1.75-per-share tariff-refund benefit, so the refund alone does not account for the earnings upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income per diluted share was $4.17, far above guidance of $1.80 to $2.00, and beat the outlook by more than the roughly $1.75 tariff-refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS $1.90 (Zacks) / $1.95 (broader Street)” and company guide “$1.80–$2.00.”

surprises.description: Q2 net sales reached $1.27 billion, above both the $1.24 billion consensus and the company’s 2%–4% growth guide. Actual growth was 5%, one percentage point above the top of the company’s range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales reached a record $1.27 billion, up 5% year-over-year, exceeding the company's guidance range of 2% to 4% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales $1.24B (+2.8% YoY)” consensus; company guide “+2% to +4% ($1.235–1.259B).”

surprises.description: The company recognized about $100 million of tariff refunds in Q2, despite the preview saying no refund benefit was included in guidance, and now expects another $20 million in Q3. The remaining refund is expected to contribute about $0.35 to Q3 EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A total of ~$120 million in tariff refunds, with $100 million recognized in Q2 and the remaining $20 million expected in Q3 (contributing ~$0.35 to Q3 EPS).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$100M of IEEPA refunds applied for, with zero benefit assumed in guidance”; the preview called recognition of any portion “a clean upside surprise.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating margin was 19.9%, far above the preview’s roughly 10% expectation. The tariff refund added about 790 basis points, but the call also said underlying margin improvement exceeded the refund benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin was 19.9%, up 600 basis points year-over-year, of which approximately 790 basis points came from a ~$100 million tariff refund recognized in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview model: “Operating margin ~10.1%”; company guide: “~10% (incl. ~$20M tariff impact).”

surprises.description: Full-year EPS guidance rose to $13.10–$13.60 from $10.20–$11.00, a much larger increase than the preview’s base case of maintaining the prior range. The new outlook includes a $2.10-per-share tariff-refund benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lifted full-year EPS guidance to $13.10-$13.60, including a $2.10 tariff-refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY2026 guide: “EPS $10.20–$11.00”; the preview said the base case was the range “maintained” and that investors wanted “a raise, not a maintain.”

surprises.description: Full-year operating margin guidance rose to 14.5%–15.0% from 12.0%–12.5%. The call said the improvement was not solely the tariff refund, with underlying margin improvement beyond its roughly 220-basis-point benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year operating margin guidance was raised to 14.5%-15%, with underlying margin improvement beyond the ~220 basis points of tariff-refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY2026 guide: “Operating margin 12.0–12.5%.”

surprises.description: APAC was much stronger than the preview’s estimates: net sales grew 19% and comparable sales grew 13%. The preview’s two APAC net-sales estimates were -19.5% and +0.5%, so actual growth exceeded either forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC was the standout region with 19% net sales growth and 13% comparable sales growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: APAC estimates were “$29.9M | −19.5% (Zacks model +0.5%).”
