surprises.description: Abercrombie brands accelerated beyond the preview’s sales estimate and returned to comparable-sales growth: net sales rose 8% and comps rose 4%. The preview estimated Abercrombie net sales growth of 3.8%, while Q1 comps had been flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Abercrombie brands returned to comparable sales growth of 4% with net sales up 8% (accelerating from 3% in Q1).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Abercrombie brands estimate: “$572.6M | +3.8%”; Q1 was “+3% net sales / flat comp.”

surprises.description: Hollister comps fell 3%, worse than the preview’s -0.7% estimate and despite the preview’s note that a positive comp was a possible whisper. Hollister net sales growth, however, matched the 2% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hollister net sales grew 2% but comparable sales declined 3% against a 19% year-ago gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Hollister comparable sales estimate: “−0.7%”; the catalyst checklist noted “whisper likely for a positive comp.” Hollister brands estimate: “$669.8M | +2.0%.”

surprises.description: Despite the negative Q2 Hollister comp, management said demand exceeded available inventory at multiple points and growth accelerated above Q2 levels in August. The new Target dorm partnership also generated incremental sales and reached new customers—specific demand and distribution developments not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hollister demand exceeded available inventory at multiple points in Q2, with growth accelerating above Q2 levels in August,” and the Target partnership “drove incremental sales and reached new customers.”

surprises.description: The company moved its full-year sales outlook to around 5% growth, the high end of its prior 3%–5% range. This was an upward guidance action rather than the maintained range anticipated in the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year net sales guidance to around 5% growth (to the high end of prior range).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY2026 guide: “Net sales +3% to +5%”; the preview’s base case described the FY range as “maintained.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year buyback plan to at least $500 million, above the preview’s $450 million plan. It had repurchased about $282 million year-to-date, or roughly 7% of shares outstanding.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date the company repurchased ~$282 million of stock (about 7% of shares outstanding), raised full-year buyback plans to at least $500 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 buyback: “$450M.”

in_line: Hollister net sales grew 2%, matching the preview’s estimate of 2.0%, even though comparable sales were weaker than expected.
EMEA net sales grew 2%, within the preview’s estimated range of +1% to +4%. EMEA comparable sales were down 4%, but the preview did not provide a comparable-sales estimate for the region.

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $1.55, $0.08 above the high end of guidance and above the preview’s $1.48–$1.50 consensus range. It was at the top of the preview’s $1.52–$1.55 buy-side whisper range, so the beat was positive but less surprising against that higher bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP EPS came in at $1.55, beating the high end of guidance by $0.08” and was “aided by the buyback program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus” non-GAAP EPS was “$1.48–$1.50”; the preview also identified “$1.52–$1.55 as the buy-side whisper.”

surprises.description: Zoom raised FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $6.08–$6.12, above the preview’s roughly $6.00 consensus and the prior $5.96–$6.00 company range. That is a stronger earnings outlook than the preview’s expected modest raise to about $6.02.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Increased non-GAAP EPS guidance to $6.08-$6.12.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 non-GAAP EPS consensus at “~$6.00,” prior company guidance at “$5.96–$6.00,” and a base-case guide of “EPS ~$6.02.”

surprises.description: Enterprise revenue grew 7.8%, above the preview’s 7%–7.5% base-case expectation and its Q1 run rate of 7.2%. It was close to, but did not reach, the preview’s 8%+ bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enterprise revenue grew 7.8%, its strongest rate in three years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “enterprise 7–7.5%”; it said re-acceleration toward “8%+” would be a bull signal.

surprises.description: The FY27 revenue outlook now assumes online revenue will be flat, rather than the slight full-year growth the preview said management had guided to. Faster-than-expected enterprise growth did not prevent this weaker online assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: FY27 revenue guidance was raised, “with enterprise growing faster than expected but online now assumed to be flat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “guided to slight full-year online growth.”

surprises.description: FY27 free cash flow guidance rose to $1.78–$1.82 billion, above the preview’s roughly $1.72 billion consensus. The increase was partly driven by extending a data center’s useful life, not solely by stronger operating cash generation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was raised to $1.78-$1.82 billion,” with a downward CapEx revision from extending a data center’s useful life by two years “adding about $40 million to free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 free cash flow consensus at “~$1.72B” and prior guidance at “$1.700–$1.740B.”

surprises.description: The reported AI update showed rapid feature and Virtual Agent adoption, but supplied usage and customer-growth figures rather than the revenue contribution or attach-rate evidence the preview said investors wanted. The adoption figures are encouraging, but the central monetization question remained unanswered in the reported facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Licensed monthly active users of Workplace AI features grew 125% year-over-year,” while “Zoom Virtual Agent customer count grew more than 250% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the key question was “revenue contribution or attach rate, not another growth-rate-off-a-small-base statistic,” and that repeating an MAU statistic “without a dollar figure will read as evasion.”

surprises.description: RPO rose 14%, with noncurrent RPO up 25%, and management characterized bookings as the strongest in several years. That is a strong bookings signal beyond the preview’s identification of RPO as a metric to watch, which gave no expected growth level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPO increased 14% year-over-year to approximately $4.5 billion,” driven by “25% growth in noncurrent RPO,” marking “the strongest bookings quarter in several years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “RPO and cRPO from the 10-Q” as secondary metrics to watch, without specifying an expected result.

surprises.description: Zoom Phone’s growth remained in the expected teens range, but all 10 of its top deals were competitive takeouts; Zoom CX also set a record for seven-figure deals. Those deal-quality signals were stronger than the preview’s stated expectations for growth rates and CX displacement wins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Zoom Phone continued growing ARR in the teens with 10 of the top 10 phone deals being competitive takeouts,” while “Zoom CX ARR grew at a high double-digit rate and set a record number of 7-figure deals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Zoom Phone growth (mid-teens in Q1)” and “Customer Experience/ZCX (high double-digit growth, 8 of top 10 CC deals displaced legacy CCaaS).”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell 70 basis points year over year, with management citing higher AI usage costs and acquisition-related dilution. The preview’s operating-margin range did not anticipate this gross-margin pressure; reported operating margin itself was within the preview’s estimated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell to 79.1% from 79.8%,” partly due to “higher AI usage costs and the dilutive margin impact of acquisitions like Common Room.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview framed the business as having a “41% non-GAAP operating margin” and estimated non-GAAP operating margin at “~40–41% (implied)”; it did not give a gross-margin expectation.

in_line: Total revenue of $1.28 billion was close to the preview’s ~$1.27 billion consensus and its ~$1.275 billion base case, despite coming in $7 million above the high end of company guidance.
FY27 revenue guidance of $5.085–$5.095 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s ~$5.09 billion expectation.
Enterprise net dollar expansion remained at 99%, matching the preview’s base case, though it did not reach the bull-case threshold of 100%.
Non-GAAP operating margin was 40%, within the preview’s estimated 40%–41% range.
Zoom Phone growth in the teens and Zoom CX growth at a high double-digit rate matched the preview’s expected growth ranges.

surprises.description: BBWI reported adjusted EPS of $0.62, far above its $0.20–$0.25 quarterly guide, but about $0.31 per share came from roughly $80 million of one-time tariff refunds. Excluding those refunds, EPS was about $0.31—still above the guide range and the preview’s $0.24 consensus figure, though the guide and consensus were not presented on a clearly consistent accounting basis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.62” with “~$0.31” from “~$80 million in one-time tariff refunds,” leaving “underlying EPS of $0.31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS, diluted” consensus was “$0.24”; the preview also listed company guidance of “$0.20–$0.25” and cautioned that the guide was stated as GAAP EPS.

surprises.description: BBWI raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $2.60–$2.80 instead of maintaining the prior $2.40–$2.65 range. The new range is higher at both ends, contrary to the preview’s base case of maintained guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $2.60–$2.80.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 guidance was “maintained at Q1” at “adjusted EPS $2.40–$2.65” and described “maintain” as the base case.

surprises.description: Q2 sales declined 2.3%, better than the company’s guided decline of 3%–5% and slightly better than the preview’s roughly $1.50 billion consensus estimate. Sales also improved sequentially from Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales declined 2.3% to $1.5 billion, beating guidance of down 5% to down 3%, showing sequential improvement from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q2 sales guidance of “−5% to −3%” and consensus of “~$1.50B (−3.4%).”

surprises.description: The full-year sales range improved modestly: BBWI raised its low end from a 4.5% decline to a 4% decline while keeping the high end at a 2.5% decline. This was better than the preview’s maintained-guidance base case, though the upper end did not change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net sales guidance was narrowed by raising the low end to down 4% (high end maintained at down 2.5%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY sales guidance of “−4.5% to −2.5%” and said “Maintained is the base case.”

surprises.description: BBWI’s owned digital business returned to growth for the first time since 2021, with improvement across new, existing, and reactivated customers. The preview flagged digital traction as a watch item but did not anticipate a return to growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The owned digital business returned to growth for the first time since 2021,” improving “4 percentage points sequentially from Q1” with gains in “new, existing, and reactivated customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Amazon marketplace and digital relaunch traction” among the narrative items to watch.

surprises.description: Amazon net sales more than tripled versus Q1, and BBWI said the platform was bringing in younger, more affluent new-to-brand customers at higher AUR. The preview identified Amazon traction as a catalyst but gave no expectation of this scale or customer mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amazon net sales more than tripled versus Q1,” making BBWI “one of the largest candle brands on the platform” and attracting “younger, more affluent new-to-brand customers at higher AUR.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview named “Amazon marketplace and digital relaunch traction” as a narrative item, without a quantified expectation.

surprises.description: BBWI launched in approximately 600 Ulta Beauty stores during Q2, adding a specialty-beauty channel for product trial and discovery that the preview did not identify as an expected development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched in approximately 600 Ulta Beauty stores during the quarter, expanding into specialty beauty for trial and discovery.”

surprises.description: The Fusion body-care launch with Hilary Duff performed above expectations and generated substantial engagement, including about 615 million impressions and more than 50,000 new social followers. The preview focused on the broader body-care trajectory but did not anticipate this launch-level result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Fusion body care franchise launch … exceeded sales expectations,” generated “~615 million impressions,” added “over 50,000 social followers,” and delivered “higher AUR than the core assortment.”

surprises.description: BBWI raised its free-cash-flow outlook to about $650 million from $600 million and cut planned capex to about $240 million from $270 million. Both changes improve on the preview’s expected cash-flow and investment plans.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised free cash flow guidance to ~$650 million (from $600 million), lowered capex to ~$240 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FCF ~$600M” and “capex ~$270M.”

surprises.description: BBWI redeemed $250 million of its 2029 notes, an announced capital-allocation action not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of cash returns and buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “redeemed $250 million of 2029 notes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “buyback pace against ~$600M FCF” and the “capital return framework,” but did not mention a note redemption.

surprises.description: Management said it expects to exceed its Fuel for Growth goal by about $25 million, reaching roughly $200 million. The preview did not forecast this level of savings or goal outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “expects to exceed its Fuel for Growth goal by ~$25 million to ~$200 million.”

surprises.description: Management set a target of returning to revenue growth in 2027, providing a specific recovery timeline that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “targeting revenue growth in 2027.”

in_line: Q3 was expected to carry heavier product and marketing investment; the call said incremental consumer-first investments would be weighted 70% to Q3.
Gross margin of about 40% in Q3 was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of approximately 40% gross margin, while the preview had already highlighted tariff and input-cost pressure.

surprises.description: Dycom reported adjusted EPS of $5.29, well above the $4.62 consensus and the $4.82 high end of its guidance. The gap was substantially larger than the preview’s modest-beat setup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $5.29 grew 45.3% year-over-year and exceeded the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS … $4.62”; company guidance was “$4.40 – $4.82.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $315.5 million, beating both the roughly $289.8 million consensus and the $303 million high end of guidance. The preview’s base case had EBITDA at $298–310 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $315.5 million … rose 53.5% and also beat guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$289.8M”; company guidance was “$284M – $303M,” and the base scenario expected “$298–310M.”

surprises.description: The overall adjusted EBITDA margin reached 15.7%, above the preview’s roughly 14.7% consensus estimate and 14.9% guidance midpoint. That was a clear expansion rather than the flat year-over-year margin anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $315.5 million (15.7% of revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin ~14.7%”; “~14.9% at midpoint”; and “~flat” year-over-year.

surprises.description: Dycom disclosed that about $150 million of wireless revenue was pushed from the second half of FY2027 into FY2028, confirming the deferral risk the preview identified. Management said the program’s overall scope was unchanged and slightly increased, which limits—but does not erase—the near-term concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company deferred approximately $150 million of wireless revenue from the second half of FY2027 into FY2028,” while “overall program scope is unchanged and slightly increased.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any confirmation of deferrals is the bear case; a clean rebuttal is the bull case.”

surprises.description: Building Systems delivered $397.5 million of revenue, above the preview’s roughly $358 million estimate, and its 24.5% adjusted EBITDA margin was far above the preview’s mid-teens FY27 expectation and 17.7% Q1 margin. The company cautioned that favorable cost-estimate changes helped the quarter, with future margins guided to high-teens to low-20s.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Building Systems segment delivered exceptional 24.5% adjusted EBITDA margin (revenue of $397.5 million, ~20% of total), aided by favorable cost-estimate changes, with future margins guided to high-teens to low-20s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Building Systems rev. ~$358M”; Q1 margin was “17.7%,” and FY27 was “guided to mid-teens.”

surprises.description: Communications adjusted EBITDA margin fell 134 basis points year over year to 13.6%, whereas the preview highlighted Q1 margin expansion and treated Communications margin expansion as part of the bullish case. The reported squeeze was attributed to scaling investments, the wireless deferral’s operating-leverage impact, and higher fuel costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Communications adjusted EBITDA margin fell 134 basis points to 13.6%, pressured by scaling investments, wireless deferral operating leverage impacts, and ~35 basis points of higher fuel costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Communications margin of “12.3% in Q1, +31bps Y/Y” and said a bull case included “Communications margin expansion.”

surprises.description: Dycom disclosed more than $1 billion of contracted backlog for long-haul, middle-mile, and inside-data-center fiber, providing a concrete scale indicator for the growth areas the preview identified as important to the out-year story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contracted backlog for long-haul, middle-mile and inside data center fiber surpassed $1 billion,” with hundreds of millions already performed and a “$20 billion addressable market weighted toward the end of the decade.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said long-haul and middle-mile were “meaningfully ramping beyond this year” and called them “bridge assets” for the story after the FTTH cycle matures.

surprises.description: Trailing 12-month free cash flow grew nearly 200% year over year, a strong cash-generation result not quantified in the preview’s expectations. The preview did flag balance-sheet and capital allocation metrics, but did not anticipate this degree of FCF growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month free cash flow grew nearly 200% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: The Board approved a new $150 million share repurchase authorization through February 2028, a more concrete and sizable buyback commitment than the preview’s question about whether repurchases would accelerate beyond Q1’s $36 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board approved a new $150 million share repurchase authorization through February 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether buybacks would “accelerate beyond Q1's modest $36M / 100k shares.”

in_line: Revenue of $2.01 billion was modestly above the $1.97 billion consensus, but was at the top of company guidance and within the preview’s expected range.
FY2027 revenue guidance was raised to $7.48–$7.66 billion, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of a modest raise; the new high end just exceeded $7.65 billion.
Total backlog reached $12.2 billion, within the preview’s expected base-case range of roughly $11.5–$12.5 billion and above its stated $11.5 billion pass threshold.
Pro forma net leverage remained around 2.3x, in line with the preview’s Q1 figure.

surprises.description: Diluted EPS of $1.67 topped the preview’s $1.60–$1.65 buy-side whisper, though the gap was modest. Net income was a record $235.4 million, up 33% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net income rose 33% to a record $235.4 million ($1.67 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put the “functional buy-side whisper” at “$1.60–1.65” EPS and its base estimate at “~$1.61.”

surprises.description: ETG’s 18% organic growth and $483.5 million of sales exceeded the preview’s roughly 15% organic-growth assumption and $465–475 million segment estimate. Its margin was strong at about 26%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that a result of at least 25% would confirm the improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Electronic Technologies Group posted 18% organic growth, with net sales up 36% to $483.5 million”; operating margin rose to 26% from 22.8%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated ETG at “~$465–475M” and “~15% organic”; it said “Anything ≥25% confirms the mix shift is structural.”

surprises.description: FSG organic growth was 12%, below the preview’s mid-teens expectation and its estimate of $955–965 million in segment sales. Component repair grew only 5%, missing the preview’s expectation that it could break above roughly 10%, with part shortages still constraining it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Flight Support Group achieved 12% organic growth with net sales up 18% to $947.8 million”; component repair organic growth was “only 5%,” and management flagged persistent part shortages constraining its revenue growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s FSG build was “~$955–965M” with “mid-teens organic”; it said to watch whether “component repair breaks above ~10%” and noted supply-chain constraints as the limit.

surprises.description: Operating cash flow rose 49% to $345.3 million and was nearly 150% of net income; management also put full-year free cash flow near $1 billion. The preview highlighted cash conversion as a key risk to monitor but did not anticipate this specific full-year cash-flow outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow surged 49% to $345.3 million, representing nearly 150% of net income,” with full-year free cash flow guided “near the $1 billion mark.”

surprises.description: Leverage improved rather than continuing toward the preview’s downside scenario: net debt-to-EBITDA was 1.57x, below both the 1.74x reported for April in the preview and the 1.8x level it flagged as a concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 1.57x from 1.6x at fiscal year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited leverage of “1.74x (Apr ’26)” and warned that a “third consecutive leverage tick with soft conversion” or leverage “>1.8x” would revive balance-sheet concerns.

surprises.description: Management disclosed a $70–75 million Q4 payment to the estate of the past Chairman, an unanticipated cash outflow that will weigh on Q4 operating cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 operating cash flow will absorb a $70-$75 million payment to the estate of the past Chairman.”

surprises.description: HEICO disclosed a new, enlarged financing facility and roughly $3 billion of acquisition capacity, giving it substantial additional deal capacity beyond the preview’s discussion of its acquisition pipeline and leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: HEICO “extended its revolving credit facility to June 2031, raised committed capital to $2.2 billion with an accordion feature to $3 billion, giving roughly $3 billion of acquisition capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the “M&A cadence and pipeline” and leverage, but did not anticipate a facility extension or this level of acquisition capacity.

surprises.description: Defense organic growth was in the upper 20s despite the preview’s warning that $15–20 million of defense sales had been pulled forward into Q2, which could weigh on Q3. That points to stronger defense growth than the pull-forward concern implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: FSG defense organic growth was “in the upper 20s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had flagged a “$15–20M pull-forward of defense sales into Q2” that “was originally H2 revenue” and would affect Q3 growth.

in_line: Consolidated net sales of $1,413.1 million were close to the preview’s roughly $1.42 billion base estimate, while substantially exceeding the stale published consensus of $1.34–1.35 billion.
Consolidated operating margin was about 25.1% (calculated from reported operating income and sales), in line with the preview’s roughly 25% base estimate.
ETG’s approximately 26% operating margin cleared the preview’s 25% confirmation threshold, and the full-year ETG operating-margin guide remained at 22%–24%, rather than being raised.
FSG operating margin improved to 25.9%, within the preview’s 24%–26% guide range.
Parts/distribution organic growth rebounded to 15% from 2% in Q2, in line with the preview’s expectation that parts would reaccelerate.

surprises.description: Smucker reported an unexpected $0.84 per-share tariff-refund benefit in Q1, while expecting only about a $0.60 net benefit for the full year after reinvesting the difference in administrative costs, marketing, and McCalla preproduction. The Q1 benefit is large relative to the preview’s $2.21–$2.22 adjusted-EPS consensus, though the facts do not state the reported EPS result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received an $0.84 EPS tariff refund benefit in fiscal Q1 and expects roughly a $0.60 net benefit for the full year, reinvesting the difference into administrative costs, marketing, and McCalla facility preproduction expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: Consensus $2.21–$2.22.”

surprises.description: Smucker reached its 3x leverage target in Q1 ahead of schedule and expects to pay down about $500 million of debt this year, while also gaining flexibility to contemplate share repurchases. The preview discussed deleveraging and the FCF target, but did not anticipate reaching the leverage goal this early or the potential return of repurchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Smucker achieved its 3x leverage ratio target in Q1, ahead of schedule, and is on track to pay down about $500 million of debt this year while gaining flexibility to begin contemplating share repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow and deleveraging” were flagged for monitoring against the “~$1.0B FY27 target.”

surprises.description: Uncrustables’ full-year growth outlook was raised from mid-single digits to high-single digits. The preview highlighted the brand’s momentum and its having surpassed $1 billion in sales, but did not anticipate this stronger growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised the Uncrustables growth outlook from mid-single digits to high-single digits for the full year, following the brand surpassing $1 billion in sales last fiscal year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Uncrustables (now a >$1B brand) carrying mix” and “Uncrustables momentum post-$1B.”

surprises.description: Underlying COGS inflation, excluding green coffee tariffs, is running at mid-single digits—about 100 basis points above initial expectations—mainly because of freight and some commodity and ingredient costs. That is a cost headwind beyond the preview’s favorable coffee-deflation assumptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Underlying COGS inflation (excluding green coffee tariffs) is now running at mid-single digits, about 100 basis points higher than initial expectations, driven mainly by freight and some commodity/ingredient costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance assumed mid-single-digit green coffee deflation.”

surprises.description: The expected coffee list-price decline was reversed: rather than cutting list prices as the preview anticipated for Q2, Smucker plans to pass deflation to consumers through trade promotion, saying key commodity thresholds and sustained deflation have not materialized. The change avoids a list-price cut but also signals that the anticipated cost relief has not yet been established.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reversed a previously contemplated coffee list price decline, instead passing deflation to consumers via trade promotion since key commodity thresholds and sustained deflation have not materialized.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sequential price decreases starting in Q2 as green coffee costs pass through.”

surprises.description: Sweet Baked Snacks is expected to decline low single digits for the full year, with sharper declines in the first two quarters before a more flattish second half. That is weaker near-term guidance than the preview’s focus on a narrowing sales decline and its scenario in which a return to growth was the largest upside possibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sweet Baked Snacks (Hostess) is expected to be down low single digits for the full year, with the first two quarters down more sharply due to lapping SKU rationalization and persistent convenience-channel traffic pressure, and a more flattish back half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether the sales decline narrows”; “a return to growth is the biggest upside surprise available.”

surprises.description: Frozen Handheld and Spreads margins may step back slightly over the next few quarters as McCalla preproduction expenses increase. The preview’s segment model projected profit growth for the quarter and did not flag this upcoming margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Frozen handheld and spreads margins may take a slight step back over the next few quarters as McCalla, Alabama preproduction expenses increase to support Uncrustables capacity expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Frozen Handheld & Spreads segment profit of “~$125M” versus “$114.3M” a year earlier, or “+9%.”

surprises.description: Café Bustelo grew 23% and became the category’s #6 brand, with management pointing to further distribution opportunities in the Central and Western U.S. The preview noted that Bustelo was growing, but did not anticipate this reported growth rate or ranking.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Café Bustelo grew 23% in the quarter and is now the #6 brand in the category, with management citing continued distribution runway in Central and Western U.S. regions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Only Café Bustelo has been reliably growing volume.”

surprises.description: Pet-food results showed some brand-level improvement: Pup-Peroni sales rose 5% and Milk-Bone returned to volume growth, although Turkey treats declined. This offers a mixed signal on the pet-volume inflection the preview identified as a key issue, rather than a uniformly strong portfolio recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pup-Peroni net sales rose 5% and Milk-Bone returned to volume growth, though Turkey treats declined within the dog snacks portfolio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Volume/mix inflection in Pet Foods” was a catalyst to watch.

in_line: Coffee volumes remain guided to decline low single digits for the full year despite strength in Q1, consistent with the preview’s expectation of unfavorable volume/mix and its base case of volume/mix down low single digits.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $169.8 million, above the preview’s $164.2–$165.5 million range, with growth of 4.9% rather than the expected 1.5%–2.3%. U.S. and international sales both grew 4.9%, though the call facts do not provide constant-currency growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2027 sales rose 4.9% year-over-year to $169.8 million, with U.S. and international net sales each increasing 4.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales: Consensus $164.2M–$165.5M (+1.5% to +2.3%).”

surprises.description: Gross margin substantially exceeded the preview’s implied 55.5%–56.0% range: it reached 59.4%, and was still 57.5% excluding duty refunds. That underlying margin improvement was stronger than the preview’s expectation of a partial give-back of the tariff-related benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded to 59.4% from 54.1%, but excluding the IEEPA refunds it was 57.5%, a still-strong 340 basis point improvement driven by pricing and favorable channel/product mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: ~55.5–56.0% (implied)” and the base scenario anticipated “GM 55.5–56.0% (partial give-back of tariff benefit).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.54 was well above the published $0.35–$0.36 consensus and also above the preview’s $0.40–$0.45 whisper range. However, $0.11 per share came from IEEPA duty refunds; excluding that benefit, EPS was about $0.43, within the whisper range. The quarter also included $3.2 million of refunds, with another $6.8 million expected but not recognized until cash is received.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS more than doubled to $0.54 from $0.23 a year earlier, including a $0.11 per share benefit from IEEPA duty refunds”; “aided by $3.2 million of IEEPA duty refunds received in the quarter”; and “expects to recover a remaining $6.8 million in previously paid IEEPA duties but will not recognize the gain until cash is received.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS: $0.35–$0.36”; the preview also said to assume “a whisper in the $0.40–$0.45 range.”

surprises.description: Although management did not reinstate an annual FY27 outlook, it gave a new qualitative forecast of mid-single-digit top-line growth for the remainder of the year. That is more forward sales guidance than the preview’s base case of continued withholding, and it is constructive against the preview’s expectation that sales growth would moderate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company discontinued providing an annual outlook, instead guiding to mid-single-digit top-line growth for the remainder of the fiscal year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No FY27 company guidance exists”; the base scenario anticipated “continued no-guidance posture.” The preview also said management had pre-warned that “net sales growth will moderate in the second quarter.”

surprises.description: Inventory fell rather than remaining elevated as feared in the preview’s downside case, easing the concern raised by the Q1 inventory build. The call facts do not specify the comparison period, so the size of the improvement relative to Q1 cannot be determined.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory fell 7.1% (down $15 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified the Q1 inventory build to $182.0 million as a key swing factor and described the bear case as “inventory stays elevated.”

surprises.description: Movado disclosed a planned Kate Spade watch launch next fiscal year as part of its expanded Tapestry partnership, a product and partnership development not anticipated in the preview. No expected sales or earnings contribution was provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Movado will launch Kate Spade watches next fiscal year, expanding its long-term partnership with Tapestry.”

in_line: The expected temporary gross-margin tailwind from lower-duty legacy inventory is not expected to persist: management guided H2 gross margin to 55%–56%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a tariff-related give-back.
No annual FY27 outlook was reinstated, as the preview’s base case anticipated continued withholding of annual guidance.
The company remained debt-free, consistent with the preview’s note that it had zero debt at Q1.

surprises.description: Q4 sales grew about 8%, above the preview’s 6.4%–7.2% consensus growth range. Based on the prior-year sales figure in the preview, the reported growth implies sales of roughly $1.056 billion, slightly above the $1.04–$1.05 billion estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 sales surpassed $1 billion for the first time in company history, growing 8% year-over-year, with the Facet acquisition contributing approximately 3 percentage points of that growth.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.15 came in above the $1.12–$1.13 consensus and at the top of the preview’s estimated all-in guidance range. The beat was modest rather than a large cushion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EPS reached $1.15.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.12 (Zacks) / $1.13 (broad Street).” The preview also estimated “the all-in implied Q4 range” at “$1.08–$1.15.”

surprises.description: Facet was expected to add about $0.10–$0.15 to FY2027 EPS, but management instead expects it to dilute FY2027 EPS by about $0.12. That reverses the expected direction of its earnings contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Facet … is expected to dilute full-year fiscal 2027 EPS by approximately $0.12 due to $22 million of incremental amortization and higher interest expense, though it is accretive on a cash basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s modeled FY2027 Street bar included “full-year Facet accretion ~$0.10–0.15.”

surprises.description: Facet’s Q4 EPS dilution was twice the amount the preview said management had guided to: $0.06 versus about $0.03. This was an additional near-term drag even though reported Q4 EPS beat consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Facet diluted Q4 EPS by $0.06.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided ~ $0.03 of Q4 Facet dilution.”

surprises.description: Life Sciences grew 10%, well above the preview’s 2.4% consensus growth estimate. The preview had identified the segment as a possible upside-surprise candidate, but the reported growth substantially exceeded that low bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Life Sciences grew 10% on double-digit disk drive demand tied to the HAMR technology shift.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Life Sciences | $84M | ~$82M | +2.4%.”

surprises.description: The call reported a sharp China mobile-market surge, including nearly 40% growth in OE replacement parts. The preview discussed mobile aftermarket strength and modeled modest overall Mobile Solutions growth, but did not anticipate this specific regional and channel strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China mobile sales surged 27%, driven by a nearly 40% increase in OE replacement part sales.”

surprises.description: Donaldson restarted share repurchases after the preview described them as paused for deleveraging. The company expects repurchases of about 1% of shares, primarily to offset dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company restarted share repurchases after pausing for the Facet acquisition, expecting to buy back about 1% of shares to offset dilution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation — buybacks are paused to delever after the $820M Facet deal.”

in_line: Q4 consolidated operating margin was 17.5%, within the preview’s estimated 17%–18% range; the preview had anticipated a fresh record.

FY2027 EPS guidance of roughly $4.30 was at the low end of the preview’s modeled $4.30–$4.40 range, while the 16.9% operating-margin target with 90 basis points of expansion was consistent with the preview’s expectation of mid-year normalization.
Full-year FY2026 EPS of $3.98 was in line with the preview’s expectation that the year would land near $3.98.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $151.8 million, beating both the $146.8 million consensus and management’s expected 3%–4% year-over-year decline; sales were essentially flat instead. Actual OEM production fell only 1.4%, helping explain the stronger result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fourth-quarter net sales of $151.8 million were essentially flat year-over-year but beat the company's original 3%-4% decline estimate, as actual OEM production fell only 1.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $146.8M”; “Management's own Q4 guide ... revenue down 3–4% y/y.”

surprises.description: Q4 GAAP EPS of $0.95 came in below the $1.36 consensus, while adjusted EPS of $2.06 held steady year over year and was above the preview’s base-case adjusted EPS range. The GAAP and adjusted figures therefore tell sharply different stories about the quarter’s earnings versus expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income dropped to $3.9 million ($0.95) from $8.3 million ($2.01) though adjusted EPS held steady at $2.06.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) $1.36”; the preview’s base scenario estimated “Adj. EPS $1.25–1.55.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue reached $579.4 million, above the preview’s implied $573.5 million–$575.0 million range and growing 2.5%, rather than the expected 1.5%–1.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record annual revenue of $579.4 million in fiscal 2026, up 2.5% from $565.1 million.”

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 restructuring savings were higher than the preview’s indicated run-rate implied: management reported about $6 million realized in the year, alongside another 7% headcount reduction. The preview had cited $4.6 million of savings year to date and only about $0.2 million of additional quarterly savings beginning in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restructuring actions have delivered $9.5 million in cumulative savings since fiscal 2025, including about $6 million realized in fiscal 2026, with headcount reduced an additional 7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$4.6M of savings YTD”; “An incremental $0.8M annualized ... begins in Q4 (~$0.2M/quarter).”

surprises.description: Management gave a concrete weaker FY2027 production outlook: North American production is expected to decline about 2%, with a nearly 6% decline at its three largest customers. The preview anticipated cautious FY2027 framing, but did not give this degree of customer-specific weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guides to softer fiscal 2027 conditions, forecasting an approximately 2% decline in North American production and a nearly 6% decline at its three largest customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With restructuring savings peaking and ~$3M of EV cancellation still to annualize, does management guide FY27 revenue up, flat, or down?”

surprises.description: The company quantified a substantial peso-related margin and cost exposure: at the peso’s five-year average, FY2026 gross margin would have been about 100 basis points higher, and a 5% dollar/peso move affects annual manufacturing costs by roughly $4 million before hedging. The preview flagged FX as a key risk but did not quantify this exposure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A peso at its 5-year average of 19.50 would have improved fiscal 2026 gross margin by about 100 basis points, and a 5% dollar/peso move affects annual manufacturing costs by roughly $4 million before hedging.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FX / peso. Q3 swung to a $0.9M loss ... STRT's manufacturing base is in Mexico, so the peso is the dominant non-operating swing factor.”

surprises.description: The company bought back about 110,000 shares in Q4, around 2% of shares outstanding, for $7.4 million. That is a meaningful execution update on the $40 million program the preview identified as a key watch item, although the preview did not specify an expected amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized a new $40 million stock repurchase program after buying back approximately 110,000 shares (about 2% of shares outstanding) for $7.4 million in the fourth quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “How much was executed in Q4 is arguably the highest-conviction lever on this equity, and the first quarter of disclosure lands on this print.”

in_line: Management’s broad cautious FY2027 framing was consistent with the preview’s warning that softer OEM volumes and declining revenue were possible; the specific production declines, especially at the three largest customers, were more informative than the preview’s general concern.

surprises.description: The preview said a second straight decline in IoT Systems Solutions could undermine the view that federal delays were only a timing issue. Instead, revenue rebounded 16% sequentially to over $15 million as shutdown-related headwinds eased, including recovery in federal business, network switches, and out-of-band management.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IoT systems solutions revenue rebounded 16% sequentially to over $15 million as federal government shutdown headwinds eased, with recovery in out-of-band management, network switches, and federal business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 was $13.2M and shrinking on ‘slower federal spending and extended procurement cycles.’ Management framed this as timing, not demand. This is the highest-margin, highest-cash-flow line — a second straight decline turns a timing story into a structural one.”

surprises.description: The preview put the FY27 unmanned-systems bar at roughly $22–24 million and warned that a lower figure would break the growth math. Management said the business should be 15%–20% of FY27 revenue, or roughly $25 million-plus, a higher quantified outlook than that bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects [unmanned systems] to represent 15%-20% of total revenue (roughly $25 million-plus) in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Doubling $12M → ~$24M”; “Any FY27 drone dollar figure below ~$22M breaks the math.”

surprises.description: The preview identified Vecima’s contribution and closing as issues to confirm, and listed possible EPS dilution as a bear case. The acquisition was reported as immediately accretive, with about $5 million in annual revenue at mid-to-high-60s gross margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired Vecima Networks' Industrial IoT business (including Nero Global Tracking) for $11.7 million, adding approximately $5 million in annual revenue at mid-to-high 60s gross margins, immediately accretive to earnings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Vecima close confirmation, purchase accounting, and accretion”; “Q1 guide <$32M or Vecima dilutive to EPS.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated non-GAAP gross margin at about 43.5%. Q4 margin came in at 44.1%, above that estimate, while management expected margins to remain at or near that level in FY27 rather than signaling a further step-up to 45% or more.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP gross margin improved to 44.1%”; management is “guiding to margins at or near current levels in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin (non-GAAP) ~43.5% (est.)”; “Watch for a raised structural GM target (45%+).”

surprises.description: The preview modeled about $30 million gross from the May offering and estimated pro forma net cash of roughly $25–30 million. The company reported over $44 million in net proceeds for the quarter and ended FY26 debt-free with over $60 million in cash before the Nero acquisition, indicating a larger-than-modeled financing and a stronger cash position.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised over $44 million in net proceeds during the quarter, repaid the remaining $8.7 million of debt to end fiscal year debt-free, and finished with over $60 million in cash (before the Nero acquisition close).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Add ~$30M gross from the May 29 offering”; “Pro-forma net cash likely ~$25–30M”; “Any hint of a further raise is the worst possible outcome.”

surprises.description: The preview discussed the unmanned-systems ramp and named design wins, but did not anticipate a specific increase in active engagements. Management reported that engagements had tripled since Q1 and that products had shipped to more than a dozen customers, including in counter-UAS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active unmanned systems engagements tripled from roughly 10 in Q1 to over 30 today, with products shipped to over a dozen customers including in the counter-UAS area.”

in_line: Q4 revenue of $31.2 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.04 were within guidance and broadly matched the preview’s roughly $31 million-plus and $0.04 functional whisper; the revenue was also close to the $30.69–30.71 million consensus.

FY26 revenue of nearly $121 million was close to the preview’s approximately $120.5 million estimate. Its reported comparison was about 8% growth excluding Gridspertise, but the total revenue result was not a material headline beat against the preview.
FY26 unmanned-systems revenue of $12.6 million was close to the preview’s approximately $12 million expectation and within the $10–14 million guidance range.
Software and services mix exceeding 10% pro forma after Nero was anticipated in the preview; the full-year increase from 5%–6% to 7%–8% was consistent with that mix improvement.

Q1 FY27 revenue guidance of $31–33 million had a $32 million midpoint, broadly in the preview’s $32–33 million base range, and management’s reiterated confidence in full-year double-digit growth matched the preview’s expectation of qualitative rather than hard-dollar FY27 framing.
FY26 embedded IoT solutions growth of more than 15% was consistent with the preview’s emphasis on embedded IoT as the company’s growth driver.

surprises.description: WSM’s comparable-brand growth was 6.2% and revenue was $1.96 billion, exceeding the preview’s $1.91 billion revenue consensus and its base-case comp range of 3.5%–4.5%. Growth also came while the home furnishings industry was essentially flat, so nearly all of it represented market-share gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 comparable brand revenue grew 6.2%” and “total revenue up 6.7% to $1.96 billion,” while “the home furnishings industry was essentially flat, meaning nearly all growth was market share gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus net revenues: “$1.91B”; base scenario: “$1.90–1.93B (comps +3.5–4.5%).”

surprises.description: Pottery Barn comps rose 5.1%, well above the preview’s 2.3% consensus, making the largest brand-level beat among the brands with stated estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pottery Barn 5.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Comp — Pottery Barn: +2.3%.”

surprises.description: Williams Sonoma comps grew 7.6%, 1.5 percentage points above the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Williams Sonoma led at 7.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Comp — Williams Sonoma: +6.1%.”

surprises.description: West Elm comps were 6.4%, a smaller but positive beat against the preview’s 5.8% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “West Elm 6.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Comp — West Elm: +5.8%.”

surprises.description: Children’s comps came in at 3.5%, below the preview’s 4.9% estimate, making it the clear brand-level miss despite positive growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “children’s 3.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Comp — PB Kids & Teen: +4.9%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 45.5%, below the preview’s roughly 46% level that it said would indicate mitigation was running ahead of plan. Tariffs drove a 230-basis-point merchandise-margin decline, only partly offset by supply-chain efficiencies and occupancy leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin fell approximately 160 basis points to 45.5%, driven by a 230 basis point merchandise margin decline from tariffs, partially offset by 70 basis points of supply chain efficiencies and occupancy leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any print holding above ~46% would signal mitigation is running ahead of plan.”

surprises.description: SG&A was 28.2% of revenue, better than the preview’s 28.8% estimate, with leverage driven largely by employment expense. This was stronger cost control than the preview’s expected 40 basis points of leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A leveraged approximately 100 basis points to 28.2% of revenue,” including “120 basis points of employment expense leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SG&A rate: 28.8% of revs” and “−40 bps.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS of $2.10 was a modest beat over the preview’s published $2.05 estimate, but it only reached the low end of the preview’s stated practical bar of $2.10–$2.15.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS of $2.10 rose 5% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS: $2.05”; the preview also said “the practical bar was closer to $2.10–2.15.”

surprises.description: B2B delivered a record-volume quarter, growing 14.5%, with contract up 20% and trade up 12%. The preview did not identify a B2B growth or volume expectation against which to compare this result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “B2B grew 14.5% to a record volume quarter, with contract up 20% and trade up 12%.”

surprises.description: The emerging brands Rejuvenation, Mark and Graham, and GreenRow all posted double-digit growth, an additional area of strength not quantified in the preview’s brand estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All emerging brands (Rejuvenation, Mark and Graham, GreenRow) posting double-digit growth.”

surprises.description: Management newly flagged a roughly 150-basis-point Q4 headwind from anniversarying the prior year’s shrink-accrual benefit, as well as continued fuel-cost pressure. The preview did not identify either as a prospective headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged a Q4 headwind of ~150 basis points from anniversarying last year's shrink accrual benefit and warned of continued fuel cost pressure.”

surprises.description: WSM made no share repurchases in Q2 despite retaining about $1.1 billion of authorization, while the preview had singled out repurchase cadence as a key issue and described buybacks as a marginal EPS lever. The higher dividend partly offsets the absence of repurchases but does not establish that buybacks were expected in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company paid $90 million in dividends (15% increase) but did not repurchase shares in Q2, retaining ~$1.1 billion in buyback authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SG&A leverage and buyback pace” was a key metric to watch; the preview described “repurchase cadence” as “the marginal EPS lever.”

in_line: The full-year guidance increase was expected: the preview said the low end was stale and that the question was the size of the raise, not whether one came. The new comp range of 4.0%–6.5% also reached the preview’s bull-case threshold of a floor at 4% or higher.
The preview expected tariff refunds, if received, to be GAAP-only and non-recurring. WSM’s operational guidance raise excluded the refund benefit, consistent with that expected treatment.
The release was issued after market close, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q2 cRPO growth was 14% in constant currency, one point ahead of the roughly 13% guide and the preview’s baseline. This cleared the preview’s 14% “clean beat” threshold and addressed its main backlog concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CRPO accelerated to $33.5 billion, up 14% in constant currency and one point ahead of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guide: ~13% cc”; “≥14% cc is a clean beat.”

surprises.description: The Q3 cRPO outlook was approximately 14%, at the top of the preview’s cited 13–14% threshold rather than merely tracking the roughly 13% baseline. That gives a stronger signal for backlog growth into Q3 than the preview’s base case assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to $11.42–$11.5 billion (11–12% constant currency growth) with CRPO growth of approximately 14%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Oppenheimer's Brian Schwartz flagged (he wants 13–14% in Q3 to underwrite H2 reacceleration)”; the base scenario expected “Q3 cRPO guided ~13%.”

surprises.description: The FY27 revenue increase was partly driven by anticipated Contentful and Fin closings: $200 million of the $300 million constant-currency increase came from those deals, while the organic increase was $100 million. The preview expected a guidance raise and focused on organic reacceleration, so the acquisition-heavy composition is less supportive of that organic-growth case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised FY27 revenue guidance by $300 million in constant currency to $46.1–$46.4 billion, comprising $100 million organic and $200 million from the anticipated Contentful and Fin closings, partially offset by a $100 million FX headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side expects a raise to at least $46.0–46.2B”; the preview also highlighted “Organic growth ex-Informatica” and described the concern that “M&A is masking it.”

surprises.description: Agentforce ARR reached $1.5 billion, above the preview’s prior-quarter reference of over $1 billion and even the alternative tracker figure of $1.2 billion. That is a stronger reported ARR level than the preview’s conservative benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Agentforce ARR reached $1.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1: … Agentforce ARR >$1B (some trackers put it at $1.2B, +205% Y/Y — treat the higher figure as unverified).”

surprises.description: The call reported rapid agent usage and booking momentum, including 3.2 billion agentic uses, a 70% quarter-over-quarter increase in accounts running agents in production, and more than doubled Agentforce bookings. The preview wanted proof that AI usage and bookings were translating into monetization, but these call figures establish stronger adoption and demand rather than a quantified usage-to-revenue conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “3.2 billion agentic ‘AW’ uses in Q2 (up 97% QoQ)”; “accounts running agents in production up 70% quarter-over-quarter (2,000 new paying customers added)”; “Agentforce bookings and Agentforce 1/Agentforce for Apps bookings more than doubled quarter-over-quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for detail on “AWU consumption billing converting to recognized revenue” and described “AI monetization quality” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Salesforce launched Claudeforce with Anthropic and said the product is intended to require premium-edition upgrades carrying a 60–80% pricing premium, but only 5% of sales/service knowledge workers have upgraded so far. The partnership and pricing path were not anticipated in the preview; the low current upgrade penetration leaves adoption and monetization to be demonstrated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched Claudeforce with Anthropic, targeting general availability in September at Dreamforce,” with premium editions carrying “a 60–80% pricing premium” and “only 5% of sales/service knowledge workers have upgraded so far.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked for “AI monetization quality” and “new-logo vs. expansion split,” but did not mention Claudeforce, Anthropic, or premium-edition upgrade penetration.

surprises.description: Management reported the strongest net-new AOV growth in four years alongside near-record-low attrition, providing a concrete positive sales-quality signal where the preview had identified AOV as a key leading indicator but did not expect or quantify a four-year high.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Salesforce reported the strongest net new AOV growth in four years alongside near-record-low attrition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Net-new AOV outpacing expansion AOV … and showing up in cRPO” was needed for the bull case, and called AOV the CFO’s “stated H2 leading indicator.”

surprises.description: Combined AI and data ARR was described as about to cross $4 billion, rather than having reached the $4 billion threshold the preview identified. This is a small shortfall against that milestone expectation, even as Agentforce ARR itself exceeded the preview’s benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined AI and data ARR is about to cross $4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for: AI+data ARR ≥$4B.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $11.35 billion: a slight beat of the $11.33 billion consensus and the high end of company guidance, but below the preview’s estimated $11.40–$11.45 billion buy-side whisper range. The result therefore beat the published estimate while falling short of the higher informal bar described in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 revenue reached $11.35 billion … above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue Consensus: $11.33B”; the preview also estimated a functional buy-side whisper of “$11.40–11.45B.”

in_line: Non-GAAP operating margin of 34.1% and GAAP operating margin of 20.5% were broadly in line with the preview’s expectations of about 34% non-GAAP and 20–21% GAAP.

The FY27 revenue guidance was raised, as the preview expected; the surprise is that most of the constant-currency increase came from anticipated Contentful and Fin closings rather than organic growth.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $757 million, above both the $725–745 million guided range and the roughly $738 million consensus. FY26 revenue of $2.854 billion also exceeded the $2.82–2.84 billion annual guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue reached a record $757 million, exceeding the guided range of $725-745 million”; “full-year FY26 revenue was $2.854 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 revenue guide was “$725–745M” with consensus “$738.3M”; FY26 full-year guide was “$2.82–2.84B.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP operating margin was 26.2%, substantially above the 21–23% guide and the preview’s roughly 22.5% consensus expectation. The call attributed the outperformance to lower opex from hiring timing and higher revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP operating margin was 26.2%, well above the guided 21-23% range due to lower opex from hiring timing and higher revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 non-GAAP operating margin guide: “21–23%”; consensus: “~22.5%.”

surprises.description: FY27 non-GAAP operating margin guidance of 24–25% is above the preview’s expected roughly 22.5–23% range, despite the preview’s concern that AI investment could hold margins flat or push them down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 revenue guidance of $3.18-3.23 billion ... with non-GAAP operating margin of 24-25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “margin ~22.5–23%”; the preview said AI investment could lead management to “guide FY27 margin flat-to-down.”

surprises.description: FY26 free cash flow was $841 million, well above the prior $760–780 million full-year guide. The preview’s implied Q4 FCF was $197–217 million, but the call facts provide only the full-year result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY26 free cash flow was $841 million (29% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 FCF guide was “$760–780M.”

surprises.description: FY27 revenue guidance of $3.18–3.23 billion is centered near the $3.20 billion consensus, but it does not deliver the 14%+ growth or roughly $3.23–3.28 billion level the preview described as the buy-side whisper. The guide’s upper end only reaches the whisper’s lower bound.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 revenue guidance of $3.18-3.23 billion implies 12% growth at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY27 consensus was “~$3.20B (~13% growth)” but the buy-side whisper was “14%+, or ~$3.23–3.28B.”

surprises.description: Ending ARR reached $2.549 billion, just above the preview’s estimated $2.52–2.54 billion range, and its growth rate accelerated in Q4 rather than continuing the deceleration the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY26 ending ARR was $2.549 billion, up 16% year-over-year, with the growth rate accelerating in Q4 versus the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q4 ARR at “~$2.52–2.54B” and said ARR growth had decelerated “18% → 16% → 15%”; it noted Q4 needed a “seasonally strong add (~$90M+ sequential) to hold ~14%.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a one-time $1.2 billion tax valuation allowance release that lifted reported Q4 GAAP EPS to $4.34; without it, GAAP EPS would have been $0.21. The preview gave a non-GAAP EPS estimate, not an expectation of this large GAAP tax benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 GAAP EPS of $4.34 included a onetime $1.2 billion tax valuation allowance release; excluding it, GAAP EPS would have been $0.21.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a restructuring affecting about 5% of the workforce, with $33–43 million of nonrecurring charges; most savings are being reinvested in AI, cloud native, and sales expansion. The preview discussed AI reinvestment as a margin risk but did not anticipate the workforce action or its scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a restructuring affecting approximately 5% of its global workforce, incurring $33-43 million in nonrecurring charges with the majority of savings reinvested into AI, cloud native, and sales expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview raised “the AI reinvestment question” and noted AI-related spend could justify flat-to-down FY27 margin guidance.

surprises.description: External-storage activity showed stronger traction than the preview could confirm: bookings increased sharply quarter over quarter, several deals had seven-figure ACV, and limited-availability NetApp support helped secure multiple large Q4 wins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “External storage bookings saw a sharp quarter-over-quarter increase with several 7-figure ACV deals, and NetApp support (in limited availability) was instrumental in multiple large Q4 wins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “seven-figure deal count, and external-storage attach” and noted “NetApp and Lenovo due in CY26.”

surprises.description: FY27 free cash flow guidance of $850–950 million is above the preview’s cited bull-case threshold of at least $800 million, although the preview did not provide a base-case FY27 FCF estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 ... free cash flow of $850-950 million (28% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull scenario listed “FCF ≥$800M.”

surprises.description: Management said average Q4 billing duration was 3.3 years, slightly below expectations. The preview discussed supply-chain-related future-start licenses but did not specify an expected billing-duration figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 average billing duration was 3.3 years (slightly below expectations).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call described the 3.3-year duration as “slightly below expectations.”

in_line: FY27 revenue guidance midpoint of about $3.205 billion was close to the preview’s roughly $3.20 billion consensus/base case, though below the higher buy-side whisper.
NRR remained at 106%, flat quarter over quarter, consistent with the preview’s cited Q3 level of 106% and its concern about continued pressure.
FY26 TCV bookings grew in the high teens while revenue grew 12%, so bookings still outpaced revenue as the preview’s supply-chain timing thesis anticipated.

surprises.description: CrowdStrike was expected to add $284–286 million of net new ARR, with the buy-side looking for roughly $300–310 million. It reported a record $333 million, more than $45 million above the high end of guidance and above even the buy-side bogey.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All-time record net new ARR of $333 million in Q2 FY27,” which “beat[] the high end of guidance by more than $45 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net new ARR: $284–286M”; “~$285M consensus; ~$300–310M buy-side bogey.”

surprises.description: The preview expected at most a token full-year net new ARR guidance increase in its base case, and said a raise to at least $1.34 billion would be a bull-case outcome. CrowdStrike raised the midpoint to $1.355 billion, above that bull-case threshold, after cumulative increases of about $116 million since the initial outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year FY27 net new ARR guidance to a midpoint of $1.355 billion”; the cumulative increase since the initial FY27 outlook is “approximately $116 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the key was whether guidance moved “above $1.303B at the high end”; its base case was a “Token raise, $1.30–1.32B,” while its bull case called for “Raised to ≥$1.34B.”

surprises.description: Operating income and margin came in ahead of the preview’s estimates: non-GAAP operating income was $372 million rather than about $347 million, and the margin was 25% rather than roughly 24.1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income hit a record $372 million (25% margin, up 350 basis points YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income” consensus was “~$347M (24.1% margin).”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow margin was stronger than the preview’s seasonal-trough expectation. The preview cited about 24.5%, while CrowdStrike reported a record $377 million at a 26% margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was a record $377 million (26% of revenue), up 33% YoY.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FCF margin: ~24.5% (seasonal low)” and described Q2 as “the seasonal trough.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS exceeded the preview’s $0.29 estimate, reaching a record $0.31. The preview expected 26.1% year-over-year growth, versus the reported 34% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was a record $0.31, up 34% YoY on a split-adjusted basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS (post-split)” consensus was “$0.29,” with “+26.1%” year-over-year growth.

surprises.description: Ending ARR modestly exceeded the preview’s $5.79 billion expectation and grew faster than the preview’s approximately 24% estimate. CrowdStrike also reported a fourth consecutive quarter of accelerating ending ARR growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ending ARR reached $5.84 billion (up more than 25% YoY), marking the fourth consecutive quarter of accelerating ending ARR growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed ending ARR consensus of “$5.79B” and “+24%” year-over-year growth.

surprises.description: Falcon Flex strength exceeded the preview’s already high prior-quarter benchmarks: ARR growth accelerated from 99% to 101%, and CrowdStrike added more than 935 Flex accounts, exceeding the prior three quarters combined. The reported 53% uplift for customers who reflexed at least twice was close to the preview’s 51% historical figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Falcon Flex ARR surpassed $2.29 billion, accelerating to 101% YoY growth”; “more than 935 new Flex accounts added—exceeding the prior three quarters combined.” Customers who reflexed at least twice had ending ARR “53% higher than their initial Flex baseline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Flex accounts had reached “$1.9B ending ARR, +99% y/y,” with “300+ accounts added in Q1,” and cited a “51% uplift” for customers who had reflexed multiple times.

surprises.description: The preview specifically wanted an AIDR ARR amount, but the reported call fact gave only a sequential comparison: AIDR ending ARR nearly tripled versus Q1, without stating its dollar value. That leaves the requested dollar disclosure unmet even as the growth description was strong.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AIDR ending ARR nearly tripled versus Q1”; no AIDR dollar amount is provided in the supplied call facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Investors need a disclosed dollar figure, not another percentage off an undisclosed base.”

in_line: CrowdStrike reaffirmed at least 30% free cash flow margin for the full year, matching the preview’s expectation of “FCF margin ≥30%.”
The 53% ending ARR uplift for customers who reflexed at least twice was broadly in line with the preview’s cited 51% average uplift for customers who had reflexed multiple times.

surprises.description: Okta’s current RPO growth accelerated by roughly 200 basis points, stronger than the preview’s roughly 12–13% buy-side bar for another quarter of acceleration. Management attributed the strength mainly to large enterprises, rather than AI.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Current RPO growth accelerated by roughly 200 basis points,” which management attributed “primarily to large enterprise strength rather than AI.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side bar is realistically $2.53B+ (~12–13% growth) — a second straight quarter of cRPO acceleration is the entire re-rating thesis.”

surprises.description: Okta raised its FY27 revenue-growth outlook to 10–11%, above the prior 9–10% range and the preview’s expectation that a meaningful raise would be to at least $3.23–3.24 billion. The call facts provide a growth range, not an updated dollar range, so the size of the increase against that dollar threshold cannot be confirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Okta guided FY27 total revenue growth to 10–11%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance to be updated: revenue $3.185–3.205B (+9–10%).” The preview also said the bar was “a raise to ≥$3.23–3.24B.”

surprises.description: New products rose to approximately 30% of bookings, above the 25% Q1 level highlighted in the preview. The preview flagged new-product mix as an important measure but did not give a specific Q2 forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New products represented approximately 30% of bookings in Q2,” with Okta Identity Governance the leading contributor.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New products ≈25% of Q1 bookings”; the preview also identified “New-product mix” as a key item to watch.

surprises.description: The call provided concrete evidence of paid AI-agent deals—including several worth over $1 million—where the preview said quantified agent contribution was the key proof investors wanted and qualitative-only commentary was the likeliest disappointment. However, management said the business remains too small to register in Okta’s roughly $3 billion revenue base.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Okta closed dozens of Okta for AI agents deals including several worth over $1 million,” but management said this “remains too small to show up in the ~$3 billion revenue base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any quantified contribution — agent-identity bookings, ACV, pipeline, or customer counts” and called “Qualitative-only commentary” the likeliest disappointment vector.

surprises.description: FY27 free-cash-flow margin guidance of 28–29% was above the preview’s prior 27–28% range, while the non-GAAP operating-margin guide of 26% was at the top of its prior 25–26% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Okta guided FY27 … non-GAAP operating margin of 26% and free cash flow margin of 28–29%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance to be updated … non-GAAP op. income … (25–26%) … FCF … (27–28%).”

surprises.description: The call reported strong growth in Okta’s largest customer tier—more than 20% year over year in customers above $1 million ACV, to over 600—without a comparable forecast for that tier in the preview. This adds evidence of large-enterprise strength beyond the preview’s discussion of $100,000-plus customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers with over $1 million in ACV grew more than 20% year-over-year, bringing the total to over 600 such customers.”

surprises.description: Okta completed the Premiso acquisition, adding a platform with 400 native risk detections versus Okta’s existing 90. The preview did not flag this acquisition or the added detection capability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Okta completed its acquisition of Premiso,” which offers “400 native risk detections versus Okta’s existing 90,” to strengthen AI security and agentic runtime controls.

surprises.description: Okta used cash to settle the remaining $350 million of convertible notes and repurchased $125 million of shares, with $555 million still available under its buyback authorization. The preview noted an active buyback and cash balance but did not anticipate the debt settlement or give a repurchase amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Settled the remaining $350 million of convertible notes in cash in June, leaving no convertible debt,” ended with “about $2.3 billion in cash and investments,” and repurchased “1.5 million shares for $125 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “cash $2.589B; buyback active.”

in_line: Q3 current RPO guidance of 11–12% was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of about 11% growth for Q3.
The approximate one-point FY27 revenue drag from shifting professional services to GSI partners was already anticipated in the preview, which said the shift carried a “~1pt revenue headwind.”
The approximately 40% ACV uplift when a new product is included in a deal matched the roughly 40% uplift cited for Q1 in the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $96B, above the preview’s $94–95B buy-side whisper and well above its roughly $92B consensus; growth also accelerated for a fourth consecutive quarter rather than merely matching the implied growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2027 total revenue reached a record $96 billion, more than doubling year-over-year, with growth accelerating for the fourth consecutive quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus $91.9–92.3B”; “Buy-Side / Whisper $94–95B.”

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue guide of $108B exceeds the preview’s ~$104B consensus and its $105B bull-line threshold, reaching the top of the preview’s bull scenario rather than its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to $108 billion (plus or minus 2%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY27 rev guide” consensus “$103.8–104.1B”; “$105B as the bull line”; bull scenario “≥$106–108B.”

surprises.description: The margin outlook is materially weaker than the preview’s expectation of about 75% with no dilution from the Rubin ramp: management now expects 74% in Q3, a 71–72% trough in Q4, and only 72–73% in FY2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margins are being reset lower due to extreme memory pricing, with Q3 expected at 74%, bottoming at 71-72% in Q4, then settling at 72-73% in fiscal 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin” company guidance “74.9% GAAP / 75.0% non-GAAP ±50bp”; consensus “~75%”; buy-side “≥75%, no dilution from Rubin ramp.”

surprises.description: Data Center revenue reached $89B, above the preview’s roughly $85.7B consensus and its $85–87B base-case range. AC I&E grew faster sequentially than hyperscale, supporting the expected broadening of demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 data center revenue rose 18% sequentially to $89 billion, with hyperscale at $49 billion (up 13% QoQ) and AC I&E at $40 billion (up 25% QoQ and 138% YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Data Center rev” consensus “~$85.7B”; base case “Data Center $85–87B”; the preview identified “continued ACIE broadening” as an important proof point.

surprises.description: Management put a specific FY2028 growth outlook at about 70%, while saying unconstrained demand would imply roughly 100% growth. The preview did not give a FY2028 growth estimate, so the gap is against the demand ceiling stated on the call, not a published consensus forecast.
