surprises.description: Management disclosed a sharp G&A increase but attributed much of it to share-based compensation and public-company transition consulting, and said the cost base should not increase substantially going forward. That is more reassuring about near-term overhead growth than the preview’s concern that losses would widen as production scaled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “G&A expense jumped to $5.5 million from $1.0 million a year earlier,” including “$1.5 million public-company transition consulting,” and management expects “this cost base not to increase substantially going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “signaled losses widen as production scales ahead of revenue” and warned that “Q2 burn above ~$12M” would imply a shorter runway.

surprises.description: Management provided a much larger long-term capacity ambition than the preview’s near-term facility discussion: roughly 40 metric tons annually by decade-end, alongside an approximately 11-month modular build cycle. These scale and build-time claims were not part of the preview’s stated expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management projects capacity scaling to “~40 metric tons annually by decade-end” against a “~$3.2 billion serviceable addressable market,” and highlighted an “~11-month modular build cycle versus a 7-9 year path for new entrants.”

surprises.description: Management asked investors to model 154.3 million post-IPO shares, below the 160.67 million shares outstanding cited in the preview. The lower share-count assumption is modestly favorable on a per-share basis.
surprises.fact_evidence: Investors should model “~154.3 million post-IPO shares.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “160.67M shares now.”

in_line: June 30 total backlog was $241.5 million versus the preview’s cited $245 million, and funded backlog was $61.9 million versus $65 million—broadly in line before the subsequent August agreements.

Construction at SNTN was substantially complete, with authorization to operate targeted for Q4 2026. That remains within the preview’s 2H 2026 timing expectation, though the call facts do not report qualified production.
The Richland Framatome JV remained on the expected 2027 production path; the preview had already noted the June NRC license amendment.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $42.4 million, below the roughly $44.0 million consensus and the $44.8 million needed to meet management’s prior-year guidance floor. It also fell 3.1% sequentially, rather than stabilizing in the preview’s $43–45 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 net revenue fell 23.1% year-over-year to $42.4 million” and “declined 3.1% sequentially from Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~ $44.0M”; “Q4 needed for $185M / $0.60” was “$44.8M”; and “Sequential stabilization at $43–45M is the bull case’s foundation.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS of $0.11 missed the roughly $0.13 consensus and was also below the $0.15 needed to reach the low end of management’s FY26 adjusted EPS guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted net income dropped to $1.4 million ($0.11 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS ~ $0.13”; the “Q4 needed for $185M / $0.60” table showed “$0.15.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $2.7 million, well below the preview’s estimated $3.5–4.0 million, and its margin fell to 6.5% from 8.7% a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EBITDA fell to $2.7 million (6.5% of revenue) from $4.8 million (8.7%) a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$3.5–4.0M (est.).”

surprises.description: Gross margin slipped to 78%, despite the preview’s expectation that it would hold around 79%; management attributed the decline partly to higher inventory obsolescence and shipping and warehouse costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 78% from 79.9% year-over-year due to product mix shifts, higher inventory obsolescence, and increased shipping and warehouse costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GM has been remarkably resilient at 79.0% GAAP / 79.4% adjusted in Q3”; “If GM holds ~79% … the model de-levers gracefully.”

surprises.description: Management said it does not expect trends to turn positive until FY27 Q3–Q4, after difficult comparisons in Q1 and Q2. That points to a longer period of weak trends than the preview’s stabilization-focused discussion anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged difficult comparables in Q1 and Q2 of fiscal 2027 and does not expect trends to turn positive until fiscal Q3-Q4 as new strategies take effect.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The question is whether the base stabilized”; the preview described Q4 sequential stabilization as “the bull case’s foundation.”

surprises.description: Subscription-based revenue remained above 75% of sales and customer retention improved year over year, offering evidence of customer resilience despite the broader revenue decline and some subscribers pausing orders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription-based revenue remained strong at more than 75% of total revenue, and customer retention metrics improved year-over-year despite some subscribers pausing orders.”

in_line: Management issued no formal FY2027 guidance, citing the recent CEO transition. The preview identified deferral to the October convention or no FY27 number as a likely base-case outcome.
Year-end cash was $14.9 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that cash would finish near $15–16 million.

surprises.description: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA was $333 million, below the already-reduced $345–350 million guide the preview treated as the key credibility test. The $12–17 million shortfall was more substantial than an in-line landing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $333 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company FY26 guide … Adj. EBITDA $345–350M”; the preview calls landing inside that band the “binary credibility test.”

surprises.description: The FY2027 adjusted EBITDA range of $340–360 million came in below the preview’s practical $360–370 million anchor and its $375 million threshold for a stronger outlook. Management described the range as deliberately conservative, but its midpoint is still below the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company guided fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA to $340-$360 million … describing the guidance as deliberately conservative.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says the practical anchor is “~$360–370M,” that the buy-side likely underwrites “$360–380M,” and that “≥$375M” supports the bull case.

surprises.description: June same-store sales fell 7%, sharply weaker than the preview’s expectation of at least a flat Q4 comp and California stabilization. Management attributed the June hit partly to unusually strong at-home sports viewing, estimating a one-time $7–12 million revenue impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “June comped -7% due to record World Cup viewership and NBA finals driving at-home sports viewing, costing an estimated $7-12 million in revenue, a one-time event not repeating next summer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist calls for “FQ4 same-store sales ≥ 0%, with California stabilizing,” and says to watch whether California stabilized in the June quarter.

surprises.description: FY2026 revenue was $1.245 billion, slightly below the preview’s $1.25 billion consensus and the company’s $1.25–1.26 billion guide. The gap was small compared with the EBITDA shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 4% to $1.245 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists FY2026 revenue consensus of “$1.25B” and company guidance of “$1,250–1,260M.”

surprises.description: The events business improved unexpectedly: after losing roughly $40 million of revenue over three years, it turned positive for four consecutive months, and the December-quarter backlog was up 10% rather than down 30% a year earlier. The preview did not flag this business as a potential turnaround.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The events business, which lost roughly $40 million in revenue over three years, turned positive for four consecutive months, with December quarter backlog tracking up 10% versus down 30% a year ago.”

surprises.description: Management plans to shed roughly 10 mostly post-IPO acquired properties to improve leverage, a portfolio-reduction move not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of leverage and capital allocation. The fact that only two or three centers are currently EBITDA-negative suggests the planned exits are not limited to loss-making sites.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to shed roughly 10 mostly post-IPO acquired properties in fiscal 2027 to improve leverage, with only two or three centers currently EBITDA-negative.”

surprises.description: Marketing spend rose from $17 million to $30 million and drove a large increase in impressions, but management said engagement was weak and is shifting toward more targeted, higher-ROI spending. The preview did not anticipate this spending increase or the weak engagement, and the investment adds context to the EBITDA pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marketing spend rose from $17 million to $30 million (1% to 2.5-3% of revenue), lifting quarterly impressions from ~75 million to ~350 million, but weak engagement prompted a shift toward higher-ROI, more targeted spending.”

surprises.description: Despite the lower FY2027 EBITDA range, management guided to same-store sales growth of 1%–3%. That is a more constructive core-sales outlook than the preview’s concern that a guide below $375 million would imply the core bowling business was still shrinking on a same-store basis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company … expects same-store sales of +1% to +3%” in fiscal 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says a FY2027 EBITDA guide below ~$375M “would imply the core bowling business is still shrinking on a same-store basis.”

in_line: Water-park earnings were largely expected to fall after FY2026: the preview said most of the roughly $18 million expected “this summer” would land after the fiscal year closed, and management said roughly 80% of summer earnings would land in the FY2027 September quarter.
Capex remained on a declining path, as the preview had flagged: FY2026 capex was down from the prior year and the FY2027 budget was lower still.

surprises.description: Voyage revenue reached $24 million, above the preview’s $18–20 million pre-print estimate. That is roughly 20–33% higher than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 voyage revenues rose 124% year-over-year to $24 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Voyage revenues: $18–20M”

surprises.description: Net income and adjusted net income both came in well above the preview’s estimates: nearly $10 million versus $6–7 million for net income, and $9.8 million versus about $6 million adjusted. The reported $12 million of EBITDA also exceeded the preview’s roughly $8–9 million adjusted EBITDA estimate, though those EBITDA measures are not identical.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income swung to nearly $10 million”; “adjusted net income surged 755% to $9.8 million”; “Q2 2026 EBITDA reached $12 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net income: ~$6–7M”; “Adjusted net income: ~$6M”; “Adjusted EBITDA: ~$8–9M.”

surprises.description: The fleet-wide TCE rate was $40,300, above the preview’s roughly $33,000–$35,000 estimate. The Aframax’s $133,500 rate added a particularly strong vessel-level result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The fleet-wide TCE rate rose 145% year-over-year to $40,300 in Q2 2026, with the Aframax tanker achieving $133,500.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Daily TCE: ~$33–35k.”

surprises.description: The preview framed January’s $39.8 million tanker capex as a funding gap against $33.2 million of June cash and expected continued reliance on equity issuance. The call said the obligation was already fully covered by cash, which had risen to $48 million by the end of July.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash balance climbed to $33.2 million by end of June 2026 and further to $48 million by end of July 2026”; “$39.78 million CapEx obligation for two product tankers due in January 2027, which management says is already fully covered by cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The January 2027 funding gap. $39.8M capex is due in January 2027 for the two MR product tankers, against $33.2M of cash”; management had said “Equity issuances will continue.”

surprises.description: The call said the fleet is entirely non-Chinese-built and therefore avoids potential U.S. tariff exposure, a risk-mitigating detail the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its fleet is entirely non-Chinese-built, avoiding potential U.S. tariff exposure.”

in_line: The fleet’s 311,431 deadweight capacity was in line with the preview’s expectation of approximately 311,431 dwt following delivery of the additional MR tanker.
The company’s zero bank debt was expected; the preview stated “Bank debt: $0.”

The July share offering’s $6 million gross proceeds and continued equity issuance were consistent with the preview’s discussion of the offering and management’s prior statement that equity issuance would continue.

The first-half $2 million unrealized, non-cash warrant loss is consistent with the preview’s warning that warrant fair-value losses could affect reported results; the call facts do not provide basic EPS or a deemed-dividend figure to resolve that specific concern.

surprises.description: PAHC’s Q4 sales were $396.7 million, about 4.9% above the $378.3 million consensus. The preview said analysts had effectively plugged the top of the implied guidance range and described $365–382 million as the realistic band, so the reported quarter was stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 2026 net sales grew 5% to $396.7 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 FY26 Consensus” net sales: “$378.3M”; the preview also said the realistic band was “$365–382M.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted diluted EPS increased 35% year over year. Using the preview’s $0.57 Q4 FY25 actual, that implies roughly $0.77, above the $0.73 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS up 35%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 adjusted diluted EPS consensus was “$0.73”; Q4 FY25 actual was “$0.57.”

surprises.description: The FY27 adjusted EPS guide of $3.41–$3.59 is above the preview’s $3.32 consensus throughout the range, with a midpoint about 6% higher. This is stronger than the preview’s base-case guide of $3.05–$3.25 and its concern about a conservative new-CEO reset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance” calls for adjusted diluted EPS of “$3.41-$3.59.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus FY27: ... EPS $3.32”; the base scenario expected FY27 EPS “$3.05–3.25.”

surprises.description: FY27 revenue guidance is $1.55–$1.60 billion, with a $1.575 billion midpoint about 2% above the $1.55 billion consensus. That is slightly above the preview’s base-case range, though still within its broader expected outcomes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for net sales of $1.55-1.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus FY27: revenue $1.55B (+3.2%)”; the base scenario expected “$1.52–1.56B.”

surprises.description: Management is assuming only minimal Virginia mycin sales in FY27 after approximately $27 million of FY26 sales, and treats regulatory approval as upside rather than building it into the outlook. The preview expected therapeutic-claim approvals during the transition and discussed a base case with a quantified drag, so the near-total assumed loss is more cautious than that framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management assumed only minimal Virginia mycin sales in Brazil for fiscal 2027 after ~$27 million in fiscal 2026 sales,” with approval “as potential upside.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “expects therapeutic-claim approvals during the transition”; its base case anticipated “Brazil guided as a discrete quantified drag,” and its bull case assumed a headwind “≤$15M with therapeutic approval in hand.”

surprises.description: Despite the Q4 sales beat, the acquired new MFA portfolio fell 11% in the quarter. The preview highlighted Q4 as the first clean comparison after the acquisition and described the underlying franchise as a key growth test, but did not anticipate a decline in the acquired portfolio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The acquired new MFA (Zoetis) portfolio declined 11% in Q4 to $83.9 million against a tough prior-year comparison.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 Animal Health growth is the first honest read on the underlying franchise”; the preview also noted Q3 new MFA sales of “$95.9M (+25%).”

surprises.description: FY26 free cash flow was only $10 million, with an $86.3 million inventory build for the acquired MFA portfolio. This leaves cash conversion weak rather than showing the improvement the preview identified as a key Q4 test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was only $10 million in fiscal 2026, weighed down by an $86.3 million inventory build for the acquired MFA portfolio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called out “Q4 FCF and inventory” and said, “If Q4 doesn't show cash conversion, the quality-of-earnings question moves to the front of the thesis.”

surprises.description: PAHC announced that the Chicago Heights closure is expected to add $15–$20 million of annual adjusted EBITDA, mostly in FY28 and later. The preview did not anticipate this cost-saving opportunity, although management expects only a minimal benefit in FY27.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The planned closure of the Chicago Heights manufacturing facility is expected to generate $15-20 million in annual adjusted EBITDA benefit, mostly in fiscal 2028 and beyond, with only minimal benefit in fiscal 2027.”

surprises.description: The Chicago Heights closure also brings roughly $10 million of cash costs and about $10 million of capex, with additional non-cash write-offs still undetermined. The preview did not flag these one-time outlays.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chicago Heights closure one-time costs are estimated at roughly $10 million in cash costs plus about $10 million in capex, with additional non-cash asset write-offs still undetermined.”

surprises.description: Management expects Q1 FY27 EBIT growth to be negative because of the higher SG&A base, before growth turns positive for the rest of the year. The preview focused on annual FY27 growth expectations and did not flag a first-quarter contraction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Q1 fiscal 2027 EBIT growth to be negative due to a higher SG&A base carried forward from infrastructure investments, before turning positive for the remainder of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY27 EPS consensus of “$3.32 (+8%)” and discussed full-year guidance, but did not anticipate negative Q1 EBIT growth.

surprises.description: Year-end gross and net leverage were 2.9x and 2.6x, respectively, below the preview’s cited Q3 levels of 3.1x and 2.8x. The reduction is a modest improvement against the preview’s concern that leverage could remain around 3x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross leverage stood at 2.9x and net leverage at 2.6x at year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Gross leverage 3.1x” and “net 2.8x” and described the bear case as “leverage stuck ~3x.”

in_line: FY26 net sales of $1.518 billion were close to the preview’s $1.50 billion estimate and within the FY26 guidance range; the reported 17% year-over-year growth was not itself a surprise.
FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $255 million was at the top of the preview’s cited FY26 guidance range of $247–$255 million.
FY27 free cash flow is expected to be significantly greater, with inventory build limited to $25–$30 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a cash-flow inflection and inventory unwind.

surprises.description: Workday modestly exceeded the preview’s revenue expectations: subscription revenue was $2.471 billion versus about $2.455 billion expected, and total revenue was $2.649 billion versus a $2.63–$2.64 billion consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 subscription revenue was $2.471 billion” and “total revenue was $2.649 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $2.63–2.64B” and “Subscription revenue | ~$2.455B.”

surprises.description: AI traction was stronger than the preview’s already-positive adoption expectations: AI ARR was nearly $600 million, and AI products contributed more than $100 million of new ACV and over 25% of new ACV. More than 5,500 customers used an organic agent, above the preview’s 4,000-plus reference point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI products drove more than $100 million of new ACV, accounting for over 25% of all new ACV”; “AI ARR nearly $600 million, up more than 200% year-over-year”; and “More than 5,500 customers are now using one or more organic agents.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1: approaching $500M ARR, new agentic ACV +200% Y/Y, 4,000+ customers on ≥1 agent”; the bull case called for “agentic ARR >$600M.”

surprises.description: The margin outcome beat the preview’s expectations: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 31.1%, and Workday raised FY27 margin guidance to 31% from the preview’s cited 30.5% company guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin was 31.1% in Q2, and full-year FY27 margin guidance was raised to 31%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op margin | ~30%” and FY2027 guidance of “30.5%.”

surprises.description: Workday previewed at least 200 basis points of additional margin expansion in FY28, an incremental longer-term profitability outlook that the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management previewed “at least 200 basis points of additional margin expansion in FY28.”

surprises.description: The company completed its $5 billion buyback program six months early and authorized another $4 billion open-ended repurchase program; the preview did not flag this capital-return action.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed its $5 billion buyback program six months ahead of target, repurchasing $1.3 billion in Q2, and the Board approved a new $4 billion open-ended repurchase program.”

surprises.description: Despite broad agent adoption, monetization through Flex credits appears delayed: only about 200 customers had signed up for Flex credit consumption, with revenue monetization pushed into FY28 and beyond.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only about 200 have signed up for Flex credit consumption, signaling delayed revenue monetization into FY28 and beyond.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described AI as “the whole ‘AI is a tailwind, not an extinction event’ rebuttal” and focused on agentic ARR and adoption, but did not flag delayed monetization.

surprises.description: Management’s Q3 CRPO growth outlook of 11–12% points to a notable slowdown from Q2’s 14.2% growth, with the company citing the Paradox acquisition comparison. The preview focused on Q2 CRPO and did not anticipate this Q3 range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 CRPO growth of 11-12% impacted by lapping the Paradox acquisition.”

surprises.description: Total subscription revenue backlog grew only 8%, and management attributed pressure to a shift toward customer-base bookings versus net-new bookings; this is a weaker backlog growth signal than the preview’s Q1 reference point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total subscription revenue backlog grew only 8% to $27.4 billion, pressured by a mix shift toward customer-base bookings versus net new.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 “total backlog $27.294B (+10.9%)” as its reference point.

surprises.description: Quarterly free cash flow declined year over year to $460 million, a softer cash-flow result than the preview’s focus on FCF durability suggested, although management attributed the decline to an extra payroll run and maintained full-year operating cash flow guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow of $460 million declined year-over-year due to an extra payroll run, while full-year operating cash flow guidance of $3.45 billion was maintained.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Margin and FCF durability” and listed FY27 FCF guidance of “$3.18B (+15%).”

surprises.description: Q2 GAAP results included a large one-time tax benefit from an internal IP transfer, making the reported GAAP result unusually favorable but not indicative of recurring earnings; the preview did not anticipate this item.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP results included a $374 million nonrecurring tax benefit from an internal IP transfer.”

surprises.description: International revenue growth was faster than the preview’s bull-case assumption and the US rate was slower: international grew 17% versus 12% in the US, rather than the preview’s 16% versus 13% comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International revenue growing 17% versus 12% in the US.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case said “international sustains its 16% vs. 13% US premium.”

in_line: Q2 12-month CRPO growth was 14.2%, within the preview’s expected 13.5–14.5% range.
FY27 subscription revenue guidance was essentially reaffirmed at $9.94–$9.95 billion: the low end rose slightly from $9.925 billion, while the high end was unchanged.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $3.15 billion was about 4% above the $3.03 billion consensus and above the preview’s $3.10 billion threshold for a stronger-than-base outcome. This is a materially stronger guide than the preview’s $3.05–$3.12 billion base scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2027 revenue is guided to $3.15 billion (up 15% sequentially and over 50% YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY27 revenue” consensus: “$3.03B”; the preview says “Need $3.10B+ to signal Google/AWS ramp pull-forward.”

surprises.description: Marvell raised its FY2028 revenue outlook by $1.5 billion, from about $16.5 billion to about $18 billion. The increase is larger than the preview’s bull scenario, which described a raise to $17 billion or more.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FY2028 revenue outlook was raised by $1.5 billion to approximately $18 billion (~50% YoY growth), up from the prior $16.5 billion (~45%) forecast.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identifies “FY28 ($16.5B) target revisions” as a key watch item; its bull scenario says “FY28 raised to $17B+.”

surprises.description: The FY2027 revenue outlook rose by $500 million, from about $11.5 billion to about $12 billion. The preview highlighted a possible revision but its scenarios generally assumed the targets would be reiterated or only described a raise in FY2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its FY2027 revenue outlook to approximately $12 billion (~45% YoY growth), up $500 million from the prior ~$11.5 billion outlook one quarter ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 ($11.5B) and FY28 ($16.5B) target revisions”; the base scenario says “FY27/FY28 reiterated.”

surprises.description: Management lifted the Data Center growth outlook to about 60% for FY2027 and more than 60% for FY2028, above the preview’s roughly 50% and 55% growth framework. The segment was also 79% of Q2 revenue, making the upgraded outlook especially relevant to the overall forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data Center, contributing 79% of total revenue, grew 46% YoY in Q2 and is now expected to grow ~60% in FY2027 (up from ~50%) and more than 60% in FY2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists Data Center against “the ~50% FY27 / ~55% FY28 growth framework.”

surprises.description: Scale-up optics and switching were the largest drivers of the FY2028 outlook increase, with scale-up optics accelerating well beyond the prior roughly $300 million category estimate. The preview noted the earlier estimate but did not anticipate this acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The largest driver of the $1.5 billion FY2028 raise is scale-up optics and switching, with scale-up optics accelerating well beyond last quarter's ~$300 million category estimate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview refers to last quarter’s “~$300M” estimate for the scale-up optics category, including “~$150M from Celestial AI CPO.”

surprises.description: Q3 non-GAAP gross margin guidance of 57.5%–58.5% is weak relative to the preview’s 58.5% watch level, and management expects similar levels through FY2028. The preview had flagged below roughly 58.5% as a margin risk, but the guided range has a midpoint of 58.0%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 non-GAAP gross margin is guided to 57.5%-58.5% (down ~90 bps from Q2's 58.9%), pressured by the accelerating custom business mix, with similar levels expected through FY2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says “Q3 non-GAAP GM guide” below “~58.5%” alongside strong revenue would be a “good-news-bad-news” risk.

surprises.description: Marvell disclosed an expanded commercial warrant agreement with the Google/TPU ecosystem, referenced with $120 billion of cumulative revenue potential over six years. The preview discussed the existing Google agreement and warrant, but not this expanded agreement or its stated potential; management said the FY2028 impact is already included, with major upside beyond FY2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An expanded commercial warrant agreement with a key hyperscaler (Google/TPU ecosystem) was signed, referenced at $120 billion cumulative revenue potential over 6 years, though FY2028 impact is already in guidance with major upside in FY2029 and beyond.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says the “Google custom-silicon agreement (signed July 29, 2026) is in hand” and discusses the already disclosed warrant terms.

surprises.description: Management said non-GAAP operating margin is expected to enter the 38%–40% long-term target range in Q4 FY2027 and reach the high end during FY2028. The preview did not flag an operating-margin trajectory, so this was an additional favorable outlook detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 180 bps YoY to 36.6% in Q2, and is expected to enter the 38%-40% long-term target range in Q4 FY2027 and reach the high end during FY2028.”

surprises.description: Marvell said FY2028 operating expenses should grow at roughly half the rate of revenue, pointing to stronger expense leverage than the preview discussed. The preview did not provide an FY2028 operating-expense expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects FY2028 operating expenses to grow at roughly half the rate of revenue.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue and non-GAAP EPS modestly exceeded consensus, despite the preview characterizing the quarter as a non-event. The beats were small: revenue was $2.739 billion versus $2.71 billion and EPS was $0.94 versus $0.93.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marvell delivered record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $2.739 billion ... with non-GAAP EPS of $0.94 ... both exceeding guidance midpoints.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 consensus was “$2.71B” revenue and “$0.93” non-GAAP EPS; the preview says “Q2 itself is a non-event.”

surprises.description: Marvell reported $254 million of Q2 shareholder returns through buybacks and dividends, an additional capital-allocation detail the preview did not discuss. The preview did, however, expect the roughly $1 billion FY2027 supplier-capacity prepayment pace, so that item is in line rather than a separate surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marvell returned $200 million via buybacks and $54 million in dividends in Q2, [and] remains on pace for ~$1 billion in supplier capacity prepayments in FY2027.”

in_line: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 58.9%, close to the preview’s 58.8% consensus.
The FY2028 custom business is expected to more than double, as the preview had already described FY2028 custom revenue as “more than doubling.”
Marvell remained on pace for approximately $1 billion in FY2027 supplier-capacity prepayments, consistent with the preview’s expectation.

surprises.description: Affirm said fiscal Q4 was its most profitable quarter ever even after excluding a tax allowance release. The preview expected a comfortable Q4 beat, but did not flag record core profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Affirm reported its most profitable quarter ever in fiscal Q4 2026, even excluding the tax allowance release.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case: they beat Q4 comfortably”

surprises.description: FY27 revenue less transaction costs is guided to 4.16% of GMV: above the preview’s cited 3%–4% midterm range, but just below its 4.2% upside-watch threshold. That makes the update favorable versus the framework, though not quite at the preview’s stated catalyst level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 revenue less transaction costs is guided to approximately 4.16%, above the 3.5%-4% midterm range, supported by favorable debt capital markets funding costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 was 4.31%, above the 3–4% long-term range”; “RLTC % of GMV ≥4.2% and any reset of the 3–4% long-term range.”

surprises.description: Pay in X volume grew 41% year over year, with management saying a large low-average-order-value merchant is making it an evergreen part of its financing program. The preview did not identify this product or merchant dynamic as a key expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pay in X (Pay-in-4) volume grew 41% year-over-year, driven partly by a large low-average-order-value merchant making it an evergreen part of its financing program.”

surprises.description: Services vertical volume nearly doubled, driven by a couple of very large platform signings that management described as still being in the early innings. The preview discussed merchant wins generally but did not anticipate this scale of growth in services.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Services vertical volume nearly doubled year-over-year, driven by signing a couple of very large services platforms that management says are still in early innings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview mentioned “new merchant wins (Bed Bath & Beyond brands, Royal Caribbean)” but did not set an expectation for services volume.

surprises.description: Affirm Card attach reached 19% of active users, above the preview’s cited 17% Q3 level and its watch for attach to move beyond that level. The preview did not specify how far it would rise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Affirm Card attach rate stands at 19% of active users.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Affirm Card GMV: Q3: $2.13B, +146%; 4.4M users, 17% attach”; “Affirm Card attach beyond 17%.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that Affirm is available at only 80% of the top 250 merchants and roughly 10% of e-commerce merchants, leaving a larger stated merchant-coverage runway than the preview discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Affirm is available at only 80% of the top 250 merchants and roughly 10% of e-commerce merchants, indicating substantial greenfield growth opportunity remaining.”

surprises.description: Management said direct-to-consumer products are more than 80% interest-bearing and that the scaling Affirm Card is shifting the overall product mix back toward interest-bearing. That provides a potential counter to the preview’s concern about revenue-yield erosion, though no quantified yield impact was given.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Affirm's direct-to-consumer products run north of 80% interest-bearing loans, and the scaling of the Affirm Card is shifting overall product mix back toward interest-bearing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “–17bp of revenue yield” in Q3 and warned that “If the revenue-yield erosion accelerates, the unit-economics bull case wobbles.”

surprises.description: The call referred to a tax allowance release while emphasizing that the quarter was still the most profitable ever excluding it. The preview did not flag this one-off, so the reported quarter included an unanticipated tax-related benefit even though core profitability was also strong.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Most profitable quarter ever in fiscal Q4 2026, even excluding the tax allowance release.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue grew 16% as reported and beat the high end of guidance. That appears to clear the preview’s $2.03–$2.04 billion functional hurdle, though the call facts do not give an exact revenue figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 revenue grew 16% as reported (14% constant currency) and beat the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “the functional bar is roughly $2.03–2.04B revenue” and consensus was “$2.01B.”

surprises.description: Autodesk raised its underlying organic billings growth outlook from 8–9% to 9–10%, reaching 10–11% with MaintainX. That is stronger than a guidance increase explained only by adding MaintainX, a possibility the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the transaction model and currency, the underlying organic billings growth outlook was raised from 8-9% to 9-10%, reaching 10-11% including MaintainX's roughly 1-point contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “if management raises FY27 revenue by roughly the MaintainX contribution and trims EPS, that is an organic hold, not a raise.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY27 revenue and billings guidance and cited stronger second-half expectations as well as MaintainX. The preview warned that a raise could be only a mechanical rebase for the acquisition; the call’s stated stronger second-half expectations suggest more than that, although the facts do not quantify the organic revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Autodesk raised its full-year FY27 revenue guidance to $8.295-$8.345 billion and billings guidance to $8.575-$8.65 billion, reflecting Q2 outperformance, stronger second-half expectations, and the MaintainX acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 guidance must be re-based to include MaintainX for the first time” and “if management raises FY27 revenue by roughly the MaintainX contribution … that is an organic hold, not a raise.”

surprises.description: Management emphasized a meaningful second-half execution risk: the largest EBA renewal cohort is concentrated in Q4, alongside slower new-business normalization in Western Europe. The preview had already identified Q4 EBA and any extension of the normalization timeline as key risks, so this reinforces the downside concern rather than resolving it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “management flagged its largest EBA renewal cohort concentrated in Q4 as a key second-half risk, especially amid slower new-business normalization in Western Europe.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any language extending that normalization timeline, or hedging on the Q4 EBA cohort (the largest of the year), is a material negative.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin reached 41%, while the preview cited a 39% full-year margin guide and the prior-year Q2 margin of 39%. The quarter’s margin strength was supported by operating leverage, sales optimization, and lower stock-based compensation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP operating margin was 29% (up ~4 points) and non-GAAP operating margin was 41% (up ~2 points), driven by operating leverage, sales optimization, and lower stock-based compensation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op margin ~39% (FY guide)” and Q2 FY26 actual “39%.”

surprises.description: MaintainX is expected to bring about $45 million in transaction expenses, an additional cost not quantified in the preview’s discussion of expected acquisition dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MaintainX acquisition … is expected to add approximately $60 million to second-half revenue and $70 million to second-half billings, plus about $45 million in transaction expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “expect a revenue add of roughly $60–85M … and EPS dilution from both operating losses and interest expense.”

surprises.description: Autodesk reported $561 million of Q2 free cash flow and plans to direct about 50% of free cash flow to buybacks, including 2.1 million shares repurchased for $453 million. That is a firmer capital-return commitment than the preview’s concern that buybacks might slow after the acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was $561 million”; “Autodesk repurchased 2.1 million shares for $453 million and plans to apply about 50% of free cash flow to buybacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “After $3.6B of cash out the door plus new debt, watch for a slower buyback.”

surprises.description: The full-year free-cash-flow range was narrowed from $2.725–$2.800 billion to $2.725–$2.750 billion. The floor was unchanged, but the ceiling and midpoint came down modestly versus the preview’s cited guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “full-year FCF guidance was narrowed to $2.725-$2.75 billion.”

surprises.description: Autodesk will stop disclosing Design and Make revenue and move Media & Entertainment into an “other” bucket. The preview provided product-family estimates and did not flag this reduction in reporting detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Autodesk will stop disclosing Design and Make revenue and move M&E into an 'other' bucket.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview provided Q2 estimates for AECO, AutoCAD / AutoCAD LT, Manufacturing, Media & Entertainment, and Other.

surprises.description: The call highlighted Construction growth above 20%, attributing it to low technology penetration and diversification rather than construction-market cyclicality. The preview focused on AECO holding mid-teens growth and did not identify this Construction-specific growth and demand explanation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Construction business continues to grow north of 20%, driven by low technology penetration and diversification across geographies and segments rather than construction market cyclicality.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AECO … needs to hold mid-teens” and “AECO trajectory (~$1.01B expected, +15%).”

in_line: MaintainX was expected to contribute roughly $60–85 million of revenue in the second half; the call cited approximately $60 million.
The preview expected MaintainX to dilute earnings because of operating losses and financing costs; the call described it as an unprofitable, high-growth business and a drag on FY27 operating margin.
The FY27 non-GAAP operating margin guide remained 39%, and management reaffirmed the 41% FY29 target, as the preview expected the margin framework to be reaffirmed after the acquisition.
The preview identified the Q4 EBA cohort as a key risk; the call likewise flagged that cohort, though it also emphasized slower new-business normalization in Western Europe.

surprises.description: Elastic was expected to report about $469.5M of revenue, exactly around its guidance midpoint; it reported $478M, roughly $8.5M above consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 total revenue was $478 million, up 15% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Consensus $469.49M | Company Guidance $469–470M.”

surprises.description: Sales-led subscription revenue was expected to be about $392M, but came in at $399M; its 18% growth also exceeded the preview’s expected 15.9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sales-led subscription revenue grew 18% to $399 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sales-led subscription | ~$392M | $392–393M | +15.9%.”

surprises.description: CRPO growth was expected to be a key risk, with 15–16% described as the bear case and sustaining 18–20% as the bull case. Instead, CRPO grew 21%, above even that bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CRPO grew 21% to $1.2 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sustaining ≥18–20% is the bull case; a print of 15–16% is the bear case.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating margin was guided at about 14% for Q1, but the reported 16.2% exceeded that level by 2.2 percentage points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin was 16.2%, exceeding guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin | ~14% | ~14.0%.”

surprises.description: The net expansion rate slipped to 111% from 112%. The preview described 112% as the Q4 level and a slip to 110–111% as a downside signal, rather than the 113%+ improvement it identified as a bullish outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net expansion rate declined slightly to 111% from 112%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A tick to 113%+ would be a real signal; a slip to 110–111% undercuts the AI-expansion thesis.”

surprises.description: Elastic added more than 80 customers to its $100,000+ ACV tier, versus the roughly 60-per-quarter pace highlighted in the preview, and called it the largest sequential increase ever.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adding over 80 net new customers to this tier—its largest sequential increase ever.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$100K+ ACV customers were 1,720+ in Q4 … — roughly +60/quarter.”

surprises.description: The preview cited 600+ large customers using AI; the reported count was more than 670, with 70 net additions in Q1, exceeding that indicated level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 37% of $100,000+ ACV customers now use Elastic for AI (more than 670 customers) … with 70 net additions in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management disclosed 600+ customers with $100K+ ACV using AI capabilities.”

surprises.description: The full-year operating-margin guide rose to about 19.4%, above the preview’s expected roughly 19.0% and its concern that the margin ramp might be trimmed because of Deductive AI.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance to … non-GAAP operating margin of ~19.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance … non-GAAP op margin ~19.0%”; the preview also flagged concern about “margin trimmed for Deductive AI.”

surprises.description: The call reported RPO growth of 27% and $1.9B of RPO, offering a strong multiyear-commitment datapoint that the preview did not quantify or flag as a specific metric to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPO grew 27% to $1.9 billion, signaling multiyear customer commitments.”

surprises.description: Elastic launched a columnar index mode that it said reduces metrics-storage costs by about 20%, a product and cost-efficiency development not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Launched columnar index mode reducing metrics storage costs ~20% to approximately 3 bytes per sample.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that Elastic returned about $40M through share repurchases in Q1; the preview did not discuss capital returns or set an expectation for buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Returned ~$40 million to shareholders via 800,000 shares repurchased in Q1 ($380 million cumulative under the $500 million program).”

in_line: The FY2027 revenue guide was raised to $1.998–$2.010B, broadly in line with the preview’s base case of about $2.00–$2.01B, though below its more ambitious ≥$2.02B bull/catalyst threshold.
Deductive AI had closed after quarter-end and was expected to contribute nothing to Q1; the reported quarter did not suggest otherwise.

surprises.description: The preview estimated Q4 AI Cloud revenue of about $45–55 million; IREN reported $70.5 million, well above that range and above the preview’s $50 million catalyst threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue was $137.2 million (including $70.5 million AI Cloud revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AI Cloud Services ... Q4 FY26 ... ~$45–55M (my est.)”; “AI Cloud revenue ≥$50M.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated Q4 mining revenue of roughly $90–100 million. With total revenue of $137.2 million and AI Cloud revenue of $70.5 million, mining revenue was about $66.7 million, reflecting a sharper near-term decline than expected as hardware was decommissioned ahead of GPU installs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue was $137.2 million (including $70.5 million AI Cloud revenue), down $7.6 million sequentially as mining hardware was decommissioned ahead of GPU installs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bitcoin mining ... Q4 FY26 ... ~$90–100M (my est.).”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated a large GAAP loss driven by D&A and possible Bitcoin marks, but the reported loss was dominated by large noncash write-downs on decommissioned mining hardware and hardware held for sale—an impairment source and amount not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 net loss of $684 million, largely driven by $450.4 million of noncash impairments on decommissioned mining hardware plus a $102.1 million fair value decrease on mining hardware held for sale.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “large GAAP loss on D&A + BTC marks.”

surprises.description: The preview discussed the existing $3.6 billion GPU-backed loan and customer prepayments, but the call disclosed a much broader financing package: $6.5 billion of GPU financing secured over three months, including $2.8 billion for non-investment-grade deployments, alongside a target for another roughly $8 billion. This expands funding access, though some of the financing is costly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IREN secured $6.5 billion of GPU financing over three months,” including “$2.8 billion for non-investment-grade deployments (including $2.4 billion at 9% fixed for Mackenzie)”; it “targets an additional ~$8 billion of GPU financing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “a $3.6bn GPU-backed term loan at <6%”; “customer prepayments (~45% of associated GPU capex)”; “Any new equity or converts announced alongside the print is a negative catalyst.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the large 2027 build and funding needs but gave no CapEx forecast of this scale. IREN guided FY27 CapEx of approximately $25–30 billion and said data-center and GPU CapEx would rise 15%–20% for ongoing and new deployments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company guided FY27 CapEx of approximately $25 billion to $30 billion, with data center and GPU CapEx expected to rise 15%-20% for ongoing and new deployments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “the P&L gets worse as ARR compounds,” and the preview discusses the “1.2GW 2027 build,” but it does not provide an FY27 CapEx expectation.

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate the reported rise in contracted customer pricing: three-year pricing had increased about 125% since November, and recent three-year deals exceeded $20 million per megawatt, with discussions near $25 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “3-year contract pricing has risen about 125% since November while 5-year pricing is up about 70%, with recent 3-year deals exceeding $20 million per megawatt and active discussions near $25 million per megawatt.”

surprises.description: The preview centered on the more than $4 billion ARR target, but did not quantify how little of IREN’s secured grid portfolio that target uses. The call said the contracted ARR represents less than 10% of its 5+ gigawatt of secured grid connections, indicating substantially more capacity remains available to monetize.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The $4 billion of contracted ARR is derived from less than 10% of the company's 5+ gigawatt portfolio of secured grid connections, implying substantial untapped monetization potential.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “the >$4bn exit-2026 ARR target and the 480MW delivery schedule” are what the stock trades on.

surprises.description: The preview anticipated mining decline and watched the conversion cadence, but the call gave a firm endpoint: mining operations are expected to be effectively decommissioned by the end of December 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mining operations are expected to be effectively decommissioned by end of December 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bitcoin mining wind-down cadence” was a key metric to watch; the preview described “Bitcoin mining decay” and asked how much ASIC capacity converts to GPUs.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a sharp near-term cash overhead increase. IREN said Q1 cash SG&A would rise approximately $40–50 million sequentially as it invests ahead of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 cash SG&A is expected to increase approximately $40-50 million sequentially due to growth investments ahead of revenue.”

in_line: Total Q4 revenue was $137.2 million, within the preview’s $132.3–$142.3 million consensus range and close to its roughly $137 million midpoint.

The more-than-$4 billion ARR target for the end of 2026 was maintained; the preview identified reaffirmation of “>$4bn” as the central expectation. The call also said the contracted ARR would exceed $4 billion by the end of the December quarter.

surprises.description: Gap brand comps rose 10%, above the preview’s estimate of 6%–8%. The brand also extended its positive-comp run to 11 quarters, while the preview described the streak as at risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gap brand delivered comparable sales growth of 10%” and marked its “11th consecutive quarter of positive comps.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Gap comps at “+6% to +8%” and said the “Comp streak (9 qtrs positive) [was] at risk.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin increased 20 basis points to 41.4%, above the preview’s 40.7%–41.2% estimate and better than its company-guide range of flat to down 50 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin rose 20 basis points to 41.4% with merchandise margin up 80 basis points,” while 30 basis points of tariff benefit was largely offset by higher fuel costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put gross margin at “~40.7–41.2%” and cited company guidance of “Flat to –50 bps y/y.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance rose to $2.35–$2.45, above the preview’s expected $2.30–$2.40 range; the company also raised adjusted operating-margin guidance to 7.4%–7.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $2.35-$2.45 (up 10%-15%)” and “raised adjusted operating margin guidance to 7.4%-7.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was to “reaffirm $2.30–$2.40” for FY26 adjusted EPS.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.52, modestly above the $0.50 consensus cited in the preview, even though it declined from $0.57 a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS fell to $0.52 from $0.57 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted diluted EPS consensus was “$0.50 (Zacks); $0.48 (StockStory).”

surprises.description: The company narrowed its full-year sales-growth outlook to 1%–1.5%, below the preview’s expected 1%–2% range at the upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company narrowed full-year net sales growth guidance to 1%-1.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected to “reaffirm … +1–2% sales.”

surprises.description: Management gave a positive near-term update: Q3 sales are expected to grow 1.5%–2.5%, gross margin to expand 25–75 basis points, and Old Navy was showing meaningful sequential improvement in August. The preview highlighted Old Navy weakness and tariff uncertainty but did not provide a Q3 outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales up 1.5%-2.5% with gross margin up 25-75 basis points,” and “Old Navy is showing meaningful sequential improvement in August.”

surprises.description: Old Navy is getting a new brand president and CEO effective November 2, a leadership transition not raised in the preview. The shareholder implications are not established by the provided information.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Old Navy will undergo a leadership transition, with Michael Francis becoming Brand President and CEO effective November 2, succeeding Io Barbado.”

in_line: Q2 net sales were about $3.7 billion, matching the preview’s ~$3.70 billion consensus estimate.
Old Navy comps declined 4%, within the preview’s estimated down 2% to down 4% range and consistent with its expectation of a low-single-digit decline.
Athleta comps declined 12%, within the preview’s estimated down 9% to down 12% range; the preview also expected Q2 to be similar to Q1.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $102 million, about $6 million above the preview’s roughly $96 million estimate; the year-over-year decline was also smaller than the preview’s expected 13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 revenue was $102 million,” up 14% sequentially and down from $110.5 million a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 FY26 (my base est.)” revenue: “~$96M” and “-13% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: Instead of roughly breakeven, KTCC reported a $34.3 million Q4 net loss, or $3.16 per share. The loss included a $28.4 million non-cash deferred-tax valuation allowance and an $8.4 million distressed-customer receivables write-off.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 net loss was $34.3 million ($3.16 per share), including a $28.4 million non-cash valuation allowance against deferred tax assets and an $8.4 million write-off of distressed customer receivables.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~breakeven” net income and “~$0.00 to $0.02” EPS; it also highlighted management’s prior statement that the company expected to be “in the black bottom line” in Q4.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached only 8.3%, missing the preview’s roughly 9.0% estimate and its 9.0% proof-point threshold, although reported gross margin improved year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gross margin improved to 7.8% (adjusted 8.3%) from 6.2% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~9.0% adj.” gross margin and said to watch for “Adjusted gross margin ≥9.0%.”

surprises.description: KTCC won over $60 million in new programs, including a data-center program worth $40–45 million per year. The preview anticipated new program wins but highlighted earlier wins totaling $16.5–20.5 million annualized, so the scale of these new awards was substantially greater than the preview’s cited pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured over $60 million in new program awards during Q4,” including “a $40-45 million/year data center program in Mexico.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “new program wins announced with the print” were worth watching and cited four Q3-announced wins of “$16.5–20.5M annualized.”

surprises.description: Supply-chain financing constraints delayed about $10 million of Q4 shipments. The company said the shipments should move to future quarters rather than be lost, but the financing-driven disruption was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Supply chain financing constraints forced the company to delay approximately $10 million of shipments in Q4, which will shift to future quarters rather than being lost revenue.”

surprises.description: Management said it was liquidity-constrained and was evaluating additional capital sources, including customer capital-sharing and use of unencumbered foreign assets. The preview flagged debt and liquidity as risks, but this explicit need to pursue additional financing makes the concern more immediate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is liquidity-constrained and evaluating additional capital sources, including customer capital-sharing partnerships and leveraging unencumbered foreign assets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Debt reduction and liquidity” as a key metric to watch, citing $99.3 million of debt and $0.4 million of cash, and called liquidity “the tail risk that isn’t in the stock.”

surprises.description: The preview expected FY2027 framing and anticipated growth to be affirmed, but management declined to provide Q1 FY2027 guidance. That leaves near-term visibility less clear than the preview’s expected discussion suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management was “declining to provide Q1 FY2027 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY2027 revenue framing on the call” as a key metric and described its base case as “FY27 growth affirmed, back-half weighted.”

surprises.description: Vietnam-based revenue more than doubled sequentially, a stronger contribution than the preview’s discussion of doubled capacity and a roughly 50% U.S./Vietnam manufacturing mix had indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vietnam-based revenue more than doubled sequentially in Q4,” driven by medical-device and consumer-products programs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Vietnam capacity doubled” and that the “US/Vietnam mix” was about 50% of manufacturing, but did not anticipate a more-than-doubling of Vietnam revenue.

surprises.description: Full-year revenue was slightly above the preview’s model, though it still fell sharply year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY2026 revenue fell to $386.7 million from $467.9 million in FY2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated FY2026 revenue of “~$381M” and a 19% year-over-year decline.

surprises.description: The reported Mexico headcount reduction was about 40% over 27 months, compared with the preview’s description of a 42% reduction over 24 months, suggesting a somewhat smaller and slower cut than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced Mexico headcount by approximately 40% over 27 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Mexico headcount is down 42% over 24 months.”

in_line: The China wind-down savings were broadly in line with the preview’s expectation: the preview cited about $1.2 million per quarter, while the call described approximately $4 million in annualized FY2027 savings.
The call’s statement that U.S. and Vietnam facilities account for about half of manufacturing activity was consistent with the preview’s roughly 50% U.S./Vietnam mix.

surprises.description: Q2 total revenue was $427.3 million versus the $396.4 million consensus, about 7.8% above expectation; subscription revenue also exceeded its $382.2 million consensus, reaching $407.2 million. The revenue beat was substantially larger than the preview’s expectation that the quarter would clear company guidance of $395–397 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription revenue grew 37% year-over-year to $407.2 million, while total revenue rose 38% to $427.3 million (up 43% normalized for material rights).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2 FY27 Consensus $396.4M”; “Subscription revenue | $382.2M”; “Q2 will almost certainly clear the $395–397M guide.”

surprises.description: Subscription ARR reached $1.66 billion, above the $1,639.4 million consensus, while net new ARR of about $96 million exceeded the preview’s implied roughly $70 million and its $80–90 million whisper range. The preview identified $90 million or more in net adds as the bull case; management also said net adds accelerated year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription ARR reached $1.66 billion in Q2 FY27”; “Net new subscription ARR was approximately $96 million, growing 35% year-over-year, which management characterized as an acceleration from prior quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Subscription ARR | $1,639.4M”; “consensus is effectively modeling zero growth in net adds”; “Whisper is $80–90M”; “$90M+ is the bull case.”

surprises.description: FY27 subscription ARR guidance rose to $1.88–1.885 billion, above the preview’s base case of roughly $1.87–1.88 billion and at or just above its $1.88 billion catalyst threshold. The raise was meaningful but fell short of the preview’s $1.90 billion-plus bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 subscription ARR guidance was raised to $1.88–$1.885 billion (~29% growth), with the raise adding $24–$25 million and lifting implied net new ARR growth from 7% to 14%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case is a raise to ~$1.87–1.88B; the bull case needs $1.90B+”; “FY27 subscription ARR guide ≥ $1.88B.”

surprises.description: The FY27 revenue outlook increased to $1.685–1.693 billion from $1.638–1.648 billion, a materially larger outlook than the preview’s starting guide. The company still cited a material-rights revenue headwind of about $18 million, close to the preview’s roughly $17 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance calls for total revenue of $1.685–$1.693 billion”; “material rights being a ~$18 million revenue headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance to be updated: revenue $1.638–1.648B”; “maintenance-to-cloud migration material rights benefit is rolling off (~$17M for FY27).”

surprises.description: FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $0.47–$0.53 was well above the preview’s existing $0.25–$0.35 range, a much stronger outlook than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance calls for … non-GAAP EPS of $0.47–$0.53.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance to be updated: … non-GAAP EPS $0.25–0.35.”

surprises.description: FY27 free cash flow guidance rose to $323–$333 million from $293–$303 million, exceeding the preview’s expectation that the guide would be raised above $303 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance calls for … free cash flow of $323–$333 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FCF $293–303M”; “FCF guide raised above $303M.”

surprises.description: FY27 subscription ARR contribution-margin guidance is about 15.5%, above the preview’s expected roughly 14% full-year target. The reported LTM margin was already 14%, although that is not directly comparable to the preview’s 11–12% Q2 guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription ARR contribution margin improved 460 basis points year-over-year to 14% (LTM)”; FY27 guidance calls for “~15.5% subscription ARR contribution margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sub. ARR contribution margin … FY27: ~14%”; “confirm this is deliberate and that the ~14% FY27 target … [is] raised, not just held.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for quantified Identity Resilience and Agent Cloud ARR, with a combined figure tracking toward $100 million as a positive validation. Instead, the call reported more than 15 paying Agent Cloud customers but minimal ARR assumed this year, and provided no combined new-product ARR figure—less evidence of near-term revenue contribution than the preview’s hoped-for outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rubrik Agent Cloud now has over 15 paying customers with minimal ARR assumed this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If management quantifies a combined new-product ARR number and it's tracking toward $100M, the ‘multi-product platform’ thesis gets validated”; “Quantified Identity Resilience + Agent Cloud ARR … A disclosed, accelerating combined figure” was the catalyst.

surprises.description: The call disclosed that non-cloud ARR is now growing at about 10%, driven by sovereign and regulated-industry demand, and that it carries higher margins than cloud. The preview focused on cloud ARR mix and did not anticipate this additional growth and margin contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-cloud ARR is now growing (~10% expected) driven by sovereign and regulated-industry demand and carries higher margins than cloud.”

surprises.description: The company reported 3,084 customers with at least $100,000 in subscription ARR, modestly above the preview’s consensus of 3,074. The difference was small, and the reported 23% growth was essentially in line with the preview’s 22.7% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers with $100,000+ in subscription ARR grew 23% to 3,084.”

in_line: Subscription net retention remained above 119%, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of approximately 120% and not the roughly 118% level it flagged as a red flag.
The roughly $18 million FY27 material-rights revenue headwind was close to the preview’s estimate of about $17 million.

surprises.description: PagerDuty’s ARR reached $501 million, crossing $500 million for the first time and rising $2 million year over year. That clears the preview’s stated $500 million inflection threshold, although it is a little below the preview’s roughly $502 million bull-case level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annual recurring revenue crossed the $500 million milestone for the first time, ending at $501 million, a $6 million sequential increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything ≥$500M with positive YoY growth is a genuine inflection signal”; the bull scenario called for “ARR returns to YoY growth (~$502M+).”

surprises.description: PagerDuty raised its FY27 non-GAAP operating margin outlook by a percentage point at both ends, to 25%–26% from 24%–25%. The preview expected the prior 24%–25% range, so this is a meaningful improvement beyond the margin-only EPS upside it described as a base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 non-GAAP operating margin guidance was raised to 25%-26% from the prior 24%-25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op margin (FY guide 24–25%)”; the base case described “FY27 EPS nudged up on margin only.”

surprises.description: The company’s full-year free cash flow margin outlook was better than the preview’s expectation of a 2–4 percentage-point decline from FY26: management instead raised guidance to be in line with FY26.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was $33 million (26% margin), and full-year free cash flow margin guidance was raised to be in line with FY26 rather than 2-4 points lower as previously expected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow margin guidance was raised to be in line with FY26 rather than 2-4 points lower as previously expected.”

surprises.description: PagerDuty cut approximately 15% of its workforce during the quarter, with restructuring charges of $5.5 million to $7.5 million. The preview flagged restructuring as something to watch from new management, but did not say a workforce reduction of this scale was expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a workforce restructuring impacting approximately 15% of employees, concentrated in noncustomer-facing roles, with restructuring charges of $5.5 million to $7.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for any strategic reframing, restructuring, portfolio review, or change in guidance philosophy.”

surprises.description: Total RPO was $426 million, down from the $441 million Q1 figure and only $1 million higher year over year. That is a weak forward-bookings signal against the preview’s emphasis on RPO as a key forward-looking metric, though the preview did not give a Q2 RPO forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total RPO was $426 million (only $1 million higher year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “RPO. $441M in Q1 with 72% current. A forward-looking read on bookings that the ARR number smooths over.”

surprises.description: PagerDuty said its Ops Cloud/PD Reliability Platform business grew at a double-digit rate and that the platform would reach general availability this fall with usage-based pricing. The preview discussed usage-based adoption as a key mechanism for recovery, but did not anticipate this specific launch timing and pricing announcement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Ops Cloud/PD Reliability Platform business grew double digits and will move to general availability this fall with usage-based pricing.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $124.4 million narrowly exceeded the $124.0 million high end of guidance and consensus around $123.2 million, but was broadly in line with the preview’s functional whisper of a print at or above $124 million.

Dollar-based net retention improved to 98%, the level the preview identified as the clearest proof point for recovery and within its 97%–98% base-case range; annualized gross retention also improved for a second consecutive quarter.
Q3 revenue guidance implies roughly flat year-over-year growth, consistent with the preview’s flat-growth outlook.
The $100,000-plus customer cohort reached 884, adding 24 accounts since Q1, consistent with the preview’s test of whether enterprise customer additions would accelerate.

surprises.description: Net new ARR was $56 million, up only 4% year over year, well below the preview’s $72–82 million implied range and its roughly $75 million whisper. The record Q2 amount still fell short of the growth the preview said investors would look for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “record second-quarter net new ARR of $56 million (up 4% YoY)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net new ARR (not guided) ~$72–82M implied”; “If S can't show NNARR ≥$75M”; “Net new ARR vs. ~$75M whisper”

surprises.description: RPO grew 45% to a record $1.7 billion, a clear acceleration from the preview’s cited 30% growth and $1.5 billion level. Larger deals and longer contract durations contributed to the increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPO accelerated to 45% growth, reaching a record $1.7 billion, up from $1.5 billion last quarter, driven by larger lands and longer contract durations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “RPO was +30% to $1.5B.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating margin reached 10%, above the preview’s roughly 8.3% expectation, while EPS of $0.08 beat the $0.07 consensus. Both profitability measures came in stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating margin reached a record 10%, an 820 basis point YoY expansion, while EPS of $0.08 doubled year-over-year and beat expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.07”; “Non-GAAP operating income ~$24M (~8.3% margin).”

surprises.description: The $100,000-plus ARR customer count grew 13%, slower than the preview’s estimated 16–18% growth and down from 17% last quarter. Management said the company is landing larger deals with fewer new logos.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$100K+ customer count growth decelerated to 13% from 17% last quarter as the company lands larger deals with fewer new logos.”

surprises.description: Sales and marketing expense fell to 34% of revenue, an improvement of more than 900 basis points year over year. The preview expected restructuring savings to start flowing through, but the reported reduction shows a substantial improvement in go-to-market efficiency.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sales and marketing expense fell to 34% of revenue, a 900+ basis point YoY improvement, signaling significantly improved go-to-market efficiency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The May 8% RIF (~$25M cost, ~$15M cash) should start showing in Q2 opex”; “Watch for any hint the cuts hit sales capacity or pipeline coverage.”

surprises.description: SentinelOne raised its full-year operating income outlook to $124–128 million, above the preview’s $115–125 million estimate. The upper end is $3 million above that estimate’s upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “raised its full-year FY27 ... operating income outlook to $124-$128 million (~10% margin, up ~700 bps over FY26).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 non-GAAP op income / EPS $115–125M / $0.32–0.38”; “~10% margin.”

surprises.description: Management said AI-security ARR, from Prompt Security and Purple AI, tripled year over year and is expected to become the company’s next nine-figure ARR category. The preview discussed strong AI-security growth but did not anticipate that specific scale outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ARR from AI security offerings (Prompt Security and Purple AI) tripled year-over-year and is expected to become the company's next 9-figure ARR category.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AI security ARR nearly doubling sequentially off a small base”; the preview also called for “Quantified AI-security / non-endpoint ARR.”

surprises.description: SentinelOne Flex had already exceeded 10% of total ARR within a year of launch, a scale milestone the preview did not flag as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SentinelOne Flex exceeded 10% of total ARR within a year of launch.”

surprises.description: Q3 operating margin guidance was about 13%, above the roughly 10% full-year margin outlook, and management indicated the full-year outlook implies a notably higher Q4 exit rate. This points to a stronger near-term margin trajectory than the preview quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 operating margin of ~13%, with the full-year implying a notably higher Q4 exit rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 non-GAAP op income ... ~$115–125M”; “~10% margin.”

surprises.description: Net revenue retention among customers spending $100,000 or more in ARR expanded both sequentially and year over year. The preview said a qualitative update would matter but did not set an expectation for expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue retention for customers spending $100,000+ in ARR expanded both sequentially (third consecutive quarter) and year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any qualitative update matters given the endpoint-competition narrative.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $292 million was close to the preview’s $291–293 million base case and its $292–294 million buy-side whisper, despite topping the formal $290 million consensus and the company’s $289–291 million guide.
Total ARR growth of 22% matched the preview’s expected 22–23% growth.

The FY27 revenue outlook of $1.202–1.207 billion was around the preview’s expected high-end range of $1.205–1.21 billion; it was a modest raise rather than the preview’s stronger bull-case threshold of at least $1.21 billion.

surprises.description: Frontline’s adjusted EPS was $2.61, below the preview’s primary $2.66 consensus estimate and further below its $3.00 base-case estimate. The miss was small against primary consensus but more noticeable against the preview’s model.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted profit of $580.2 million ($2.61/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $2.66”; the preview’s base case was “Adjusted EPS ~$3.00.”

surprises.description: Q2 TCE rates came in below the preview’s expected levels across all three vessel groups, including below the disclosed booking benchmarks. The largest gap was LR2/Aframax at $92,400/day versus the preview’s $105,000/day base estimate and $125,000/day booked figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 TCE rates reached $152,700/day for VLCCs, $117,400/day (booked) for Suezmax and $92,400/day for LR2/Aframax.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed booked rates of “$181,700” for VLCCs, “$131,300” for Suezmax and “$125,000” for LR2/Aframax, and base-case estimates of “$165,000,” “$122,000” and “$105,000,” respectively.

surprises.description: Q3 VLCC bookings covered 86% of days, far more than the preview’s roughly 50% base-case assumption. The booked rate of $156,900/day was within the preview’s expected $150,000–$175,000 base-case range, so the surprise was the much higher coverage rather than the rate level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “86% of Q3 VLCC days already booked at $156,900/day.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “$150–175k on ~50%”; it also said a print above $175,000 on 50%+ of days would be bullish.

surprises.description: Frontline reduced its weighted-average interest-rate margin by about 52 basis points, a financing improvement the preview did not identify as an expected development. This is a favorable cost-of-debt change, though the call facts do not quantify its earnings impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reduced its weighted average interest rate margin by approximately 52 basis points, from 178bps to 126bps.”
