surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided that third quarter results are expected to be profitable and better than the same period last year, supported by record ethanol export demand.”

surprises.description: The expansion remains on schedule for end-2026 completion, but REX’s target of reaching production near 200 million gallons is early-to-mid next year. That points to full-volume production after the preview’s expectation of full operation in late FY2026, even though the construction completion date remains on track.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The One Earth ethanol expansion remains on schedule for completion by end of 2026, targeting production near 200 million gallons by early-to-mid next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview assumed “full operation” in “late FY2026” and described the project as “fully operational during fiscal 2026.”

in_line: Revenue was $168.5 million: below the preview’s $194.8 million vendor consensus, but within its own $162–$170 million estimate range. The preview had already characterized the consensus revenue bar as stale and too high.
The One Earth expansion’s end-2026 completion schedule remained on track, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Tilly’s reported Q2 sales of $163.5 million and comps up 12.1%, above the company’s $154–160 million sales guide and 6–10% comp range. Sales also exceeded the roughly $157 million consensus, and comps beat the top of the guide by 2.1 percentage points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total net sales rose 8.1% to $163.5 million, with comparable net sales up 12.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview: “Net sales” guide of “$154M – $160M,” with comparable net sales “+6% to +10%”; sell-side consensus “~$157.0M.”

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS was $0.27, above the preview’s company-guidance range of $0.13–$0.20 and its cited consensus range of $0.14–$0.17. Net income of $8.4 million also exceeded the preview’s $3.8–$6.0 million guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net income was $8.4 million ($0.27 per diluted share), up $5.2 million from $3.2 million ($0.10) a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview: net income guide “$3.8M – $6.0M” and diluted EPS guide “$0.13 – $0.20”; consensus EPS “~$0.14 – $0.17.”

surprises.description: Gross margin rose to 35.5%, well above the preview’s expectation of flat to slightly higher than the prior-year 32.5% level. The 300-basis-point gain also surpassed the preview’s estimate that roughly 33.5% would be the threshold for demonstrating durable margin improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved 300 basis points to 35.5%, driven by a 140-basis-point product margin gain and 160 basis points of buying/distribution/occupancy leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview: company guidance was “Flat to up slightly” versus 32.5% prior year; its watchpoint said “Anything above ~33.5%” would prove the margin story structural.

surprises.description: Fiscal August comps accelerated to 14.6%, materially stronger than the preview’s mid-single-digit-or-better framework for August and notable against the tougher comparisons it had flagged. That suggests momentum strengthened rather than merely holding around the prior May run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal August comps accelerated to 14.6%, extending the streak to 13 consecutive months of comparable sales growth despite tougher year-over-year comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview: the Q3 trend would be signaled by “mid-single-digit-or-better comps”; its base case assumed “May’s run-rate simply holds,” with +3–5% Q3 comps.

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook is substantially stronger than the preview’s framework: sales guidance of $150–155 million and comps up 10–14% are well above its $138–144 million sales and +3–6% comp bogeys. The preview had focused on whether the business could sustain mid-single-digit comps as it began lapping positive comparisons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales of $150-155 million (comps up 10-14%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview’s Q3 framework bogey: “net sales ~$138–144M” and “+3–6% comps”; it described a guide implying “mid-single-digit-or-better comps” as evidence the trend survived the lap.

surprises.description: Q3 is now guided to be profitable, with net income of $2.2–$3.7 million, rather than around breakeven to modestly profitable as the preview expected. The outlook also contrasts with the prior-year Q3 net loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for … net income of $2.2-3.7 million ($0.07-0.12 per share), versus a $1.4 million net loss last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview’s Q3 framework was “EPS around breakeven to +$0.05” versus $(0.05) last year.

surprises.description: Tilly’s returned to positive trailing-four-quarter earnings for the first time since fiscal 2022, instead of the trailing loss cited in the preview. Management is now targeting its first profitable fiscal year since 2022.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned to profitability on a trailing four-quarters basis (just under $2 million) for the first time since fiscal 2022, and is targeting its first profitable fiscal year since 2022.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview cited “TTM net loss of $3.25M” and said confirming positive cash generation mattered.

surprises.description: A $1.5 million Q2 bonus accrual appeared despite not being included in the model for four years, and management said it will continue to weigh on SG&A leverage. This is an unexpected cost headwind alongside the otherwise strong results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Improved performance triggered $1.5 million in bonus accruals in Q2, an expense absent from the model for four years that will continue to pressure SG&A leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview modeled Q2 SG&A at “$48M – $49M” and discussed expected leverage, but did not anticipate a bonus accrual; it noted “100–150bps of likely occupancy leverage.”

in_line: Liquidity was broadly in line with the preview: Tilly’s remained debt-free, with $62.2 million in cash and investments and $63.3 million of undrawn credit capacity, versus the preview’s expectation of $59–63 million cash/investments and about $63 million undrawn.

surprises.description: HPE reported non-GAAP EPS of $1.11, well above the preview’s $0.97–$1.00 whisper range and above the high end of its $0.88–$0.93 guidance. It was also the first quarter in which HPE exceeded $1 of EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached a record $1.11,” “the first time HPE surpassed $1 in a single quarter,” and was “well above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the functional bar is a whisper closer to $0.97–$1.00.”

surprises.description: HPE raised FY26 EPS guidance to $3.75–$3.85 and FCF guidance to at least $3.75 billion, substantially exceeding the preview’s expectation of an approximately $0.05 EPS increase and its existing FCF floor. The preview said an in-line reaffirmation would disappoint; HPE instead made a much larger update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HPE raised FY26 EPS guidance to $3.75–$3.85 and free cash flow to at least $3.75 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY26 EPS guidance of “$3.35–$3.45” and FCF of “≥$3.5B,” and said the buy-side wanted EPS raised “~$0.05 to $3.40–$3.50+.”

surprises.description: HPE lifted its FY27 framework well above the preview’s revenue-growth and FCF expectations: revenue growth is now 13–17% and FCF at least $5 billion. The new $4.40–$4.60 EPS range also implies stronger growth than the preview’s 12–16% EPS-growth framework when compared with the raised FY26 guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HPE” lifted its FY27 framework to “13–17% revenue growth, EPS of $4.40–$4.60, and free cash flow of at least $5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the FY27 framework as “revenue +8–12%, EPS +12–16%, FCF ≥$4.5B.”

surprises.description: AI systems orders reached $2.4 billion, comfortably above the preview’s $1.8 billion threshold for the quarter. Enterprise demand more than doubled, adding evidence of stronger demand than the preview’s minimum watchpoint implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI systems orders grew over 30% sequentially to $2.4 billion with enterprise demand more than doubling.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Need orders ≥$1.8B.”

surprises.description: AI systems backlog increased 14% sequentially to a new high, rather than merely holding roughly flat as the preview’s base case anticipated. This indicates HPE built backlog during the quarter instead of simply drawing it down to support revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI systems revenue was ~$1.6 billion and backlog rose 14% sequentially to a new high.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected backlog “roughly flat $5.5–6.2B” and said backlog should be “at least flat sequentially.”

surprises.description: Networking orders were much stronger than the preview’s focus on roughly 10% normalized revenue growth suggested: orders grew 36%, networks-for-AI orders hit a record, and HPE raised its full-year networks-for-AI target. This points to strong demand even though shipments were constrained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Networking orders grew 36%,” networks-for-AI orders hit “a record $700 million,” cumulative FY26 networks-for-AI orders reached “$2.2 billion,” and HPE raised its full-year target to “$2.5–$3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on “Networking normalized growth” versus “the ~10% normalized figure” and asked whether it accelerated; it gave no comparable order-growth or networks-for-AI target expectation.

surprises.description: Despite that order strength, networking revenue did not accelerate from the preview’s roughly 10% normalized-growth reference, and data center networking revenue declined. HPE attributed the gap to supply constraints and shipment timing, making conversion weaker than the order trends suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Networking revenue grew only 10% on a normalized basis due to supply constraints,” while “data center networking revenue actually declin[ed] 6% on shipment timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the key was whether normalized networking growth “accelerated” from “~10% normalized,” and flagged supply as the binding constraint.

surprises.description: HPE entered the quarter-end with net leverage already at 1.8x, below its 2x target and a year ahead of plan, rather than merely confirming a path to reach 2x by fiscal year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HPE exited Q3 with net leverage of 1.8x (below its 2x target and a year ahead of plan).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “confirmation of 2x net leverage by FYE” and described reaching that target by fiscal year-end as a year-early plan.

surprises.description: HPE announced an expanded, multi-year, multi-gigawatt Oracle collaboration to deploy Juniper networking equipment for AI cloud build-out. The preview did not identify this specific large deployment as an expected catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HPE announced an expanded multi-year, multi-gigawatt collaboration with Oracle to deploy Juniper routers and switches for AI cloud build-out.”

surprises.description: HPE also disclosed a post-quarter multibillion-dollar server deal with a hyperscaler for inferencing, an additional large commercial win not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call cited “a post-quarter multibillion-dollar server deal with a hyperscaler for inferencing.”

surprises.description: Management said the FY27 outlook excludes the AMD Helios opportunity, which it estimates could be a tens-of-billions-of-dollars market ramping in late 2026 and 2027. That is a substantial potential opportunity, but it is not included in the already-raised framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FY27 outlook explicitly excludes the AMD Helios opportunity,” which management estimates “could represent a tens-of-billions-of-dollars total market ramping in late calendar 2026 and 2027.”

surprises.description: HPE’s server revenue grew sharply, but management attributed the increase primarily to higher average selling prices while unit volumes remained supply-constrained. That leaves the preview’s question about durable traditional-server demand unresolved: the reported revenue growth was not primarily volume-driven.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Server revenue grew 35% to an all-time high driven primarily by higher ASPs amid supply-constrained unit volumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged whether traditional/general-purpose server demand was “durable or a pre-buy” as a key issue.

in_line: Revenue growth of 34% was within the preview’s expected year-over-year range of 32–35%, although the $12.2 billion result modestly exceeded the cited consensus estimates.
HPE’s plan to return at least 75% of free cash flow to shareholders in Q4 was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of concrete language on activating the 75% payout policy.

surprises.description: Revenue was $5.0 billion, below the preview’s $5.67 billion primary consensus and its roughly $5.8 billion base case, though above the alternate $4.26 billion estimate. Given the unusually wide estimate range, the result is a mixed surprise rather than a clear miss against every forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue nearly doubled year-over-year, rising 99% to $5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $5.67B”; alternate estimate: “$4.26B”; base scenario: “Revenue ~$5.8B.”

surprises.description: Q4 GAAP diluted EPS was $0.41, below the preview’s roughly $0.50–$0.55 GAAP base case; full-year EPS of $3.02 also came in below the preview’s implied $3.17. The preview cautioned that the Street’s $0.96 EPS figure was on a different, adjusted pre-tax basis, so it is not a direct comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 net income was $12.2 million or $0.41 per diluted share”; “full-year EPS surged to $3.02 from $0.71.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “GAAP EPS ~$0.50–0.55”; implied FY2026: “GAAP diluted EPS ~$2.65 + ~$0.52 = ~$3.17.”

surprises.description: Gross profit reached $110.3 million, above the preview’s roughly $107 million base case, and the 2.2% gross margin was also above its 1.85% base assumption. This was a positive result despite margin compression compared with the prior-year quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gross profit rose 35% to $110.3 million, but gross margin compressed to 2.2% of revenue from 3.25% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “Gross profit ~$107M (1.85%).”

surprises.description: Gold.com declared a $1.00-per-share special dividend in addition to its regular $0.20 quarterly dividend. The preview identified the special-dividend decision as unresolved and treated no decision as part of its base case, so the payout exceeded that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company declared a special dividend of $1.00 per share on top of its regular $0.20 quarterly dividend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “explicitly deferred the special-dividend decision until he saw Q4 results” and described the base case as “no capital-return decision.”

surprises.description: Management said the demand slowdown had continued into the first two months of Q1 FY2027, with geopolitical uncertainty causing customers to hold back. The preview discussed Q4 volume normalization and flagged July–August demand as a qualitative tell, but did not anticipate management confirming that weakness was continuing into the new quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A demand slowdown that began mid-March/early April and has continued through the first two months of Q1 fiscal 2027,” with customers “sit[ting] on their hands.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY2027 tell was “qualitative language about July–August demand (not addressed on the May call).”

surprises.description: Gold ounces sold were 521,000, almost unchanged from Q3’s 527,000, despite the preview expecting a sequential decline as volumes normalized. That was a modestly better sequential outcome than the preview’s setup suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gold ounces sold rose 51% year-over-year to 521,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Sequential decline is expected and priced; the question is depth,” and listed Q3 gold sales at 527,000 ounces.

surprises.description: The Tether partnership’s gold and silver lease and storage activity was running at multiples of the levels initially disclosed, a larger scale than the preview quantified. Management tempered the upside by saying the business is low-margin and will take a couple of quarters to fully benefit results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Tether partnership is generating gold and silver leases and storage business at multiples of the levels initially disclosed,” though it is “low-margin” and “benefits will take a couple of quarters to fully materialize.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described storage value doubling to “$2.2B by May” and flagged the Tether/XAUT roadmap and storage balance as items to watch, but did not anticipate activity at multiples of the initially disclosed levels.

surprises.description: Cash rose to $578 million, substantially above the $143.6 million balance cited in the preview, even with Sunshine Minting acquired in an all-cash deal. That represents a stronger liquidity position than the preview’s balance-sheet discussion suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The cash position surged to $578 million from $77.7 million a year earlier,” with liquidity also reflecting Tether-related activity.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview stated, “Cash was only $143.6M and Sunshine was an all-cash deal.”

in_line: Silver ounces sold fell to 15.3 million, close to the prior-year quarter’s 15.7 million. The preview expected Q4 sequential volume declines and a return toward more typical volumes, though it noted that the depth of silver’s decline was uncertain.

surprises.description: Q2 sales reached $1.3 billion, comps were +14%, and adjusted EPS was $1.68—well above the preview’s roughly $1.21–$1.22 billion sales, +8.7% consensus comp, and $1.32–$1.33 consensus EPS (even above its $1.45–$1.55 whisper EPS range).
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 23% year-over-year to $1.3 billion,” driven by “a 14% comparable sales increase”; “Adjusted diluted EPS more than doubled to $1.68.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview consensus: net sales “~$1.21–1.22B,” comparable sales “+8.7%,” adjusted diluted EPS “$1.32–$1.33”; functional buy-side bar “~$1.45–1.55 EPS.”

surprises.description: Profitability was stronger than the preview’s derived operating-margin estimate: adjusted operating margin reached about 9% versus the preview’s 7.5%–8.0% estimate. Gross margin also expanded 220 basis points despite higher fuel costs, whereas the preview highlighted tariff-related margin pressure as a key risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded approximately 220 basis points to 35.6%” despite “higher fuel costs”; adjusted operating margin was up “about 360 basis points to 9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview estimated operating margin at “~7.5–8.0%” and said “Any quantified tariff drag is the single most likely source of a guide-down surprise.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year outlook substantially above the preview’s expected range and bar: FY2026 sales are now $5.63–$5.71 billion and adjusted EPS is $10.07, versus preview expectations of $5.40–$5.48 billion and a roughly $9.00-plus EPS bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to sales of $5.63-$5.71 billion” and “adjusted EPS of $10.07.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview cited prior FY sales guidance of “$5.40–5.48B,” expected a “modest FY raise to ~$5.50–5.55B / ~$9.10–9.30,” and said the FY EPS guide faced a “~$9.00+ bar.”

surprises.description: Despite the strong full-year raise, the near-term comp outlook points to a sharper second-half slowdown than the preview’s “comping the comp” focus implied: Q3 comps are guided to 8%–10%, and the call implies only about a 3% Q4 comp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for… comps of 8-10%” and implies “a low-single-digit (~3%) Q4 comp.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Management must guide to ‘comping the comp’ against” prior-year Q3 and Q4 comps of “+14.3%” and “+15.4%,” and put the functional buy-side bar at a “+10–11% comp.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed $170 million of pretax IEEPA tariff refunds in its cash and investments, but excluded the refunds from guidance. The preview focused on tariff assumptions and potential drag but did not anticipate this refund balance.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “approximately $1.2 billion in cash and investments, including $170 million in pretax IEEPA tariff refunds excluded from guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for attention to “the tariff assumption reset” and “Tariff math post-July 24,” but did not mention refunds.

surprises.description: The board approved a new $600 million share-repurchase authorization, and the company had already repurchased $60 million of shares in Q2; the preview did not flag a new authorization or buybacks as an expected capital-allocation action.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The board approved a new $600 million share repurchase authorization with no expiration,” following “$60 million… repurchased in Q2.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year CapEx to $250–$260 million to remerchandise stores, including tearing down Five Beyond walls. The preview discussed store openings and productivity but did not anticipate this spending increase or the teardown program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year CapEx to $250-$260 million” to fund store remerchandising, “tearing down the Five Beyond wall at roughly $40,000-$45,000 per store.”

surprises.description: Management said squishy dumplings contributed only a low-single-digit amount directly to comps, offering evidence against the idea that the strong comp performance depended heavily on one fad product. The preview flagged the broader debate over whether gains were structural or “squish,” but did not identify this product or quantify its contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Squishy dumplings were only a low-single-digit direct comp contributor.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “Narrative: structural vs. squish” was being tested and asked whether “per-store productivity gains are framed as permanent.”

surprises.description: The company announced entry into Puerto Rico in late 2027, a new geographic expansion plan not mentioned in the preview’s discussion of store growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “plans to enter Puerto Rico in late 2027.”

in_line: Store openings were broadly in line with the preview: FIVE opened 52 net new stores versus the preview’s expectation of 50, and its 2,022 ending stores were close to the expected 2,020. The preview had also said the 2,000th store had just opened.

surprises.description: The preview expected free cash flow to improve as the company stepped down from Q4's $54.4 million loss, but the company reported positive free cash flow of $2.1 million, versus negative $54.8 million last quarter and negative $34.3 million a year ago.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated positive free cash flow of $2.1 million,” compared with negative $54.8 million last quarter and negative $34.3 million a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether “the –$54.4M Q4 burn actually step[s] down” and said guided burn was around –$40.5M to –$48.5M.

surprises.description: The preview expected a Q1 non-GAAP operating loss of roughly $44 million, within a guidance range whose midpoint was $44.5 million. The reported loss was $36.2 million—$8.3 million better than that midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating loss was $36.2 million, coming in $8.3 million better than the midpoint of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed non-GAAP loss from operations of “~–$44M” and company guidance of “–$40.5 to –$48.5M.”

surprises.description: The preview said there was “no bookings proof yet” and highlighted concern after a prior billings miss. Instead, bookings grew 73% year over year, with federal bookings up 138%, and the company closed 22 enterprise agreements, including major corporate and government customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bookings grew 73% year-over-year, while federal bookings grew 138% year-over-year”; the company also “closed 22 enterprise agreements,” including Johnson & Johnson, Ford Motor Company, the U.S. Department of Defense, and the Defense Logistics Agency.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “no bookings proof yet” and flagged bookings and pipeline proxies as key indicators after Q4 “missed billings estimates badly.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted Q4 non-GAAP gross margin of 37% and warned that failure to recover would lengthen the path to profitability. Margin rose to 50% sequentially, although management expects it to moderate to the mid-40s next quarter as engineering investment increases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin improved sequentially from 37% to 50%,” with expected moderation to “mid-40s next quarter due to engineering investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Non-GAAP GM collapsed to 37% in Q4” and warned, “If margin doesn't recover with the cost actions” the path to profitability would get longer.

surprises.description: The preview implied that the FY27 midpoint required an average of about $57.7 million per quarter across Q2–Q4. Q2 guidance is $51 million to $55 million, so achieving the unchanged full-year midpoint now requires a stronger average in Q3 and Q4 than that earlier implied pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue guidance is $51 million to $55 million,” while FY2027 revenue guidance remains $210 million to $240 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: At the FY27 midpoint, the preview calculated an implied Q2–Q4 average of “$57.7M” per quarter.

surprises.description: Subscription revenue was modestly above consensus and increased sequentially, whereas the preview described consensus as essentially flat against Q4. The sequential gain was positive, but small.
surprises.fact_evidence: Subscription revenue was “$49.2 million,” representing 94% of total revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed subscription revenue consensus of “$48.3M” versus Q4 revenue of “$48.4M,” and called consensus “essentially ‘flat.’”

surprises.description: Total revenue slightly exceeded consensus, but remained within the company's prior guidance range and the preview's expected base-case outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue for Q1 FY2027 was $52.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave consensus of “$51.5M,” prior guidance of “$50.0–54.0M,” and a base scenario of “$52–54M.”

surprises.description: The FY27 revenue range was reaffirmed, as expected, but the non-GAAP operating-loss range improved modestly versus the preview's stated guide: its endpoints were each $5 million lower.
surprises.fact_evidence: FY2027 guidance is revenue of “$210 million to $240 million” and non-GAAP operating loss of “$123 million to $155 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected FY27 revenue guidance of “$210–240M” and cited an operating-loss guide of “$128 to $160M.”

in_line: The FY27 revenue range stayed at $210–240 million, matching the preview's expectation that management would reaffirm it.

The approximately $135 million in annualized cost savings was in line with the preview, which said approximately $135 million had already been removed; the preview also anticipated a substantial headcount reduction.

surprises.description: Revenue was $384 million, far above the preview’s $297.8 million consensus and $300 million base estimate. The $86 million gap was much larger than a routine beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record consolidated Q2 fiscal 2027 revenue of $384 million,” up 62% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus: “$297.8M”; preview base estimate: “$300M.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS of $3.76 substantially exceeded the preview’s $2.68 consensus and approximately $2.85 base estimate, despite the preview already anticipating an earnings beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 net income of $53.3 million or $3.76 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: EPS consensus: “$2.68”; preview base estimate: “~$2.85.”

surprises.description: Backlog fell to $2.5 billion, below the preview’s $2.7–$2.9 billion base range and even below its $2.6 billion bear-case threshold. The preview expected another decline, but the reported level was materially weaker than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total committed backlog fell to $2.5 billion from $2.9 billion at the start of fiscal 2027,” with “no major new power projects” added.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview base: “$2.7–2.9B”; bear case: “<$2.6B.” It also said a third decline below “~$2.7B” would confirm the bear case.

surprises.description: Consolidated gross margin was 19.3%, below the preview’s roughly 20% watchpoint and 20.5% base estimate, though above the 18.5% margin implied by consensus and still within management’s stated high-teens-to-low-20s range. The margin decline was attributed to earlier-stage Power work rather than early-completion benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin has declined sequentially over three quarters from 25% in Q4 FY2026 to 21% in Q1 to 19.3% in Q2,” reflecting “earlier-stage Power projects rather than early-completion benefits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged gross margin “vs. ~20%,” gave a base estimate of “20.5%,” and said consensus implied “~18.5%.”

surprises.description: Industrial margin dropped to 7.3%, well below the 11.8% reported for Q1 FY2027 that the preview highlighted as a key reference point. The segment’s sharp revenue growth therefore came with weaker-than-expected profitability from underperforming non-data-center work.
surprises.fact_evidence: Industrial revenue “surged 111% to $76 million but carried a weak 7.3% margin due to underperforming non-data-center projects.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Industrial at “$58M/20% at 11.8%” and said to “Watch Industrial margin (the swing factor for mix).”

surprises.description: Management pulled forward the expected window for a handful of new projects: the preview cited 10–18 months, while the call cited 7–15 months. This is a more encouraging timeline, although no major new Power projects had yet been added to backlog.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects to add “a handful of new projects over the next 7-15 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview quoted management expecting “a handful of new projects over the next 10–18 months.”

surprises.description: The Valcor acquisition was described in the preview as an immaterial tuck-in, but the call said it could double Tele Data revenue from fiscal 2026 levels. That gives the acquisition a potentially much larger growth role than the preview suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: Argan acquired Valcor Communications to expand Tele Data, “which could double revenue from fiscal 2026 levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the acquisition “~$8.3M” and “Immaterial to the quarter; relevant as a signal that the smallest segment is being fed.”

surprises.description: The North Carolina fabrication facility was already expected to support a data-center contract, but the call added a quantified outlook of more than $10 million in quarterly Industrial revenue from the facility. That revenue contribution was not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The new North Carolina fabrication facility, “completing in Q3,” is “expected to add $10+ million in quarterly Industrial revenue.”

in_line: Management’s plan to pursue a handful of projects and capacity to execute 10–12 jobs simultaneously were consistent with the preview’s discussion of the pipeline and execution capacity.
Gross margin remained within the previously described high-teens-to-low-20s range and stayed above the preview’s sub-19% downside trigger.
The company’s approximately $1 billion in cash and investments, net liquidity, and lack of debt were broadly consistent with the preview’s balance-sheet figures and capital-allocation capacity.

surprises.description: Management announced an Investor Day for December 17 at the New York Stock Exchange, including presentations from the Chief Strategy Officer and Head of Mobility and product demonstrations; the preview did not mention a planned event.
surprises.fact_evidence: John announced an Investor Day on December 17 at the New York Stock Exchange, with presentations from the Chief Strategy Officer and Head of Mobility and product demonstrations.

surprises.description: The preview expected FY2026 AI revenue of $56B and Q4 AI revenue of about $21B. Broadcom raised the FY2026 target to $58B and guided Q4 to $21.7B, above the preview’s roughly $21B estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Broadcom raised its full-year fiscal 2026 AI revenue guidance to $58 billion … from the prior $56 billion, with Q4 AI revenue guided to $21.7 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management's FY26 AI target of $56B”; “leaves exactly ~$21B for Q4”; Morgan Stanley modeled “AI revenue $21.2B (+32% q/q).”

surprises.description: The preview expected FY2027 AI revenue to be above $100B, but did not have a specific figure. Management put a number on it at approximately $115B, and also forecast another doubling to $230B in FY2028 with supply secured for both targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided AI semiconductor revenue to approximately double to $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and double again to $230 billion in fiscal 2028, with supply already secured for both targets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 ‘>$100B’ — raised, quantified, or merely reaffirmed”; supply and capacity for 2028–29 were “still under negotiation as of June.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Q3 AI semiconductor revenue of about $16.0B. Broadcom reported $16.7B, about $700M higher, with 221% year-over-year growth versus the preview’s 208% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI semiconductor revenue tripled year-on-year to $16.7 billion in Q3, growing 221% year-over-year and 54% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AI semiconductor rev … ~$16.0B”; “+208%.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted Google’s dual-sourcing of ASICs as a concern and called for updates on TPU share. Broadcom instead announced a long-term Google agreement expected to deliver multiple tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually, with the next-generation TPU already in production.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A long-term agreement with Google will deliver multiple tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually over several years, with next-gen TPU v8i now in production ahead of the prior Ironwood generation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Tan conceded last quarter that Google is dual-sourcing ASICs. Watch for … any color on Google TPU share.”

surprises.description: The preview described OpenAI’s roughly $18B, 1.3GW first phase as reportedly stalled and noted deployment was still guided to 1GW+ in 2027. The call projected OpenAI as Broadcom’s second-largest XPU customer, with over 5GW of deployment in 2028; that projection does not itself resolve the preview’s question about the first phase or its 2027 timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OpenAI is projected to become Broadcom's second-largest XPU customer, with over 5 gigawatts of deployment in 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The ~$18B, 1.3GW first phase reportedly stalled”; “Volume XPU deployment is still guided to 1GW+ in 2027.”

surprises.description: The preview did not cite a specific Anthropic deployment scale or forecast it becoming Broadcom’s largest XPU customer. Management said it is on track to become the largest in 2027, with deployments rising from 1GW in 2026 to 5GW in 2027 and an additional 10GW in 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Anthropic is on track to become Broadcom's largest XPU customer in 2027, deploying 5 gigawatts of TPU v8i in 2027 and an incremental 10 gigawatts in 2028, after 1 gigawatt of Ironwood in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Anthropic among the “current six” named XPU customers but gave no customer-ranking or deployment forecast for it.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a Broadcom accelerator performance or cost comparison with Nvidia’s product. The call reported that OpenAI’s Jalapeno accelerator outperforms Grace Blackwell Ultra at roughly half the cost of a GPU.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its Jalapeno accelerator reportedly outperforms Grace Blackwell Ultra at roughly half the cost of a GPU.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Q3 gross margin around 74%. Broadcom reported 75%, about one percentage point above that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin … in Q3” was 75%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin … ~74%.”

surprises.description: The preview centered on gross margin around 74% and described below 73% as a bear-case outcome. Broadcom guided Q4 gross margin to about 73%, indicating further decline rather than holding near 74%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Gross margin] is guided to fall to about 73% in Q4 due to rising XPU and memory mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP GM ~74%”; the preview’s bear scenario included “GM guided <73%.”

surprises.description: The preview expected operating margin around 67%. Management said Q4 operating margin would be about 66%, a modest step below that level, despite describing operating leverage as resilient.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin remains resilient at ~66% from operating leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin ~67%”; the preview said bulls needed management to re-anchor on “operating margin (67%).”

surprises.description: The preview did not include a long-term EPS target. Management said Broadcom is on target to exceed $30 in EPS in FY2028, adding a specific long-range earnings milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Broadcom stated it is on target to exceed $30 in earnings per share in fiscal 2028.”

in_line: Q3 consolidated revenue was $29.6B, broadly in line with the preview’s $29.43–29.44B consensus and its $29.6–30.0B base-case range.
Q3 free cash flow of $13.7B and 46% of revenue were within the preview’s expectation of at least $13B and 40–46% conversion.
Q3 operating margin of 67.9% was broadly in line with the preview’s approximately 67% expectation.

surprises.description: The preview estimated net new ARR of roughly $33–37 million and set $35 million as the bar; Netskope reported $54 million. That is a large dollar beat, although the reported 9% growth rate is less compelling than the preview’s hoped-for reacceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new ARR of $54 million growing only 9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net new ARR (not guided): ~$33–37M (my est.)”; “Bar: ≥$35M, and ideally flat-to-up YoY.”

surprises.description: Operating margin was much better than the preview’s expected Q2 range: negative 9% versus guidance of negative 14% to negative 15%. The improvement was driven largely by an approximately 8-point reduction in R&D as a percentage of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin improved 11 percentage points year-over-year to negative 9%, significantly ahead of guidance, driven largely by an ~8-point improvement in R&D as a percent of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin: (14)% to (15)%.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $220.5 million cleared both company guidance and the preview’s assumed buy-side bar of roughly $216–217 million, rather than merely delivering the expected beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue grew 29% to $220.5 million, beating guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $213–215M”; “Assume buy-side bar ≈ $216–217M.”

surprises.description: Netskope raised its FY2027 revenue outlook to $888–892 million, above the preview’s base-case raise to $885–888 million and around the preview’s $890 million confidence threshold. The company said the increase exceeded the Q2 beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $888-892 million (~26% growth), lifting it by more than the Q2 beat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise to $890M+ with explicit 2H net new ARR commentary is the bull trigger”; base case: “Raised to $885–888M.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow improved substantially from Q1 but remained weaker than the preview’s preferred Q2 range of roughly negative $20 million to breakeven. Full-year FCF margin is now guided to about 2%, the bottom of the preview’s prior 2%–4% range; Q3 positive FCF and faster-than-expected annual-billing transition partly offset the shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was negative $29.8 million in Q2, with full-year free cash flow margin guided to ~2% and Q3 FCF of $10-20 million, aided by a faster-than-expected transition to annual billings that grew contracted future billings 75%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FCF materially worse than roughly ‑$20M to breakeven” was the downside threshold; FY guidance was “+2% to +4%”; management had called Q1 the “low-water mark” and expected positive quarterly FCF in the back half.

surprises.description: Expansion and product adoption were stronger than the preview’s already-high baseline: NRR rose to 114% from 113%, 4+ product adoption reached 59% from the 57% Q1 baseline, and 41% of customers used 5+ products.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net retention rate rose to 114% and gross retention hit an all-time high, with 59% of customers now using 4+ products (up from 51%) and 41% using 5+ products (up from 35%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “NRR (113%)” and “57% of customers on 4+ products” as metrics to watch.

surprises.description: The AI security pipeline showed meaningful progress, with about one-third of it in or entering POC, but the disclosed 6–12-month enterprise sales cycle pushes expected AI revenue contribution toward the second half and Q4 rather than showing near-term conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly one-third of its AI security pipeline is in or entering the POC phase, with most deals following a 6-to-12-month enterprise sales cycle that pushes AI revenue contribution toward the second half and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called AI suite conversion a key watch item: “pipeline → closed ARR contribution, named logos, attach rates,” while noting that prior commentary concerned “pipeline, not bookings.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed an approximately 5% workforce reduction alongside a shift of spending toward AI infrastructure and tokens. The preview did not anticipate this restructuring and investment reallocation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced approximately 5% of its workforce while reallocating spend toward AI infrastructure and tokens as part of driving ‘AI nativeness’ across the business.”

surprises.description: Management presented AI security as a new revenue pillar and sized it as a roughly $170 billion greenfield opportunity within a $336 billion total addressable market—an expansive market framing not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Netskope frames its opportunity as a $170 billion greenfield AI security market within a $336 billion total addressable market, positioning AI security as a new revenue pillar beyond SASE/SSE.”

in_line: Total ARR reached $899 million, up 27% year-over-year, matching the preview’s estimated 27% growth rate even though the dollar amount exceeded its $875–885 million estimate.
Gross retention remained at a record high, as the preview noted Q1 gross retention was already at a record level.
Customers spending over $100,000 in ARR grew 23% year-over-year, consistent with the preview’s Q1 baseline of 23% growth.
About half the sales reps were still ramping, consistent with the preview’s expectation that roughly half the sales force was new or ramping.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $32.9 million, above the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $30–32 million; the reported 25% margin also exceeded its 23.7% base estimate. This was a modest operating-performance upside relative to the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $32.9 million with a 25% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: ~$30–32M”; base estimate: “$31M (23.7% margin).”

surprises.description: Phreesia reported a 2.4% Payment Solutions revenue rate, above the 2.3% rate the preview highlighted as the level to watch. That points to a slightly better rate than expected to hold as AccessOne mixed in.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total managed payments were $1.626 billion in the quarter, with a Payment Solutions revenue rate of 2.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Payment Solutions rate (2.3%) … Watch whether the rate holds as AccessOne mixes in.”

surprises.description: A Provider Connect study produced follow-on business during FY27, earlier than the preview’s framing of Provider Connect primarily as an FY28–FY30 opportunity. The preview did describe FY27 dollars as possible upside, so the commercial conversion is an upside signal rather than a wholly unanticipated revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 4-month GLP-1 category study using Provider Connect showed a 4% incremental lift in new-to-brand prescriptions versus a matched control group and more than 1,000 new patient starts, and converted follow-on business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has framed ProviderConnect as an FY28–FY30 runway, so any FY27 dollars are upside.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted a possible buyback authorization as a notable capital-allocation surprise, while the reported capital-allocation action was to reduce debt principal by more than $23 million. The provided facts do not report a buyback, so the disclosed action leaned toward deleveraging rather than the potential repurchase catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced debt principal by over $23 million during the quarter while maintaining a healthy cash balance of $74.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management named ‘share repurchases, as appropriate’ as a priority”; “A buyback authorization at ~$12 … would be a meaningful sentiment reset.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $129.5 million was within the preview’s $129.1–$130.6 million consensus range, consistent with its expectation that the quarter would be broadly in line.
Management maintained FY27 revenue guidance of $510–$520 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $125–$135 million, as the preview’s base case expected.

Average healthcare services clients grew 6% year over year and revenue per client rose 4%, consistent with the preview’s mid-single-digit client growth and low-single-digit revenue-per-client expectations.
Management’s deliberate subscription-pricing moderation and its emphasis on downstream payments and network monetization were consistent with the strategy described in the preview.

surprises.description: Snowflake reported $1.49 billion of product revenue, above the preview’s $1.46–$1.48 billion whisper range and the $1.47 billion bull-case threshold. The beat was modest, but growth accelerated to 37%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 product revenue reached $1.49 billion, growing 37% year-over-year, marking the third consecutive quarter of acceleration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Product revenue … Est. Buy-Side Whisper $1.46–1.48B”; the bull case expected “≥$1.47B.”

surprises.description: Snowflake raised FY’27 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion, well above the preview’s anticipated $5.95 billion-or-higher bar. This was a substantially larger raise than the preview’s base-case range of $5.88–$5.94 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year FY'27 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion (36% growth), an increase of over 500 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 product guide ≥$5.95B” was the catalyst threshold; the base scenario expected “$5.88–5.94B.”

surprises.description: The company lowered FY’27 non-GAAP product gross margin guidance to 74%, below the preview’s 75% catalyst threshold and the level at which it warned AI-related margin dilution would become a concern. Management attributed the reduction to the growing mix of lower-contribution-margin AI workloads.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year non-GAAP product gross margin guidance was lowered to 74% due to a higher revenue mix from fast-growing AI workloads that carry lower contribution margins today.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP product gross margin ≥75%” was a catalyst; the preview said “Sub-74.5% turns the AI story into a margin-dilution story.”

surprises.description: Snowflake raised FY’27 non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 14.5%, above the preview’s 13–14% whisper range. Q2 margin was also 15%, expanding by more than 400 basis points year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year non-GAAP operating margin guidance was raised from 13.5% to 14.5%, with Q3 guided at 15.5%”; Q2 margin “expanded over 400 basis points year-over-year to 15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Non-GAAP op margin … Est. Buy-Side Whisper 13–14%.”

surprises.description: Net new customer additions exceeded the preview’s expected range: Snowflake added 692 customers, versus the preview’s sell-side expectation of 440–490 and its comparison point of 616 additions in Q1. Total customers reached 14,554, above the preview’s 14,450-plus whisper.
surprises.fact_evidence: “692 net new customers added (a 32% year-over-year increase) bringing total customers to 14,554.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “~14,350–14,400 (+440–490 net)” by consensus and “14,450+” in its whisper; it also noted “+616 in Q1.”

surprises.description: CoCo adoption was stronger than the preview’s already-raised expectation: it reached 9,100 accounts, versus the preview’s Q1 reference of 7,100 and expectation for accounts “well above” that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CoCo surpassed 9,100 accounts, adding over 2,000 net new accounts in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “CoCo accounts vs. 7,100 last quarter” and described the bull case as having accounts “well above 7,100.”

surprises.description: The revenue acceleration was not solely dependent on AI products: management attributed roughly half to AI and the other half to core platform strength, migrations, and other products. That counters the preview’s concern that the prior-quarter AI surge might have been a pull-forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly half of the revenue acceleration” came from AI products, “with the other half from core platform strength, migrations, and other products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview raised the possibility that “Q1's Cortex Code surge” was “a pull-forward” and said the bear case would involve Q1 acceleration reflecting “front-loaded AI experimentation.”

surprises.description: RPO growth slowed to 30% from 38% in Q1, a weaker headline trend than the prior-quarter figure the preview highlighted. However, the portion expected to convert within 12 months implies about 42% year-over-year growth, making the signal mixed rather than uniformly weak.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligations grew 30% year-over-year to $9 billion, with approximately 54% expected to be recognized as revenue in the next 12 months (about 42% year-over-year growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “RPO growth (+38% in Q1)” as a key metric to watch and noted that RPO “is lumpy on large renewals.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed CoWork at 5,800 accounts, up nearly 11% quarter over quarter. The preview discussed AI adoption and CoCo but did not anticipate or provide an expectation for CoWork adoption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CoWork expanded to 5,800 accounts, up nearly 11% quarter-over-quarter.”

in_line: NRR was 126%, matching the preview’s base-case expectation and its stated catalyst threshold, although it did not reach the 127%+ level described as the clearest evidence of stronger expansion.
The preview anticipated a meaningful FY’27 product revenue guidance raise, including a bull-case threshold of at least $5.95 billion; the actual $6.07 billion guidance exceeded that expectation.

surprises.description: Genesco reported an adjusted loss of $0.83 per share, substantially smaller than the preview’s $1.34 expected loss, even though revenue and comparable sales were roughly in line.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted loss per share improved to $0.83” and “bottom-line results came in well ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS Consensus $(1.34).”

surprises.description: Genesco cut its full-year comparable-sales outlook from growth of 1%–2% to flat, and now expects total sales to fall about 2% rather than its prior outlook of down 1% to flat; it cited greater pressure at schuh in the promotional UK market.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was cut to flat comparable sales (from up 1%-2%) and total sales down approximately 2%, reflecting greater sales pressure at schuh in the increasingly promotional UK market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance … comps +1–2%; total sales –1% to flat.”

surprises.description: While the $2.00–$2.40 full-year adjusted EPS range was not raised, Genesco now expects to finish at its high end, above the midpoint expectation described on the call and more constructive than simply reiterating the range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now expects full-year adjusted EPS at the high end of its $2 to $2.40 range, up from the prior midpoint expectation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reiteration of $2.00–$2.40 is the minimum acceptable outcome”; the preview’s base case was that the FY guide would be reiterated.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin expanded 140 basis points, well ahead of the company’s 50–70-basis-point Q2 guide; schuh’s 300-basis-point improvement and a 10-point rise in full-price mix were key drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 140 basis points to 47.2%, driven largely by schuh's 300 basis point margin improvement as full-price mix rose 10 percentage points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … +50–70 bps.”

surprises.description: Journeys’ comp accelerated from 2% for Q2 to mid-single digits in August, providing a stronger late-quarter signal than the preview’s concern that back-to-school demand had shifted later and needed confirmation in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Journeys posted its eighth consecutive quarter of positive comps (up 2%) and accelerated to a mid-single-digit comp in August.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2026 BTS intent has skewed later (September 29% of intent vs. August 26%), pushing revenue into Q3”; the preview called for explicit September/Q3 color to establish whether demand had shifted or failed to materialize.

in_line: Q2 revenue was $530 million, close to the preview’s $528.4 million consensus and within the company’s guided range.
Overall comparable sales were down 1%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of roughly flat comps and its stated base-case range of flat to down 1%.
Journeys remained comp-positive, consistent with the preview’s focus on continuation of its positive-comp streak.

surprises.description: NetApp reported Q1 revenue of $2.03 billion, well above the $1.836 billion consensus and the $1.90 billion high end of guidance. Even excluding the roughly $65 million from the extra week flagged in the preview, revenue was about $1.965 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% year-over-year to a record $2.03 billion (26% growth excluding the extra week that added ~$65 million), exceeding the high end of all guidance ranges.”

surprises.description: Q1 non-GAAP EPS reached $2.58, far above the $2.12 consensus and even the preview’s bullish scenario of $2.30–$2.40. The preview’s base case was $2.18–$2.26.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached $2.58, up 66% year-over-year—more than double the revenue growth rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus (as of 9/1/26): $2.12”; the bull scenario forecast EPS of “$2.30–2.40.”

surprises.description: Q1 operating margin reached 31.9%, substantially above the approximately 28.9% consensus expectation. That was a 6.1-point year-over-year expansion, versus the preview’s expected 3.1-point expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded 6.1 points to 31.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q1 operating-margin consensus at “~28.9%” and implied year-over-year growth of “+310bp.”

surprises.description: NetApp raised its FY27 revenue midpoint to $8.1 billion, well above the prior $7.45 billion midpoint and the preview’s roughly $7.5 billion consensus. It also lifted the EPS midpoint to $9.88 from $8.85, above the preview’s roughly $8.90 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management materially raised full-year FY27 guidance, increasing the revenue midpoint by $650 million to $8.1 billion (17% growth) and lifting the EPS midpoint to $9.88 (22% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 company guidance of “$7.325–7.575B” revenue and “$8.70–9.00” EPS, with consensus of “~$7.5B” revenue and “~$8.90” EPS.

surprises.description: The Q2 revenue midpoint of $2.1 billion is far above the $1.84 billion consensus, despite the preview’s base scenario of $1.87–$1.95 billion. The reported 23% year-over-year growth represents deceleration from Q1, but the dollar guide is much stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 guidance implies decelerating growth of 23% year-over-year at the $2.1 billion revenue midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY27 revenue: $1,840M”; the preview’s base scenario forecast “Q2 rev $1.87–1.95B.”

surprises.description: Q2 EPS guidance of $2.59 is well above the $2.16 consensus and the preview’s base-case range of $2.18–$2.26.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 guidance implies … EPS midpoint of $2.59.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY27 EPS: $2.16”; the preview’s base scenario forecast “Q2 … EPS ~$2.18–2.26.”

surprises.description: The Q2 gross-margin guide of 67%–68% is below the preview’s key threshold of 69% and well below the level it said would confirm the product-margin trough. Product gross margin had also fallen 150 basis points sequentially to 54.6% as component costs rose.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 guidance implies … gross margin of 67%-68%”; “Product gross margin declined 150 basis points sequentially to 54.6% due to higher component costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Above 69.5% = trough confirmed”; “Below 69.0% = the FY27 $8.70–9.00 bridge is in question.”

surprises.description: Despite the weak near-term gross-margin guide, management said product gross margin for the rest of FY27 should be slightly better than its prior low-50% outlook, as pricing actions are being captured faster. That is better than the preview’s concern that component-cost increases might outrun pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects [product gross margin] to run slightly better than the prior low-50% outlook for the rest of the year as pricing actions are captured faster.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned: “If the Q2 GM guide is below ~69%, the trough call breaks,” and noted that price increases would have their “full effect over 2–3 quarters.”

surprises.description: All-flash array revenue grew 47%, a sharp acceleration from the 18% growth reported in Q4, and product revenue rose 51%, lifting its share of total revenue to 49% from 42%. The preview flagged the AFA run rate but did not anticipate this degree of acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All-flash array revenue grew 47% year-over-year to $1.31 billion, and product revenue jumped 51% to $987 million, rising to 49% of total revenue versus 42% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q4 AFA revenue of “$1,216M (+18% y/y)” and FY26 AFA growth of “+11%.”

surprises.description: Public cloud revenue grew 28% year over year, or 19% excluding the extra week, accelerating from the preview’s cited Q4 growth of 11% (18% excluding Spot). The preview highlighted public cloud as a metric to watch but did not set a Q1 growth estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Public cloud revenue grew 28% year-over-year to $206 million (19% excluding the extra week).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q4 public cloud revenue of “$182M (+11%; +18% ex-Spot)” and identified public cloud as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: NetApp reported about 350 AI and data-lake modernization wins, down from roughly 500 in the prior quarter and below the preview’s 500–600 base-case expectation. Increasing deal sizes temper the weaker count, but management still declined to quantify AI’s revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company won approximately 350 AI and data lake modernization deals with increasing deal sizes, down from about 500 in the prior quarter, though management declined to quantify AI's revenue contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “AI wins ~500–600” and identified conversion into production deployment as a key debate.

surprises.description: Inventory nearly doubled sequentially and inventory turns fell to 6. The preview discussed sharply rising component costs and demand, but did not anticipate this degree of inventory build or the resulting drop in turns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory nearly doubled sequentially as the company secured supply against rising component costs and strong demand, with inventory turns falling to 6.”

in_line: The extra week added about $65 million of Q1 revenue, as the preview specifically warned; the reported revenue beat remained substantial even excluding that contribution.

surprises.description: Ciena’s Q3 adjusted operating margin reached 22.5%, 250 basis points above its 19–20% guidance and above the preview’s 21% whisper estimate. That was a much stronger margin result than investors were led to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin more than doubled year-on-year to a record 22.5%, exceeding guidance by 250 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin | 19–20% | ~19.6%”; the preview also says Morgan Stanley modeled “21% operating margin.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.11 substantially exceeded both the $1.73 consensus and the preview’s roughly $1.95 whisper estimate. The preview described its $1.72–1.76 guidance-based build as having “no beat embedded.”
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS hitting a record $2.11.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS ... consensus $1.73”; “Treat ... ~$1.95 EPS as the real whisper.”

surprises.description: Backlog rose by $800 million to $8.5 billion, beating the preview’s greater-than-$8.3 billion bogey and its requirement for sequential growth above Q2’s $600 million. The call also added that backlog is on track to exceed $10 billion by fiscal-year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog increased $800 million in Q3 to $8.5 billion, and Ciena expects to exit fiscal 2026 with over $10 billion in backlog.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Morgan Stanley's stated bogey is sequential growth greater than Q2's $600M, i.e., backlog >$8.3B.”

surprises.description: Ciena’s preliminary FY27 outlook was far more specific and strong than the preview expected: it projected at least 30% revenue growth to $8.3–$8.4 billion and a record 25–27% operating margin, despite calling the revenue outlook a supply-constrained floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Preliminary fiscal 2027 outlook projecting revenue growth of at least 30% to $8.3–$8.4 billion (a supply-constrained floor) ... and record operating margin of 25–27%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 framing (no formal guide expected until December)”; “Any quantified FY27 growth framing is the single biggest potential narrative unlock.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue guidance of $1.75 billion was above the preview’s implied Q4 estimate of about $1.677 billion, and the FY26 revenue midpoint rose to $6.42 billion versus the preview’s $6.3 billion guidance. Full-year adjusted operating margin was also lifted to 20–21%, above the preview’s Q3 margin guidance range of 19–20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 revenue is guided to $1.75 billion (+/- $50 million), raising the full-year midpoint to $6.42 billion and lifting full-year adjusted operating margin to 20–21%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied Q4 is ~$1,677M”; “FY26 guidance is $6.3B ± $100M”; Q3 adjusted operating margin guidance was “19–20%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 46.4%, above the preview’s roughly 45.0% consensus and 45.5% whisper, although a one-time tariff refund contributed 70 basis points. The underlying result therefore beat expectations by less than the headline gap suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 46.4% (including a one-time 70 bps tariff-refund benefit).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin ... Consensus ~45.0%”; Morgan Stanley modeled “45.5% GM.”

surprises.description: Direct cloud provider revenue grew more than 80% year-on-year, exceeding the preview’s expected growth of about 70%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct cloud provider revenue grew over 80% year-on-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview describes direct cloud revenue as “(+70% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: Data-center-related growth exceeded the preview’s stated target: “in and around the data center” revenue quadrupled year-to-date versus a committed 3x target. Interconnects also more than doubled, for which the preview gave no specific bogey.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interconnects more than doubled, and ‘in and around the data center’ revenue quadrupled year-to-date, well ahead of the committed 3x growth target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says management had guided “pluggables ... to more than double vs. 2025” and flags data-center growth drivers, but does not give an expectation of quadrupling; the call says the 3x target was exceeded.

surprises.description: Management said negotiated price increases ranging from high single digits to high-teens or low-20s percentages will selectively apply to existing backlog. The preview did not anticipate repricing already-booked orders, a potential lift to future revenue economics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ciena secured negotiated price increases ranging from high single digits to high-teens/low-20s percent that will selectively apply to existing backlog.”

surprises.description: Ciena secured long-term supply agreements for key optical components through 2029, providing a specific supply-security development beyond the preview’s open question about capacity investments and constrained components.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New long-term supply agreements securing key optical components through 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asks whether “capacity investments are landing in FY27” and whether management will discuss pump-laser and DSP-modem constraints; it gives no expectation of agreements extending through 2029.

surprises.description: RLS Hyper-Rail was described as on track for customer standardization by the end of 2026 and expected to generate several hundred million dollars in 2027 at above-company-average margins. That is more specific about the timing, scale, and economics than the preview’s expectation of deployments beginning in FY27 and hundreds of millions over multiple years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RLS Hyper-Rail is on track for customer standardization by end of 2026 and is expected to ramp to several hundred million dollars of revenue in 2027 at margins accretive to the corporate average.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says Hyper-Rail had “hundreds of millions over multiple years” and that “deployments begin FY27.”

surprises.description: Management said the supply-demand imbalance is likely to persist into at least 2028, extending the constraint horizon beyond the preview’s focus on constraints into FY27. That tempers the otherwise strong outlook by indicating supply is not expected to normalize soon.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management believes supply-demand imbalance persists into at least 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flags “continued constraint into FY27” as a possibility and asks whether capacity investments are landing in FY27; it does not extend the outlook to 2028.

surprises.description: Ciena said it expects to raise combined optical systems and plug market share by about four points to roughly 30% in Q4. The preview discussed market-share-related growth drivers but did not set an expectation for this gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects to raise combined optical systems and plug market share by about 4 points to roughly 30% in Q4.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that hyperscalers represent about half of Ciena’s business, highlighting greater exposure to that customer group than the preview’s cited customer-concentration figure alone conveyed. This underscores concentration risk, even as cloud demand is strong.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hyperscalers now represent about 50% of Ciena's business, and two customers each contributed more than 10% of revenue in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says “Two customers at 34% of revenue” in Q2 and identifies customer concentration and diversification as a key issue; it does not state that hyperscalers represent about half of the business.

surprises.description: Gross margin was expected to be about 47.5%, but reached 52%, a much larger improvement than the preview anticipated. The call attributed most of the increase to the IEPA tariff refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin expanded approximately 320 basis points to 52%, primarily driven by the IEPA tariff refund.
surprises.expectation_evidence: My Base Est.: Gross margin ~47.5% (−150bp).

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was expected to be about $12.5 million, but came in at $11 million, the bottom of the $11–14 million guide. The call said tariff-refund benefits were offset by the new WHP JV royalty structure and warehouse-management-system disruptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA fell $4 million year-over-year to $11 million, as tariff refund benefits were offset by the new WHP JV royalty structure and warehouse management system disruptions.
surprises.expectation_evidence: My Base Est.: Adj. EBITDA $12.5M; Q2 guide $11.0–14.0M.

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA range was lowered to $62–70 million, below the prior $68–78 million guide; the preview specifically identified a cut below $68 million as a bearish trigger.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year fiscal 2026 guidance calls for adjusted EBITDA of $62–$70 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 guide: Adj. EBITDA $68–78M. The preview also said an outright EBITDA cut below $68M was the bear trigger.

surprises.description: The new full-year adjusted EPS range of $0.44–0.72 is higher than the prior $0.32–0.65 range, improving both the low and high ends even as the EBITDA guide was cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year fiscal 2026 guidance calls for adjusted EPS of $0.44–$0.72.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 guide: Adj. EPS $0.32–0.65.

surprises.description: The reported $9 million U.S. e-commerce growth obscured weaker underlying performance: the preview expected underlying low-single-digit growth, while management said year-to-date growth was essentially flat and that Q2 growth was inflated by catching up on Q1 backlog.
surprises.fact_evidence: U.S. e-commerce sales grew 9% year-over-year, but management disclosed this was inflated by Q1 backlog catch-up, with underlying year-to-date U.S. e-commerce growth essentially flat.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management said the DC systems rollout delayed Q1 shipments and that underlying demand supported low-single-digit growth; those delayed orders should be a Q2 revenue tailwind.

surprises.description: Inventory remained substantially above the preview's desired trajectory: it was up 13% year-over-year rather than closing toward flat. The explanation that last year's position was intentionally lean and tariff headwinds continued gives context, but does not remove the gap from the preview's expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Inventory rose 13% year-over-year to $342 million, attributed largely to an intentionally lean prior-year position amid tariff uncertainty and continued tariff headwinds.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Inventory ... needs to close toward flat. Still +10%+ means H2 margin is pre-committed to markdowns.

surprises.description: The preview expected the Q1 shipment delays to create a Q2 recapture tailwind, but school-uniform shipments were delayed and backlog rose during Q2. Management did say throughput is now normal or higher and expects no Q3/Q4 guidance impact beyond Outfitters catch-up, which partially limits the concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: Warehouse management system issues delayed school uniform shipments and raised backlog, but management stated operations are now running at normal or higher throughput with no expected impact on Q3/Q4 guidance beyond Outfitters catch-up.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Those delayed orders should be a Q2 revenue tailwind. The preview also identified Q1 shipment recapture as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Adjusted net income and EPS were below the preview's point estimates: $2.7 million and $0.09 per share versus estimates of $3.5 million and $0.11. Both results were still within the preview's stated ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reported Q2 adjusted net income of $2.7 million, or $0.09 per share.
surprises.expectation_evidence: My Base Est.: Adj. net income $3.5M; Adj. diluted EPS $0.11. Preview ranges: $2.0–5.0M and $0.06–0.16.

surprises.description: Third-party marketplace revenue fell roughly 20%, an outcome the preview did not flag, although management said it was intentional: like-for-like gross margin improved by more than 500 basis points as the company prioritized profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: Third-party marketplace revenue declined roughly 20% as the company prioritized profitability, yet like-for-like gross margin improved over 500 basis points year-over-year.

surprises.description: The company repurchased about 900,000 shares for roughly $11 million in the quarter, a capital-allocation action not discussed in the preview; $89 million remained under the authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company repurchased approximately 900,000 shares for about $11 million in Q2, leaving $89 million remaining on its $100 million buyback authorization through March 2029.

surprises.description: ABL borrowings were $60 million, above the preview's roughly $30 million post-repayment reference point. The company had repaid the term loan with WHP proceeds and reduced interest expense, but the higher ABL balance is a less favorable borrowing position than the preview suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: ABL borrowings increased to $60 million from $35 million a year ago, though the $300 million WHP Global proceeds were used to fully repay the term loan, reducing interest expense.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net debt near zero post-repayment (~$30M ABL vs. $23.1M cash at Q1).

in_line: Q2 revenue was $302 million, close to the preview's $300 million base estimate and within the $290–310 million guide.
Full-year revenue guidance of $1.3–1.35 billion narrowed toward the low end, as the preview expected, rather than being an unexpected revenue-guide reduction.
Capital expenditures of roughly $40 million matched the preview's approximately $40 million expectation.

surprises.description: Q4 sales reached $436.9 million, 2.1% above the $427.9 million consensus, while organic growth was 8.4%—above the preview’s 7–8% base-case range. That put revenue above the preview’s bull-case threshold of $435 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 total sales grew 10% (8.4% organic, 1.1% acquisitions, 0.5% FX).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 FY26 revenue | $427.9M”; base case “$425–435M” and “Organic ~7–8%”; bull case “>$435M.”

surprises.description: Americas and Asia organic growth reached 11.6%, above the preview’s bull-case threshold of 10%, and segment profit rose 43.9% with margins expanding 530 basis points. This was stronger than the preview’s recent-growth reference of 8.2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Americas and Asia region posted 11.6% organic growth with segment profit up 43.9% to $74.3 million, expanding margins 530 bps to 25.1% (23.7% excluding the tariff benefit), led by wire ID growth of nearly 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic growth in Americas & Asia. Ran +8.2% in Q3”; bull case: “Americas organic >10%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 52.9%, above the preview’s roughly 51.8% run-rate expectation and above its bull-case threshold of 52%. The improvement was partly helped by a roughly $4 million tariff refund, though margin still rose 110 basis points after adjusting for one-time items.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 52.9% from 50.4%, though this included a ~$4 million tariff refund; adjusting for one-time items, gross margin rose 110 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin. 51.8% in Q3”; base case “GM ~52%”; bull case “GM >52%.”

surprises.description: FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance has a $6.50 midpoint, slightly below the $6.55 consensus, although it meets the preview’s stated $6.50 buy-side hurdle. The $6.25–$6.75 range also extends below the preview’s expected $6.40–$6.60 base-case range; the expected roughly $0.80 IPS accretion was included.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY2027 guidance calls for adjusted EPS of $6.25 to $6.75 (18.1%–27.6% growth), including ~$0.80 of IPS accretion weighted toward the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 revenue / adj. EPS | $2.84B / $6.55”; “Buy-side needed ≥$6.50 to validate the ~$0.80 stated accretion”; base case FY27 guide “$6.40–6.60 (in line).”

surprises.description: Printer unit sales surged 25% in Q4, supporting nearly 10% organic growth in high-margin specialty adhesive consumables. The preview discussed engineered-product mix but did not anticipate this specific volume surge or consumables growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Printer unit sales surged 25% in Q4 and 10% for the full year, driving high-margin specialty adhesive consumable sales that together represent over 40% of Brady's organic sales and grew nearly 10% organically.”
