surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $1.16 (up 26%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “$1.08–1.09”; the preview’s base case was “$1.14–1.17.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $876 million was above the preview’s $867.2 million consensus and just above its $872–875 million base-case range, though the gap to the base case was small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $876 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “$867.2M”; the preview’s base-case revenue range was “$872–875M.”

surprises.description: Direct-customer dollar net retention was 103%, slightly better than the preview’s 102.5% base case and at the preview’s 103%+ bull-case level. The expected improvement streak continued, with expansion contributing more to the improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dollar net retention from Direct customers was 103% (rounded), up modestly from 102% last quarter, with expansion now contributing a larger share of the improvement rather than just retention.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “DNR ~102.5%”; its bull case specified “DNR ~103%+.”

surprises.description: The call reported a sharp increase in MCP activity—active accounts more than quadrupled during the quarter—alongside more than 300 million documents ingested through Agreement Manager. The preview discussed MCP as a catalyst but sought customer wins and dollars; the reported usage is adoption evidence, not quantified commercial conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cumulative documents ingested through IAM's Agreement Manager surpassed 300 million, and MCP active accounts more than quadrupled during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “conversion evidence on Gemini Enterprise for Legal / Perplexity / MCP connector — customer wins and dollars, not announcements.”

in_line: Non-GAAP gross margin was 81.7%, at the top of the preview’s 81.5–81.7% company-guidance range; the slight year-over-year decline was consistent with the preview’s expectation of cloud-migration-related gross-margin pressure.
Diluted shares were 193 million, within the preview’s expected 191–196 million range.

surprises.description: AOUT reported Q1 sales of $37.3 million, above the $35.64 million consensus and the preview’s +20% growth reference. However, after adjusting for orders pulled into the prior-year Q4, underlying growth was about 4%, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of flat-to-slightly-positive normalized growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 net sales rose 25% year-over-year to $37.3 million,” and adjusted for “~$6 million of orders pulled into Q4 fiscal 2025,” underlying growth was “approximately 4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales $35.64M”; management’s Q1 color was “~20% above reported Q1 FY26.” The preview also said “normalized Q1 growth is roughly flat to up slightly.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 53%, far above the preview’s mid-40s expectation. The increase was not solely a temporary tariff-accounting benefit: management attributed roughly 400 basis points to product mix, channel mix, and pricing, alongside about 200 basis points from tariff capitalization timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 gross margin expanded 630 basis points to 53%,” with “roughly 200 bps from tariff capitalization timing and about 400 bps from sustainable product mix, channel mix, and pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected gross margin around the “mid-40s” and said “GM >47% must be interrogated for refund content.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was positive $1.2 million, rather than slightly negative as management had indicated for Q1 and the preview’s base case of a loss. This was a substantial improvement even against the preview’s bull scenario of roughly breakeven to positive $0.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved by $4.3 million year-over-year to a positive $1.2 million,” versus a “$3.1 million loss” in the prior-year quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview quoted Q1 guidance as adjusted EBITDA “slightly negative,” with a base case of “$(1.5)M to $(0.5)M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS turned positive at $0.03, above the preview’s base-case loss range and the stale consensus estimate of a $0.24 loss. The preview did warn that an EPS beat was likely to be optical and included +$0.03 in its bull scenario, so the result was better than its base case but not wholly unanticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS turned positive at $0.03 versus a $0.26 loss a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “$(0.24)”; the preview’s base case was “$(0.13) to $(0.08),” while its bull scenario included “$(0.02) to +$0.03.”

surprises.description: AOUT raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $14.5 million–$17.5 million while leaving its $200 million–$210 million sales outlook unchanged. The higher profitability outlook exceeded the preview’s expectation of simply reaffirming the existing EBITDA margin framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $14.5 million-$17.5 million” while “maintaining net sales guidance of $200 million-$210 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of “6.5–7.5%” and said the key test was an “Unqualified FY27 reaffirm at $200–210M.”

surprises.description: POS growth continued for a sixth consecutive quarter, one quarter beyond the five-quarter streak the preview was watching. Outdoor Lifestyle POS rose 6% and Shooting Sports POS rose 3%; the corresponding segments also reported sales growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 marked the sixth consecutive quarter of positive POS growth, with Outdoor Lifestyle POS up 6% and Shooting Sports POS up 3%, and segment net sales up 34.4% and 15.3% respectively.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s line in the sand was “5th straight positive POS quarter”; it also said “Shooting sports accessories demand should not be the excuse.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that new Section 301 tariffs will start pressuring gross margin later in Q3, with a full-quarter effect in Q4. The preview discussed tariff-related margin quality and existing tariff costs, but did not anticipate this specific upcoming tariff timing and margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New tariffs (Section 301 at 10%-12.5% plus prior tariffs) will begin impacting gross margin later in Q3 with full quarterly impact in Q4 due to inventory turn timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Gross margin + IEEPA content” and said guidance “excludes future refund windfalls,” but did not state that new Section 301 tariffs would begin affecting margins in Q3/Q4.

surprises.description: Operating cash flow was $13 million, versus a $1.7 million use in the prior-year quarter, and ending cash was $33.3 million compared with the $21.4 million balance cited in the preview. This was a stronger cash generation and liquidity outcome than the preview’s seasonal working-capital watch suggested, though it gave no Q1 cash-flow forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $33.3 million in cash, no debt, and over $120 million in total available capital, generating $13 million in operating cash flow versus a $1.7 million usage last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “$21.4M cash, zero debt” and said Q1 would involve “a seasonal build ahead of fall hunting.”

surprises.description: Products introduced in the last 24 months contributed 36% of sales, well above the company’s historical 20%–25% range. The preview anticipated broad placement of new products in its bull case but did not set an expected contribution level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New products introduced over the last 24 months contributed 36% of Q1 net sales, well above the historical 20%-25% average, driven largely by the Caldwell ClayCopter family.”

surprises.description: BUBBA’s paid subscriptions had reached six figures in trailing-twelve-month dollars and accelerated as complimentary two-year subscriptions began expiring. The preview mentioned BUBBA product launches but did not anticipate this subscription-revenue milestone or acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BUBBA's paid subscriptions reached the six-figure dollar range on a trailing-twelve-month basis and accelerated in Q1 as complimentary two-year subscriptions began rolling off.”

in_line: Underlying Q1 sales growth, after adjusting for the roughly $6 million of orders pulled into the prior-year Q4, was approximately 4%, broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of normalized growth that was flat to slightly positive.
FY27 net sales guidance remained at $200 million–$210 million, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating margin reached 21%, versus the preview’s 18% expectation—a 3-point outperformance. The preview flagged margin expansion as important, and the reported margin was also above the 20% level it identified as a bullish signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin reached 21%, up 6 percentage points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin … 18%”; the bull-case management tell was “lifting the FY27 operating-margin target above 20%.”

surprises.description: Samsara’s large-customer additions exceeded the preview’s expected range: it added 242 customers with $100,000+ in ARR, ending at 3,605 versus an expected roughly 3,530–3,560. It also added 20 customers with $1 million+ in ARR, ending at 210 versus an expectation of 205 or more.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Set quarterly records by adding 242 customers with $100,000+ in ARR (ending at 3,605) and 20 customers with $1 million+ in ARR (ending at 210).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for ~3,530–3,560 $100K+ customers … and 205+ million-dollar accounts.”

surprises.description: The FY27 revenue outlook came in slightly above the preview’s base-case expectation: $2.043–$2.047 billion versus a base case of $2.03–$2.04 billion. That is a modestly stronger outlook, though it is below the preview’s bull-case threshold of $2.05 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 revenue to $2.043–2.047 billion (26% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected the guide to be “Raised to $2.03–2.04B”; the bull case required “Raised to ≥$2.05B.”

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue guide was modestly above the roughly $512 million implied by the preview’s full-year outlook. The preview expected normal sequential growth to resume in the second half; the reported Q3 range is a little stronger than that implied figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guided Q3 revenue to $514–516 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The existing full-year guide “mathematically embeds ~$512M in Q3”; the preview said “normal sequential growth resumes in H2.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was positive, but at $0.03 it was below the preview’s consensus estimate of $0.05–$0.07. This was the fourth consecutive profitable quarter, but the reported per-share result fell short of the stated consensus bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Positive GAAP EPS of $0.03.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a weaker full-year free-cash-flow outlook, expecting FY27 FCF margin to be roughly 100 basis points below FY26. The preview discussed Q1 FCF margin but did not flag an annual margin decline or the cited spending and supply-cost pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow margin was 13% in Q2, but management now expects full-year free cash flow margin to be roughly 100 basis points lower than FY26 due to more IoT device purchases, inventory pre-buys, and elevated supply chain costs in the second half.”

surprises.description: Large emerging-product transactions became more numerous: more than 60 transactions included at least $100,000 of emerging-product ACV, up from 42 in the prior quarter. The preview expected emerging products to remain above 20% of net new ACV, but did not anticipate this jump in large transactions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 60 transactions containing $100,000+ in emerging product ACV, up from 42 last quarter”; 8 of the top 10 net new ACV deals included an emerging product.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “>20% of net new ACV from emerging products for two straight quarters.”

surprises.description: Adoption of the latest AI features accelerated sharply, with engagement rising more than fourfold in two months and more than 1,000 customers engaged. That is stronger engagement than the preview’s description of agentic AI as very early, although management still characterized agentic use cases as early-stage and did not report paid GA commercialization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adoption of Samsara's latest AI features rose more than 4x over the past two months with over 1,000 customers engaged, though management noted agentic use cases remain early-stage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Agentic AI is still in beta with customers ‘very early’”; the preview identified a move “from beta to paid GA, with pricing/attach detail” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Public sector produced its second-highest-ever net new ACV mix, including a top-five U.S. city deal with more than $2 million of emerging products. The preview did not identify this public-sector result or deal as an expected contributor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Public sector delivered its second-highest-ever net new ACV mix, driven by a top-5 U.S. city deal that included more than $2 million from emerging products.”

surprises.description: Field services was the largest vertical and reached its highest net new ACV mix in more than two years, a vertical-specific strength not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Field services was the largest vertical with its highest net new ACV mix in over two years.”

surprises.description: The share of large customers using three or more products rose to 72%, above the preview’s 70% figure. The preview’s 96% figure for large customers using at least two products was unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “96% of $100,000+ customers using two or more products and 72% using three or more.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Multi-product: 96% of $100K+ customers on 2+ products, 70% on 3+.”

in_line: ARR growth was 30% year-over-year, in line with the preview’s expectation of roughly 29–30%; crossing $2.1 billion also cleared the preview’s $2.0 billion milestone.
Emerging products contributed more than 20% of net new ACV, consistent with the preview’s expectation that this level would continue.
Core-customer dollar-based net retention was approximately 115%, matching the preview’s Q1 reference of approximately 115%.

surprises.description: Guidewire’s ending ARR was close to, but did not reach, the preview’s $1.243 billion whisper: it was $1.242 billion before a $5 million year-end FX adjustment and $1.237 billion as reported. The adjusted figure was at the high end of company guidance, rather than delivering the preview’s expected $10 million-plus beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ARR finished FY2026 at $1.242 billion,” though “a year-end FX adjustment lowered reported ARR by $5 million to $1.237 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Stifel's Parker Lane looks for a ‘$10M-plus ARR beat’ (~$1,243M+).”

surprises.description: Guidewire signed 26 core cloud deals in Q4, substantially more than the 19 deals in the year-ago quarter that the preview used as a benchmark for whether slipped deals had closed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed 26 core cloud deals in Q4, bringing the full-year total to 62.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “11 deals in Q3 (2 net-new core wins) vs. 19 in Q4 FY25”; the preview called Q4 deal count “proof that Q3's slipped deals actually closed rather than evaporated.”

surprises.description: FY26 total revenue exceeded the top of the preview’s full-year guidance range by $5 million, a small but clear beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 23% to $1.475 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY26 guide: Revenue $1,460–1,470M.”

surprises.description: Subscription and support revenue also finished above the preview’s FY26 guidance range, by $2 million over its high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription and support revenue grew 33% to $971 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY26 guide: … S&S $963–969M.”

surprises.description: FY26 non-GAAP operating income beat the top of the preview’s full-year guidance range by $16 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income surged 63% to $340 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY26 guide: … Non-GAAP OI $314–324M.”

surprises.description: FY26 operating cash flow exceeded the preview’s full-year guidance high end by $10 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow grew 30% to $390 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY26 guide: … OCF $365–380M.”

surprises.description: Guidewire reported record-low gross ARR attrition, which helped drive ARR growth; the preview did not flag such a low attrition result as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record-low gross ARR attrition of less than 1.5% overall and under 1% for core systems customers,” contributing “roughly 1 percentage point to FY2026 ARR growth.”

surprises.description: The preview’s bull case called for a Tier-1 win, and Guidewire reported a particularly notable one: a multiyear cloud migration agreement with Nationwide, which also became its first U.S. Tier 1 PricingCenter customer for home and auto.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guidewire signed a defining multiyear cloud migration agreement with Nationwide, a Fortune 100 insurer,” which “became its first U.S. Tier 1 PricingCenter customer for home and auto lines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bull case listed a “Tier-1 win” as a key driver.

surprises.description: The preview anticipated PricingCenter and other product cross-sell as something to watch, but Guidewire disclosed substantial wins across PricingCenter and ProNavigator, including 14 ProNavigator wins in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PricingCenter closing 8 deals in Q4 (12 for the year) and ProNavigator delivering 14 wins in Q4 (28 for the year), primarily via cross-sell into the installed base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “PricingCenter/UnderwritingCenter cross-sell” as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: The reported repurchase of $606 million in shares was a substantial capital-allocation action not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $606 million in shares (4.1 million shares at $148.41 average).”

surprises.description: Although FY27 ARR guidance matched the preview’s expected range, management said the outlook assumes attrition normalizes rather than staying at FY26’s record-low level, a potential headwind to the ARR build.
surprises.fact_evidence: FY27 ARR guidance “assumes attrition normalizes rather than repeating record lows.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected FY27 ARR guidance of “$1.45–1.46B (in line)” but did not specify an attrition assumption.

surprises.description: Guidewire disclosed a FY27 license-revenue decline tied to cloud migration, a specific revenue headwind not quantified in the preview’s outlook discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “License revenue is guided to decline $46 million to approximately $189 million in FY2027 due to cloud migration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the Q4 revenue slowdown as “a license comp artifact,” but gave no FY27 license-revenue outlook.

in_line: Fully ramped ARR grew 22% year-over-year, matching the preview’s cited 22% growth rate.
FY27 ARR guidance of $1.45–1.46 billion matched the preview’s expected $1.45–1.46 billion range.

surprises.description: Revenue came in at $96.8 million versus the preview’s $93.5 million consensus, a 3.6% beat. This was a modestly positive gap against expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenues were $96.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2'26 Actual $96.8M | Consensus $93.5M | Δ +3.6%”

surprises.description: The preview presented sponsor dropdowns as a multi-year source of growth, but the partnership disclosed that it had removed Frieda Knudsen and Sindra Knudsen from its drop-down inventory. That reduces the visible pool of potential dropdown vessels, though the call facts do not quantify the impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In June 2026, the partnership removed the Frieda Knudsen and Sindra Knudsen from its drop-down inventory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has flagged sponsor inventory dropdowns ‘over the next 4 to 5 years.’”

in_line: The distribution was raised to 7.5 cents per common unit, as the preview anticipated a second consecutive increase and cited a 7.5-cent distribution.
The Heda Knudsen acquisition matched the preview’s cited $113 million price, $89.4 million debt funding, and $24.4 million net cash cost.
The $225 million five-year refinancing at SOFR plus 165 basis points matched the preview’s expected facility terms.
Utilization was 96.8% excluding scheduled dry docking and 92.4% including it, matching the preview’s stated figures.
The $881.2 million fixed contract backlog and its 2.5-year average duration matched the preview.
The preview expected the Investor Day to take place in October; the call announced it would be held in New York next month.

surprises.description: Planet reported Q2 revenue of $116 million, well above the roughly $105 million consensus and the preview’s $106–108 million whisper range. The preview treated a result near $105 million as in-line to soft, so the reported revenue was a clear beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $116 million,” representing “approximately 58% year-over-year growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “~$105M”; the preview said the buy-side whisper was “effectively $106–108M” and that “a print of $105M would be an in-line-to-soft outcome, not a beat.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 59%, far above the preview’s roughly 53–54% consensus and its 52–55% company-guide range. The preview identified 56% or higher as the level needed to repair the margin thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin was 59% … and beat expectations,” and full-year gross margin guidance was raised to 55–57%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 gross margin consensus was “~53–54%” against company guidance of “52–55%”; the preview said “≥56% = thesis repaired.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $13.9 million, substantially above the preview’s roughly $2–3 million consensus and the company’s breakeven-to-$5 million quarterly guide. The preview’s bull case was only $8–12 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA profit was $13.9 million for the quarter, exceeding expectations due to higher margins and revenue outperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted EBITDA guidance of “breakeven to +$5M” and consensus of “~$2–3M”; its bull scenario called for “+$8–12M.”

surprises.description: The FY2027 gross-margin outlook moved up to 55–57%, rather than remaining near the prior 52–55% guide. This is a meaningful improvement in the margin trajectory that the preview identified as the central debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin guidance was raised … to 55%-57%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the prior FY guide as “52–55%” and emphasized the “margin trajectory” as the key issue.

surprises.description: Planet raised the low end of FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance from breakeven to $3 million, instead of simply reaffirming the prior breakeven-to-$10 million range. The preview’s base case expected guidance to be reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company raised “adjusted EBITDA guidance to $3-$10 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance as “breakeven to +$10M” and described its base case as “Reaffirmed / narrowed.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $101–105 million implies a sequential decline and only about 27% year-over-year growth, a much weaker near-term run rate than the strong Q2 result might suggest. Management attributed the decline to point-in-time satellite handover revenue landing in Q2 rather than Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue guidance of $101-$105 million implies only ~27% year-over-year growth and a sequential decline,” because handover revenue landed in Q2 rather than Q3.

surprises.description: Backlog was about $815 million, below the preview’s watch level of at least $950 million and down from the $906 million reported for Q1. That fell short of the preview’s expectation for backlog to keep supporting the growth narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog stood at approximately $815 million (up 11% year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for backlog ≥ $950M” and warned that a backlog “that goes sideways” could suggest the order surge had peaked; it cited Q1 backlog of “$906M (+72%).”

surprises.description: Defense & Intelligence grew more than 90% year over year, well above the preview’s base-case expectation of 50–60% growth. The segment also accounted for roughly 70% of quarterly revenue, showing even greater concentration in the strongest demand area than the preview’s already-positive outlook implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense & Intelligence revenue grew over 90% year-over-year and represented roughly 70% of total quarterly revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “D&I +50–60%”; it cited Q1 D&I growth of “+65%.”

surprises.description: EMEA revenue growth accelerated to more than 130%, above the preview’s cited Q1 growth rate of 86%. The preview highlighted international defense demand, but this degree of further acceleration was not specified as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EMEA revenue surged over 130%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 EMEA growth of “+86%.”

surprises.description: Planet disclosed more than $4 billion of Satellite Services opportunities, with over $1 billion qualified as near-term across EMEA, APAC, and North America. The preview focused on booked backlog and particular deal wins, not this sizable qualified pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over $4 billion of Satellite Services opportunities in its pipeline, with over 25% (~$1 billion) qualified as near-term,” spanning EMEA, APAC, and North America.

surprises.description: The company raised FY2027 CapEx guidance to $100–115 million from the prior $80–95 million range. The higher investment is intended to fund next-generation fleets and manufacturing expansion, but it also means substantially more spending than the preview’s stated outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx guidance was raised to $100-$115 million to fund Pelican and Owl next-generation fleets and German/San Francisco manufacturing expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2027 CapEx of “$80–95M.”

surprises.description: Planet used its ATM, raising $120 million at an average $31.96 per share. The preview’s base case expected no ATM drawdown, although the reported average sale price was above the $20–25 range it highlighted as a dilution concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cash and short-term investments were approximately $865 million, “including $120 million raised via ATM at an average $31.96 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario assumed “no ATM drawdown” and warned about ATM shares issued at “$20–25/share.”

in_line: FY2027 revenue guidance was raised at the low end to $430 million, producing a $430–441 million range; this matched the preview’s base-case expectation of a range around $430–441 million.
Planet continued to target annual adjusted free-cash-flow positivity, consistent with the preview’s expectation that management would reaffirm that commitment.

surprises.description: UiPath raised its FY27 ARR guidance to $2.065–$2.070 billion, just above the prior upper end of $2.063 billion. The preview’s base case expected the ARR guide to remain unchanged, although it identified a raise above $2.063 billion as a bullish signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full year fiscal 2027 guidance calls for ARR of $2.065-$2.070 billion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Current: $2.058–2.063B”; “An ARR guide raise above $2.063B is the genuinely bullish signal”; base case: “ARR guide unchanged.”

surprises.description: The $1 million-plus ARR customer cohort grew 21%, faster than the 18% growth figure the preview cited from Q1. This points to stronger growth among UiPath’s largest customers than that prior benchmark suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers with $1 million or more in ARR grew 21% to 387.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$1M+ ARR customers +18% YoY.”

surprises.description: AI appeared in 18 of the top 20 deals, up from the preview’s cited Q1 figure of 16. Management described AI/platform-attached deals as larger, but the reported facts give no dollar figure for agentic ARR, leaving the preview’s monetization question unanswered.
surprises.fact_evidence: “18 of the top 20 deals this quarter included AI”; deals with AI/platform attached are “naturally much larger,” driving higher ROI and deal values.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 datapoints: 16 of top 20 deals included AI”; “Does management put a dollar figure on agentic ARR this quarter?”

surprises.description: The call reported that coding agents used by forward deployed engineers reduced implementation effort by nearly 60%, a substantial efficiency improvement that the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Coding agents used by forward deployed engineers reduced implementation effort by nearly 60%,” potentially accelerating time-to-value and lowering total cost of ownership.

surprises.description: The call disclosed a CFO succession: Ashim Gupta is moving to focus exclusively on the COO role, with Deputy CFO Hitesh Ramani succeeding him as CFO. The preview did not flag a leadership transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ashim Gupta moving to focus exclusively as COO and Deputy CFO Hitesh Ramani succeeding him as CFO.”

surprises.description: UiPath reported a fourth consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability, a positive result not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of non-GAAP EPS conversion and recent EPS misses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability.”

surprises.description: Cloud ARR reached about $1.3 billion and grew more than 19%, a growth detail the preview did not identify even as it focused on total ARR growth of roughly 12%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cloud ARR reached approximately $1.3 billion, up more than 19% year-over-year.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $410 million was within the preview’s $408–$415 million base-case range and at the low end of its $410–$415 million whisper range.
Q2 ARR of $1.938 billion was at the top of the preview’s expected $1.935–$1.938 billion base-case range.
Net new ARR of $37 million landed within the preview’s $34–$38 million base case, though below its $39 million-plus bull-case threshold.
Dollar-based net retention of 109% (108% FX-adjusted) matched the preview’s cited 109% reported / 108% FX-adjusted level and its 109% watchpoint.
Non-GAAP operating income of $89 million fell within the preview’s expected $85–$95 million range for the quarter.
FY27 revenue guidance of $1.789–$1.794 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of a raise to roughly $1.79–$1.80 billion.

surprises.description: Q1 sales were $112.6 million, up 32.3%—well above the company’s 15–20% guidance and the preview’s roughly $100 million guide-midpoint benchmark. This was also well above the preview’s $102 million threshold for beating the guide high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 net sales grew 32.3% year-over-year to $112.6 million, well above the company's June guidance of 15% to 20% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | ~ $98.7M”; company guide “+15–20% → $97.9–102.1M”; “The clean threshold is >$102M (above the guide high end).”

surprises.description: EPS turned positive at $0.06 rather than the preview’s expected loss of about $0.055 per share. The result was a substantial improvement against the preview’s soft consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EPS turned positive to $0.06 (net income of $2.6 million) versus a loss of $0.08 ($3.4 million net loss) in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | ~$(0.055)”; the preview’s base case was “$(0.04) to $0.00.”

surprises.description: Reported gross margin reached 28.7%, above the preview’s roughly 27% consensus and the 27.9% high end of the company’s expected range. But a one-time tariff refund supplied 260 of the 280 basis points of year-over-year improvement, leaving the underlying margin improvement much less than the headline suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin of 28.7% was up 280 basis points year-over-year, but 260 basis points came from a one-time $2.9 million tariff refund.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~27% (derived)”; company guide “+100–200bps → 26.9–27.9%”; the preview also said “If GM prints ≥27.9% despite” the expected handgun ASP decline, that would show mix and absorption were working.

surprises.description: Handgun ASPs rose nearly 9% year over year instead of falling about 5% as management had warned investors to expect. That is a clear reversal of the anticipated price headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Handgun ASPs were up nearly 9% year-over-year (flat sequentially).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management pre-warned handgun ASPs down ~5%.”

surprises.description: The Q2 outlook calls for sales growth of only about 10%, a marked slowdown from Q1’s 32.3% growth; management also maintained full-year growth guidance of 5–7%, implying a flat-to-down second half. The preview wanted the full-year outlook walked up toward high-single-digit growth after a strong Q1, though it also identified reaffirmation as its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q2 fiscal 2027 sales to be roughly 10% above last year with gross margin 200-300 basis points higher, while maintaining full-year revenue growth guidance of only 5% to 7%, implying a flat-to-down second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side wants mid-single-digit growth walked up toward high-single-digit”; the preview said “A reaffirm after a strong Q1 will read as conservatism-or-caution.”

surprises.description: Long-gun ASPs rose more than 18% year over year and nearly 11% sequentially, with management citing favorable mix and limited promotions. The preview focused on the expected handgun ASP decline as a margin risk and did not anticipate this strength in long-gun pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Long gun ASPs rose over 18% year-over-year and nearly 11% sequentially, driven by favorable mix and limited promotions.”

surprises.description: The 1854 lever-action rifle shipped at twice last year’s level, expanding SWBI’s presence in the higher-priced hunting segment. The preview did not identify this product or growth as an expected driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “1854 lever action rifle shipments doubled versus last year, expanding the company's foothold in the higher-priced hunting segment.”

surprises.description: The quarter ended with $40 million drawn on the credit line against $25.2 million of cash, or about $14.8 million of net debt, rather than the preview’s cited $8.2 million of net cash. That is a weaker balance-sheet position than the preview’s starting point, alongside the dividend payment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $25.2 million in cash and $40 million drawn on its line of credit, paid $6 million in dividends, and reaffirmed its $0.13 quarterly dividend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “net cash of only $8.2M” and highlighted “whether the ~4.3% yield is being funded out of FCF or the balance sheet.”

in_line: New products were 35% of shipments, above the preview’s concern threshold of 30% for a potential innovation-cadence slowdown.

Handgun and long-gun shipments both grew faster than NICS, consistent with the preview’s focus on SWBI continuing to outrun the industry, though the preview did not set a specific expected spread for this quarter.
Management maintained full-year revenue growth guidance of 5–7%, consistent with the preview’s base case that the existing mid-single-digit guide would be reaffirmed.
The large increase in capital spending was anticipated: the preview expected a significant FY27 capex step-up for Springfield and manufacturing investments.
The $0.13 quarterly dividend was reaffirmed, consistent with the preview’s focus on the existing dividend and its coverage.

surprises.description: ABM reported revenue slightly above $2.3 billion, below the preview’s $2.32 billion consensus estimate. The gap appears small, while adjusted EPS of $1.04 matched consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly revenue of slightly above $2.3 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year”; adjusted EPS was “$1.04 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q3 FY26 Consensus | $2.32B”; “Adj. diluted EPS | Q3 FY26 Consensus | $1.04.”

surprises.description: Technical Solutions fell short after roughly $15 million of work for an important microgrid client was deferred, rather than delivering the anticipated H2 mix improvement. Management expects deferred work to resume in Q4, with double-digit organic ATS growth and an 11%–13% operating margin, making the near-term miss partly a timing issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Technical Solutions revenue missed expectations due to roughly $15 million in project deferrals from an important microgrid client”; management expects “double-digit organic ATS growth and 11%-13% operating margin in Q4 as deferred work resumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management promised a ‘ramp in higher-margin project mix’ in H2 off a ~$500M backlog”; ATS margin was described as “the single most diagnostic line in the release.”

surprises.description: Cash generation and deleveraging were ahead of the preview’s expected path: ABM reached 2.9x debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA a quarter before its sub-3x year-end goal, while year-to-date free cash flow reached $199.6 million. The preview had highlighted a substantial second-half cash requirement and recent weak cash conversion as risks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow improved by over $150 million to $199.6 million”; leverage “fell to 2.9x, achieving the sub-3x leverage goal a quarter ahead of plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “H2 FY26 required” free cash flow was “~$179M”; leverage was “3.2x at Q2 vs. a stated <3.0x FYE target”; the preview also flagged “EBITDA-to-cash conversion recently negative.”

surprises.description: The FY2026 adjusted EPS range was narrowed and its midpoint edged up, rather than simply being reaffirmed as the preview’s base case anticipated. The new $3.95–$4.10 range has a $4.025 midpoint versus $4.00 previously, a modest improvement rather than a move to the preview’s bull-case upper half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS midpoint to a range of $3.95 to $4.10.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The existing guidance was “Adj. EPS $3.85–$4.15”; the preview’s base case expected the range to be “held, not raised,” while its bull case described narrowing to the “upper” half.

surprises.description: B&I’s recovery appears later than the preview’s focus on H2 organic growth and Q3 bookings suggested: revenue declined 2.6%, and management does not expect organic growth to return until mid-fiscal 2027. Margin did improve despite the decline, so the surprise is mainly the extended revenue-growth weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “B&I revenue declined 2.6% due to a large U.K. client exit and West Coast losses”; “organic growth not expected to return until mid-fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “B&I organic growth and bookings” as a key metric and described West Coast office softness as “episodic”; it also noted a TfL exit as an H2 headwind.

surprises.description: WGNSTAR was tracking above its guided annualized revenue range, and ABM had already completed several cross-sells. The preview discussed WGNSTAR’s strategic opportunity but did not anticipate this level of progress against its revenue guide or the completed cross-selling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “WGNSTAR is tracking well above its guided $120-130 million annualized revenue,” and management had “already completed 2-3 cross-sells.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “M&D/semis (WGNSTAR, 60+ clients, 300+ sites)” as a secondary item to watch, without predicting results above the WGNSTAR revenue guide or completed cross-sells.

in_line: Adjusted EPS was $1.04, matching the preview’s $1.04 consensus.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.79, well above the preview’s $0.66 consensus estimate—about a 20% beat, despite the preview describing that estimate as the key bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased to $0.79.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $0.66.”

surprises.description: Hardware Solutions adjusted EBITDA recovered to $27.1 million, exceeding the preview’s $20 million catalyst threshold and its bull-case level of $22 million or more. That recovery came even as segment sales fell, so the earnings rebound was stronger than the preview’s key operating test implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hardware Solutions net sales fell to $220.9 million” while “adjusted EBITDA rose to $27.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hardware Solutions adj. EBITDA ≥ $20M”; the preview also said “Below ~$15M and the guide breaks.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $72.7 million, just above the preview’s $70–72 million range; the resulting margin was about 14.5%, slightly above the preview’s 14.2–14.45% range. This was a modest beat against a preview that framed margin recovery as the pass/fail test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew modestly to $72.7 million from $70.3 million.” Net sales were $501.8 million, implying an adjusted EBITDA margin of about 14.5%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$70–72M (guide)” and “Adj. EBITDA margin 14.2–14.45% (guide).”

surprises.description: Revenue reached $501.8 million, modestly above the preview’s roughly $495–500 million expectation. The beat was small, with year-over-year growth of 1.3% versus the preview’s flat-to-1% guide framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 consolidated net sales rose 1.3% year-over-year to $501.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~$495–500M (guide-anchored)” and management had guided Q3 revenue “flat to +1% YoY.”

surprises.description: The preview expected price increases to be the recovery driver, but reported tariff reimbursements created a notable offset: roughly 2% of consolidated sales and about $9 million of Hardware Solutions revenue. This unanticipated drag helps explain why the Hardware segment’s sales fell despite pricing gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: Sales growth was driven by “roughly 3% pricing gains offset by a ~2% negative tariff reimbursement impact”; Hardware had “a ~4% tariff reimbursement headwind (about $9 million in revenue).”

surprises.description: Extruded Solutions revenue grew, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $35.6 million from $37.1 million. That was weaker than the preview’s picture of the segment as stable, especially since it said completed Monterrey remediation should be a tailwind; inflation instead weighed on profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Extruded Solutions revenue grew 2.8% to $179.3 million” but “adjusted EBITDA declined to $35.6 million from $37.1 million due to inflationary pressures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Extruded Solutions “the most stable segment” and said Monterrey remediation “should now be a tailwind.”

surprises.description: Custom Solutions grew 8.5%, with both volume and pricing contributing, and the results included roughly $10 million per year of new Wood Solutions business that the preview had not identified. The segment’s growth outpaced its prior-quarter 6.6% increase noted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Custom Solutions was the fastest-growing segment with revenue up 8.5% to $111 million on ~3% volume and ~5.5% pricing gains, boosted by roughly $10 million/year of new Wood Solutions business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Custom Solutions as “the bright spot in Q2 (+6.6%: volume +1%, price +4.5%).”

surprises.description: Net debt-to-EBITDA leverage fell to 2.8 times, better than the preview’s watchpoint of no more than 3.1 times. The company also repurchased $1.7 million of stock while paying down debt, although the preview had said management prioritized debt paydown over buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company paid down $42.25 million of debt and repurchased $1.7 million of stock in the quarter, lowering net-debt-to-EBITDA leverage to 2.8 times.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net debt/LTM adj. EBITDA ≤ 3.1x with positive FCF”; the preview also said management had “explicitly prioritized debt paydown over buybacks.”

surprises.description: The preview identified reinstating FY2026 guidance as the buy-side’s top ask, but the reported outlook was Q4-only; no full-year guidance reinstatement is reported. The company did provide Q4 revenue and margin targets, but that did not restore the annual outlook the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: The reported guidance is for “Q4 2026”: revenue growth of 2%–3% and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 50–75 basis points; no FY2026 guidance is given in the reported facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance reinstated — the buy-side’s #1 ask”; the preview also noted guidance had been withdrawn at Q2.

surprises.description: Management characterized weak housing demand as deferred rather than destroyed, pointing to higher permits and homes authorized but not started despite sharply lower single-family starts. That was a more constructive demand interpretation than the preview’s emphasis on volume attrition risk, though the housing indicators themselves were mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said weak housing demand was “deferred rather than destroyed,” citing single-family starts down about 16% year over year, total permits up 3%, and homes authorized-but-not-started up about 10%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “price realization vs. volume attrition” and asked whether price increases would stick “without share loss.”

in_line: Free cash flow was positive and increased 3.5% year over year, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Q3 is seasonally the strongest free-cash-flow quarter.
The Q4 outlook pointed to full-quarter price realization as a support for revenue growth and margin expansion, consistent with the preview’s view that the full pricing benefit would land in Q4.

surprises.description: FY2026 adjusted EPS was $2.65, above both the $0.61–$0.62 Q4 consensus (with Q4 EPS at $0.69) and the $2.40–$2.60 full-year guidance range. The earnings result cleared the preview’s already-high Q4 consensus bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year adjusted EPS was $2.65 (Q4 at $0.69), coming in above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $0.61–$0.62” consensus; full-year guidance of “$2.40–2.60.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $172 million exceeded the roughly $166 million consensus midpoint and landed near the top of the implied Q4 guidance range. Full-year adjusted EBITDA of $701 million also finished near the top of the $685–$705 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $172 million,” and full-year adjusted EBITDA “finished near the top of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$166M (derived)” for Q4; the implied Q4 range was “$156–176M” and FY26 guidance was “$685–705M.”

surprises.description: FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance has a $3.25 midpoint, above the preview’s derived street expectation of about $3.05–$3.10. The $3.00–$3.50 range therefore points to stronger earnings growth than the preview’s central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for… adjusted EPS of $3.00-$3.50 (23% growth at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “a street FY27 EPS around $3.05–3.10” and a base case of “$2.95–3.15.”

surprises.description: FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance has a $755 million midpoint, below the preview’s expected $760–$780 million street range, although the company’s high end reaches $780 million. The guide is therefore somewhat softer than the expectation at its midpoint, rather than a clear beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for… adjusted EBITDA of $730-$780 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put the likely street model at “$760–780M” and its base case at “$750–770M.”

surprises.description: The FY2027 free-cash-flow range of $275–$325 million has a $300 million midpoint, below the preview’s roughly $350 million base expectation. The range’s high end is also below that base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 plans include… free cash flow of $275-$325 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “FCF ~$350M”; its bull case was “FCF ≥$375M.”

surprises.description: The company says its FY2027 EBITDA midpoint is $25 million above its Investor Day target and that it expects to reach its FY2028 margin target a year early. The preview focused on the street bar and did not anticipate this acceleration against the company’s longer-term targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA midpoint is $25 million above the Investor Day target, and the company expects to hit its fiscal 2028 margin target one year early.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call says the FY2027 midpoint is “$25 million above the Investor Day target” and the FY2028 target will be reached “one year early.”

surprises.description: The Board authorized a new $200 million share-repurchase program. The preview specifically raised the possibility of an upsized FY2027 buyback as a potential positive, though the call facts do not state how the new authorization compares in size with the expiring one.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized a new $200 million share repurchase program replacing an expiring one.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With leverage through 2.5x, does management upsize the buyback in FY27?”

in_line: Q4 sales were reported at over $7.6 billion, consistent with the preview’s $7.59–$7.79 billion guidance-implied range and its $7.60–$7.71 billion consensus range.
FY2026 sales of approximately $31.2 billion were within the preview’s cited $31.1–$31.3 billion guidance range.
FY2026 free cash flow of $323 million was close to the preview’s approximately $330 million expectation.
Net leverage of 2.2x was in line with the preview’s expected Q4 exit near 2.2–2.3x.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $227 million, above the preview’s $225.5 million estimate and roughly $220.4 million live consensus. The beat was solid but slightly below the preview’s $228–231 million bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $227 million” and exceeded guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Est.: $225.5M”; Street consensus “~$220.4M.”

surprises.description: Braze raised FY27 revenue guidance to $910–913 million, above the preview’s roughly $905 million estimate and its $903–907 million base scenario. The new range also clears the preview’s $910 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year revenue guidance to $910-913 million (~23% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Raise to ~$905M”; the base scenario anticipated “FY27 to $903–907M,” while the bull case called for “≥$910M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating income was $22 million, above the preview’s $21 million estimate and well above the company’s prior $17–18 million Q2 guide. This produced a 9.7% margin, and management said the company remains on track for at least 400 basis points of full-year margin gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income surged to $22 million (9.7% margin)” and the company is “on track for at least 400 bps of full-year margin gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP Op. Income” estimate: “$21M (9.3% mgn)”; company guide was “$17.0M – $18.0M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP gross margin reached 68.6%, above the preview’s 67.4% pass mark and its base-case expectation of roughly 67.4%. It remained below the year-ago 69.3%, but the quarter showed a better margin result than the preview’s stabilization threshold implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin declined slightly to 68.6% from 69.3% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “≥67.4% is the pass mark”; the base scenario expected “GM flat ~67.4%.”

surprises.description: Current RPO grew 24% to $691 million, above the preview’s 20–22% base-case range and the roughly $670 million level it said was required. It did decelerate, however, and management attributed the timing partly to seasonal renewals and lapping OfferFit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Current RPO growth decelerated to 24% year-over-year ($691 million)” partly due to “seasonal renewal timing and lapping the OfferFit acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “cRPO ~20–22%”; it said “>20% YoY (~$670M+) is required.”

surprises.description: Large-customer retention rose to 112%, one percentage point above the preview’s 111% confirmation level. Overall retention remained at 110%, as the preview’s 110–111% range anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dollar-based net retention for large customers ($500K+ annually) rose 100 basis points to 112%, while overall trailing 12-month DBNR held flat at 110%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “111% would confirm” for the $500K+ cohort and expected all-customer DBNR of “110–111%.”

surprises.description: Excluding Decisioning Studio, year-over-year revenue growth was 24%, slightly above the preview’s roughly 23% estimate for that underlying growth line. Decisioning Studio revenue itself was essentially as previewed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BrazeAI Decisioning Studio contributed $6.6 million of revenue, implying an organic (ex-Decisioning Studio) year-over-year growth rate of 24%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a $225–226 million print implied “~23%” ex-acquisition growth and estimated Decisioning Studio at “~$6.6–6.8M.”

surprises.description: Paid AI-tool adoption among large customers rose sharply, with roughly one-third of the cohort paying for the tools and adoption up about 900 basis points from Q1. The preview discussed AI as a key issue and watched for deployment evidence, but did not anticipate or quantify this adoption result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paid adoption of Braze's AI tools reached roughly one-third of the large customer cohort, up about 900 basis points from Q1.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a three-year strategic collaboration with AWS covering co-sell incentives and marketplace procurement, a new commercial initiative not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed a 3-year strategic collaboration agreement with AWS establishing co-sell incentives and marketplace procurement.”

surprises.description: Q3 operating income guidance of $16–17 million implies a roughly 7% margin, below Q2’s 9.7% margin, with Forge conference costs and sales hiring cited as drags. The preview did not forecast this near-term operating-margin step-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue guidance of $229-230 million implies deceleration to ~20% year-over-year growth, with Q3 operating income guided to $16-17 million (~7% margin) due to Forge conference costs and new sales hiring.”

in_line: Decisioning Studio revenue of $6.6 million was within the preview’s estimated $6.6–6.8 million range.
Overall DBNR of 110% was within the preview’s expected 110–111% range.

The $50 million accelerated share repurchase matched the preview’s expectation that about $50 million of the $100 million authorization had been executed; the additional $50 million remained authorized.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $292.8 million, about 2.4% above the $285.96 million consensus and above the preview’s $290–292 million base case. It was below the preview’s $294 million-plus bull case, but clearly stronger than the central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 total revenue grew 21% year-over-year to $292.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $285.96M”; the preview’s base scenario was “$290–292M” and bull scenario “~$294M+.”

surprises.description: The FY27 revenue outlook rose only to $1.139–$1.144 billion, short of the preview’s expected base-case raise to roughly $1.145–$1.150 billion and well below its “through the beat” threshold of $1.155 billion. The range is above the prior company guide, but the raise was smaller than the preview framed as important.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance is $1.139 billion to $1.144 billion in revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” expected FY27 raised “to ~$1.145–1.150B”; “through the beat” was defined as “≥$1.155B.”

surprises.description: Operating performance and the incremental-margin outlook were stronger than the preview’s margin benchmark: the reported operating margin was 15.2% against the preview’s roughly 13.4% guided margin, and management now calls 25% incremental margins a floor while guiding to 33% for FY27.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating income was $44.4 million for a 15.2% operating margin”; management is “now viewing 25% incremental margins as a floor rather than a target, and guiding to 33% incremental margins for FY27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “13.4% margin at midpoint” and said incremental margins “should run above the original 25% target.”

surprises.description: GTV growth slowed to 17%, below the preview’s 23% reference and beneath its 20% threshold for a potential end-demand warning. Management attributed the slowdown mainly to softer lead volume growth, notably in HVAC, in May and June, though it said activity stabilized in July.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GTV reached $26.8 billion, up 17% year-over-year, which was about 200 basis points below recent quarters,” driven by “softer lead volume growth (notably in HVAC) during May and June before stabilizing in July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “+23% in Q1” and said “A sub-20% GTV print would be the first genuine macro crack.”

surprises.description: The FY27 operating-income outlook increased substantially from the prior company range, even though the preview did not flag an annual operating-income raise as a central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance is … $152 million to $154 million in operating income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior FY27 company guidance of “$142–147M” for non-GAAP operating income.

surprises.description: Free cash flow was not merely positive as the preview expected for Q2; it reached a record $50.5 million, up 47% year over year. The preview gave no numerical Q2 benchmark, so the size of the beat against expectations cannot be quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow hit a record $50.5 million, up 47% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 should swing positive.”

surprises.description: The call described stronger Max rollout progress than the preview’s location-count checkpoint alone captured: the company said it had exceeded its Q2 goal and now targets more than 700 enrolled locations by fiscal year-end. The call did not give a Q2 location count, so it is not possible to verify the preview’s expected second doubling directly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Max locations more than doubled to just over 100 in fiscal Q1” and the company is “now targeting over 700 enrolled Max locations by fiscal year-end after exceeding its Q2 goal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management was committed to “doubling Max locations again in Q2.”

surprises.description: Management reprioritized investment away from planned expansion into new commercial trades and broader residential exteriors, concentrating instead on Max and its AI software factory. The shift also creates an unanticipated near-term revenue headwind of about $4–5 million for the rest of the fiscal year.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is “delaying planned expansion into new commercial trades and broader residential exteriors to concentrate resources on Max and its internal ‘software factory’ AI initiative”; this is expected to create “a $2 million to $3 million subscription revenue headwind and roughly $2 million lower professional services revenue” over the remainder of the year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on Max adoption and AI investment costs, but did not anticipate delaying those trade expansions or a roughly $4–5 million near-term revenue headwind.

surprises.description: The call supplied more concrete Max monetization economics than the preview’s focus on adoption and proof of pricing uplift: at full contract ramp, Max roughly doubles subscription revenue per customer versus prior spend. However, Max is not billed in the first contract quarter, tempering the near-term revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “At full contract ramp, Max roughly doubles a customer's subscription revenue versus prior spend, driving an average platform earn rate just north of 2%, though Max is not billed for the first quarter of a contract.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “pricing uplift showing in platform revenue, not just location counts.”

surprises.description: Virtual-agent activity accelerated sharply, with both revenue and call volume more than doubling sequentially; the preview did not identify this product’s adoption as a specific expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Virtual agent revenue and call volume each more than doubled sequentially in Q2,” with adoption split between first-time buyers and customers replacing competing solutions.

in_line: Net dollar retention remained above 110%, matching the preview’s key durability checkpoint.
Management’s incremental-margin outlook remained above the original 25% target, consistent with the preview’s expectation that incremental margins should run above that target.

surprises.description: Chewy raised its full-year net sales range to $13.46–$13.57 billion from $13.40–$13.55 billion, rather than merely reaffirming the prior outlook. The increase is modest, but it goes against the preview’s concern that softer demand could prompt a second consecutive guidance cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised total net sales guidance to $13.46-$13.57 billion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the key question was “FY2026 net sales guidance — reaffirm vs. cut #2” and described the base case as “FY guide reaffirmed, low end emphasized.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin reached 6.8%, above the 6.3%–6.4% guide. However, roughly $15 million of timing and discrete items accounted for essentially all of the outperformance, tempering the quality of the beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $227 million (6.8% margin), beating guidance of 6.3%-6.4%, but roughly $15 million of timing and discrete items “accounted for essentially all the outperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of “6.3–6.4%.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales were slightly above the $3.32 billion consensus and reached the top end of the company’s prior range. This was a modest beat rather than the below-guide result feared in the preview’s bear case.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 total net sales reached $3.33 billion, “at the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus net sales of “$3.32B” and company guidance of “$3.30–3.33B.”

surprises.description: Chewy added 208,000 net customers sequentially, ahead of the preview’s roughly 162,000-add consensus estimate and above the low end of the anticipated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Chewy ended the quarter with 21.7 million active customers and “adding 208,000 sequential net additions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said consensus implied “~162K net adds” and cited a “low end of 150–250K” framing.

surprises.description: Autoship sales grew 9.3%, below the roughly 10% growth level the preview identified as the threshold to watch. Its 84.6% share of sales remained above the preview’s 84% penetration benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: Autoship customer sales grew 9.3% year-over-year to $2.8 billion and represented 84.6% of total net sales.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “Autoship growth ≥10% and penetration ≥84%” and that deceleration below about 10% would be the first real crack in the recurring-revenue thesis.

surprises.description: NSPAC was $602, slightly below the preview’s $603.42 consensus. The reported growth rate was 1.9%, although it was 3.8% after adjusting for the prior year’s extra week.
surprises.fact_evidence: NSPAC reached $602, “up 1.9% reported and 3.8% on a normalized basis adjusting for the prior year's extra week.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed NSPAC consensus of “$603.42” and flagged “NSPAC ≥ $603” as a catalyst to watch.

in_line: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.36, matching both consensus and the company’s Q2 guide of $0.36.
The full-year adjusted EBITDA margin range of 6.7%–6.8% remained within the previously expected 6.6%–6.8% range, though its low end was raised.

The AI savings timeline broadly matched the preview: low tens of millions in fiscal 2026 and about $50 million annualized in fiscal 2027. Management clarified that the savings would partly offset wage inflation rather than fully flow to the bottom line.

surprises.description: J.Jill expected Q2 sales to decline 1%–3% and comparable sales to decline 2%–4%, but both sales and comps increased 0.5% year over year, exceeding company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total company sales rose 0.5% year-over-year to $154.8 million with comparable sales also up 0.5%, exceeding company guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guide: net sales “-1% to -3%” and comparable sales “-2% to -4%.”

surprises.description: The full-year outlook was raised well beyond the prior $70–75 million adjusted EBITDA range: J.Jill now expects $75–80 million, with sales flat to up 2% and comps down 1% to up 1%. The preview had described a flat-to-down 2% sales outlook and highlighted the difficulty of reaching the prior EBITDA range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance to adjusted EBITDA of $75-80 million, sales flat to up 2%, comps down 1% to up 1%, and gross margin up 100-150 basis points versus prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identifies the full-year adjusted EBITDA guide as “$70–75M” and says the full-year sales guide was “flat-to-down-2%.”

surprises.description: A $13.3 million net tariff refund arrived in the quarter, far exceeding the preview’s description of only a small early-Q2 refund and its assumption of no refund benefit in guidance. The refund materially boosted reported adjusted EBITDA and gross margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received $13.3 million in net tariff refunds in the quarter”; reported adjusted EBITDA was “$32.8 million” and reported gross margin was “76.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says J.Jill had received “a small portion” of its IEEPA refund claim early in Q2 but “assumed zero refund benefit in guidance.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.24, far above the preview’s $0.57 consensus estimate, despite only about $0.01 of help from share repurchases. The quarter’s tariff refunds also boosted reported earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS jumped to $1.24 from $0.81 a year earlier, aided by roughly $0.01 from share repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus: “$0.57 (4 analysts).”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance calls for sales growth and positive comps, rather than just the gradual sequential improvement the preview described as the base case. J.Jill also expects flat Q3 gross margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for sales up 3-5%, comps up 1-3%, flat gross margins, and adjusted EBITDA of $20-22 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “gradual sequential improvement through Q3, accelerating into Q4.”

surprises.description: Even excluding tariff refunds, gross margin was roughly flat at 68.3%, better than the preview’s expectation of about a 100-basis-point decline. The much larger reported expansion reflects the refund benefit rather than the underlying margin result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported gross margin expanded about 840 basis points to 76.8%, but excluding tariff refunds gross margin was roughly flat at 68.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Q2 company guide in the preview was for gross margin of “~-100 bps.”

surprises.description: J.Jill ended the quarter with inventory down about 5% year over year, improving on the preview’s latest reported inventory position of down 3.5% excluding capitalized tariff costs and its concern about back-half markdown risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory ended the quarter down about 5% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 inventory “-3.5% ex-$5.5M of capitalized tariff cost” and warned that inventory turning positive against negative comps could mean “promotional Q3/Q4 margin.”

surprises.description: The company expects approximately $40 million of full-year free cash flow, double the $20 million target cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects full-year free cash flow of approximately $40 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cites a “$20M FY target” for free cash flow.

surprises.description: The $13.3 million refund did not simply flow through to earnings: management chose to put most of it into marketing and technology initiatives. That allocation reduces the near-term benefit to the bottom line while increasing investment in those programs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company intentionally chose to invest most of it into marketing and technology initiatives rather than dropping it to the bottom line.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the refund as “pure upside to the print and to FY EBITDA” and identified it as an unguided upside lever.

surprises.description: The planned net store-opening range was cut further, to 1–3 from the 1–5 range described in the preview, because landlord delivery delays pushed two openings into early 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net new store openings were trimmed to 1-3 due to landlord delivery delays pushing two openings into early 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s secondary-items section says net new stores had been “cut to 1–5 from ~5.”

surprises.description: Underlying adjusted EBITDA was only $20.1 million after excluding tariff refunds and strategic investments, close to the preview’s $19–20 million expectation and well below the headline $32.8 million reported figure. Thus, most of the apparent EBITDA outperformance came from the refund rather than a large underlying beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Underlying adjusted EBITDA (excluding tariff refunds and strategic investments) was $20.1 million, while reported adjusted EBITDA reached $32.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected adjusted EBITDA of “$18–20M” under company guidance and approximately “$19–20M” from consensus.

surprises.description: Management described improving customer quality and reactivation: new-to-brand customers are younger, retain at higher rates, and spend more, while lapsed-customer reactivation is building. Those favorable retention and spending trends were not part of the preview’s stated expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New-to-brand customers are trending younger, retaining at higher rates, and spending more via higher average order value and more trips, while lapsed-customer reactivation is building.”

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted EBITDA was $94.6 million, above the preview’s $85–90 million full-year guidance range. The 9.6% margin also put InnovAge ahead of schedule for its long-term 10%+ margin target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose approximately 175% to $94.6 million”; margin improved to “9.6%” and management said it is “ahead of schedule” to hit its “10%+ long-term margin target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance was “$85–90M” and described the FY26 margin as guided to “~9%.”

surprises.description: FY26 revenue reached $989.7 million, above both the $950–975 million company guidance range cited in the preview and the preview’s roughly $944.5 million consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 total revenue grew 15.9% to $989.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave FY26 revenue guidance of “$950M – $975M” and full-year consensus of “~$944.5M.”

surprises.description: Ending census was approximately 8,230, above the preview’s reaffirmed FY26 range of 7,900–8,100. That is a clear upside to the preview’s concern that the guide midpoint was below the reported Q3 census.
surprises.fact_evidence: FY26 census increased “6.3% to approximately 8,230 participants.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited an FY26 ending-census guide of “7,900 – 8,100” and said its midpoint of 8,000 was “below the reported Q3 level.”

surprises.description: FY27 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $105–115 million is above the preview’s base-case range of $95–103 million and clears the $100 million-plus level the preview said the stock needed. It reaches the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: FY27 adjusted EBITDA guidance is “$105–$115 million,” implying “roughly 10.3% margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the stock needed a FY27 EBITDA guide with “a $100M+ handle”; its base case was “$95–103M” and bull case “$105–115M.”

surprises.description: FY27 revenue guidance of $1.05–1.085 billion is above the preview’s base-case range at the midpoint and reaches into its bull-case range, rather than merely delivering the base case’s modest growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: FY27 total revenue guidance is “$1.05–$1.085 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base-case FY27 revenue was “$1.02–1.05B,” while its bull case was “$1.06B+.”

surprises.description: InnovAge reported a FY26 net loss of $0.7 million, or $0.02 per share, rather than the positive FY26 EPS in the preview’s consensus range. Management attributed the near-breakeven result to $36.8 million of one-time legal and settlement accruals, so the litigation clean-up was not as clean as the preview hoped.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 net loss narrowed to just $0.7 million ($0.02 per share)” and the result was “driven by $36.8 million in one-time legal and settlement accruals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY26 EPS consensus of “$0.23 – $0.253” and said, “Confirm Q4 G&A reverts to a ~$38–42M run-rate. If there's a second charge, the ‘profitability’ narrative gets murky again.”

surprises.description: De novo losses came in below the preview’s FY26 expectation, and the FY27 outlook points to a much faster reduction than the preview quantified: only $0.4–0.8 million of projected losses as more centers leave de novo status.
surprises.fact_evidence: FY26 de novo losses were “$10.6 million” versus $15.3 million in FY25 and are projected to fall to “$0.4–$0.8 million in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 de novo losses were guided to “$11.5–13.5M” and identified de novo economics as a key issue to watch.

surprises.description: The V28 transition is not only a rate headwind: management said InnovAge benefits from favorable dementia coding under V28 because dementia is prevalent among its participants. The preview discussed V28 as part of the expected rate pressure but did not flag this offset.
surprises.fact_evidence: InnovAge “benefits from favorable dementia coding under V28 given high dementia prevalence among participants.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Medicare PACE rates were expected at “just 1.5–2% (V28 transition).”

surprises.description: California and Colorado, together representing about 70% of census, still had not finalized PACE Medicaid rates. The preview anticipated state budget pressure and mentioned Colorado cuts, but did not highlight that rates for this much of the participant base remained unresolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “California and Colorado, which together represent approximately 70% of census, have not yet finalized their PACE Medicaid rates,” with both states facing fiscal pressures.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said state Medicaid budgets were tightening and noted that “Colorado has already announced Medicaid cuts.”

in_line: Management’s FY27 rate outlook was broadly in line with the preview’s warning of a more tempered rate environment: it guided to a 1.5%–2.0% net Medicare rate increase after V28 adjustments and low-single-digit Medicaid increases.

surprises.description: Diluted EPS of $7.37 was well above the preview’s $6.59–$6.81 consensus range. EBITDA of $485 million also exceeded the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $470–$480 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS reached $7.37, up 28% year-over-year,” and “EBITDA increased 17% to $485 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $6.59 – $6.81”; “Implied EBITDA: ~$470–480M.”

surprises.description: Fuel margin came in at 47.8 cents per gallon, above the roughly 44.8–46.0 cents implied by the preview’s consensus-based analysis. That was a meaningful upside to a key earnings assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fuel margin was strong at $0.478 per gallon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus is embedding ~45–46 cents per gallon.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $5.68 billion was slightly above the preview’s $5.56–$5.65 billion consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 24.3% to $5.68 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $5.56B – $5.65B.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses rose 8%, above the preview’s 5–7% full-year guide and its stated threshold for a negative surprise. Management also said Q2 expense growth should be similar to Q1, suggesting the elevated pace would persist near term.
